atoms.title: Level funded adoption among small firms
atoms.q: How common are level funded plans among small firms?
atoms.text: In 2025, 37% of small firms, defined as those with 3-199 employees, reported having a level funded plan, compared to just 7% in 2019, according to KFF Employer Health Benefits Surveys. UnitedHealthcare says rising health care costs and economic uncertainty are driving employers to seek more cost-effective plan designs, and experts find confusion about how level funded plans work.
qs: What percent of small businesses have level funded plans?
Why are level funded plans growing in popularity?

atoms.title: 19% average upfront savings after switching
atoms.q: How much do small businesses save by switching to UnitedHealthcare Level Funded?
atoms.text: Businesses with 2-50 employees that switched from a traditional, ACA-compliant fully insured plan to a UnitedHealthcare Level Funded plan saw an upfront savings of 19% on average. UnitedHealthcare bases this on fully insured groups nationwide migrated to Level Funded between Jan. 1, 2025 and Dec. 31, 2025, and notes savings are not guaranteed.
qs: How much can a small business save moving from fully insured to level funded?
Are level funded savings guaranteed?

atoms.title: Level funded plans are self-funded with 3 differences
atoms.q: What is a level funded plan?
atoms.text: At their core, level funded plans are generally self-funded plans with three key differences, though some components vary by carrier: stop loss insurance to help mitigate claims risk, an opportunity for a surplus refund, and a third-party claims administration agreement. They can also include monthly reports on health care usage and wellness programs that may increase participant engagement and reduce costs.
qs: What makes a level funded plan different from self-funded?
What are the key features of level funded plans?

atoms.title: Level funded vs self-funded vs fully insured risk
atoms.q: How do level funded plans balance predictability and risk?
atoms.text: Like a fully insured plan, level funding gives employers a fixed monthly amount covering maximum claims liability, administrative fees and stop loss insurance. Unlike traditional self-funded plans, which expose employers to the full fluctuation of claims costs, Level Funded plans include stop loss protection that limits claims liability, while employers fund medical and pharmacy claims and gain flexibility over plan design.
qs: Is a level funded plan riskier than fully insured?
How is level funded different from traditional self-funded?

atoms.title: Surplus share: fully insured vs level funded
atoms.q: Who keeps savings when claims are lower than expected?
atoms.text: In a fully insured plan, the insurer pays claims if they are higher than expected and keeps the difference if they are lower. A plan sponsor with a Level Funded plan is insured against higher-than-expected claims, and the plan may receive a surplus share if claims are lower than expected, where allowed by law. That gives plan sponsors an extra incentive to keep their workforce healthy.
qs: Does the employer or insurer keep savings in level funded plans?
What is a surplus share?

atoms.title: Monthly data reports guide cost decisions
atoms.q: What data insights come with a Level Funded plan?
atoms.text: Plan sponsors with level funding can receive detailed monthly data reports on how participants use health services, which is not the case with most fully insured plans. The data can help sponsors spot utilization trends and alert participants that generics can often replace brand-name drugs, urgent care may be less costly than the ER for certain conditions, and virtual visits with a primary care provider can save time and money.
qs: Do level funded plans give employers claims data?
How can utilization reports lower plan costs?

atoms.title: Member experience in Level Funded plans
atoms.q: What member benefits are included in UnitedHealthcare Level Funded plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Level Funded plans include wellness programs and 24/7 virtual care for conditions including general medical care and behavioral health counseling. Participants may be invited to join rewards programs, and plans offer $0 copays for dependent kids' appointments and critical medications like insulin. Participants can also buy additional offerings through UHC Store, available in the UnitedHealthcare app and on myuhc.com.
qs: Do level funded plans include $0 copays for insulin?
What is the UHC Store?

atoms.title: Surest available as a Level Funded option
atoms.q: Is the Surest plan available as Level Funded?
atoms.text: Yes. The Surest health plan is also available as a Level Funded option, bringing cost transparency to a new subset of consumers. With Surest, plan participants can make decisions that may affect plan sponsor costs, since the plan features an easy-to-use app with clear upfront copays rather than estimates.
qs: Can I get Surest with level funding?
How does Surest show costs upfront?

atoms.title: Recent Level Funded enhancements for 51+ groups
atoms.q: What enhancements has UnitedHealthcare made to Level Funded for larger groups?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare has expanded its Level Funded offering with customizable benefit and pricing options for employers with 51 or more employees, with adjustable surplus share percentages now available. Recent enhancements include optional benefit buy-ups for eligible groups, such as infertility coverage, weight loss surgery options and a premium rewards program.
qs: Can larger employers customize level funded plans?
What optional buy-ups are available with Level Funded?

atoms.title: Behavioral health is at an inflection point
atoms.q: Why is behavioral health at an inflection point for employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says behavioral health is at an inflection point: demand is rising, digital tools are proliferating, and expectations from patients and employers are shifting fast. Employers want solutions that make the path to care simpler, help employees access support earlier and drive more meaningful results. The article describes 7 trends defining behavioral health in 2025.
qs: What are the biggest behavioral health trends for employers in 2025?
Why is behavioral health demand rising?

atoms.title: More people seek behavioral health care earlier
atoms.q: How many Americans are expected to use behavioral health services?
atoms.text: Declining stigma is leading to a sustained rise in first-time users of behavioral health benefits, particularly among young people and families. An estimated 25% of Americans will access behavioral health services by 2026, while more than a third of Americans live in areas with mental health professional shortages and 6,200+ professionals are needed. About 50% of members seeking support could be good candidates for virtual behavioral coaching as an alternative to therapy.
qs: What percent of Americans will use behavioral health services?
Can virtual coaching replace therapy for some people?

atoms.title: Whole-person care is becoming the norm
atoms.q: How is behavioral health care becoming more integrated with physical health?
atoms.text: The industry is moving away from siloed treatment models toward approaches that connect behavioral and physical health, driven by awareness of how mental health affects chronic conditions, medication adherence and overall well-being. Models integrating behavioral support with primary care and chronic condition management are becoming the new standard, and 3 in 4 surveyed employees agreed their employer has a responsibility to make sure they are physically, mentally and emotionally well.
qs: Why are behavioral and physical health being integrated?
Do employees expect employers to support mental well-being?

atoms.title: AI is reshaping access to behavioral health care
atoms.q: How is AI changing behavioral health care?
atoms.text: Artificial intelligence is changing how people find, begin and stay engaged in behavioral health care, through tools such as predictive analytics, automated triage and natural language processing. UnitedHealthcare says AI is not replacing clinicians but supporting them; used responsibly with human oversight, it can surface needs earlier, streamline care pathways and ease administrative burden such as scheduling.
qs: Will AI replace therapists?
How is AI used to help people find behavioral health care?

atoms.title: Youth mental health is at a tipping point
atoms.q: What is driving the youth mental health crisis?
atoms.text: The youth mental health crisis continues to deepen, driven by digital pressures, academic stress and post-pandemic disruptions. Long wait times for therapy and a shortage of pediatric specialists are prompting a shift toward earlier, more scalable support for families. Dr. Donald Tavakoli, national medical director of behavioral health for UnitedHealthcare, says solutions must meet young people where they are, whether through digital resources, therapists, schools or community organizations.
qs: Why is youth mental health getting worse?
What support exists for young people with mental health challenges?

atoms.title: Behavioral health is moving closer to home
atoms.q: How much care is moving to home settings, and what is the top telehealth category?
atoms.text: The shift from facility-based to home-based care is accelerating. Up to $265B in services were expected to move to home settings by 2025, and behavioral health is leading that move. From January to June 2024, mental health conditions ranked as the number one telehealth diagnostic category nationwide, which can remove logistical barriers and improve engagement for employees.
qs: What is the most common telehealth diagnosis?
How much care is moving to the home?

atoms.title: Employers want ROI from behavioral health
atoms.q: What return do employers expect from behavioral health benefits?
atoms.text: Employers are looking beyond access and want to know their behavioral health offerings are working, which means clear navigation, measurable outcomes and solutions that demonstrate value. As usage rises, so does the need for programs that deliver return on investment, such as better retention, reduced absenteeism and improved employee satisfaction.
qs: How do employers measure ROI on mental health benefits?
What outcomes should behavioral health programs deliver?

atoms.title: Investment surge in behavioral health
atoms.q: How much investment is flowing into behavioral health?
atoms.text: Private equity investments accounted for 60% of all behavioral health deals in recent years, and 90% in autism care alone. $1.4B was invested in the digital behavioral health space in 2024 alone. UnitedHealthcare says this creates a dynamic but potentially confusing landscape and underscores the importance of choosing a carrier or vendors with a track record of delivering results, not just rapid growth.
qs: How much private equity is in behavioral health?
How should employers choose a behavioral health vendor?

atoms.title: Behavioral health as a core benefit
atoms.q: Is behavioral health still considered a fringe benefit?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says behavioral health is no longer a fringe benefit. It describes it as a core part of whole-person health and workforce well-being, business continuity and employee retention. The 2025 trends create new challenges and opportunities for employers to reimagine how they support mental health, starting with clarity, access and care that truly works.
qs: Why should employers treat mental health as a core benefit?
What is the future of workplace behavioral health?

atoms.title: What is artificial intelligence?
atoms.q: What is artificial intelligence (AI)?
atoms.text: AI performs tasks that typically require human intelligence, including learning, reasoning and making decisions based on data and algorithms. Generative AI is a type of AI that creates new data or content, such as images, music or text, that did not previously exist. Unlike other AI designed to recognize patterns and make predictions, generative AI can create new and original content.
qs: What does AI mean?
What is generative AI?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI for coverage decisions?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to make coverage decisions?
atoms.text: No. UnitedHealthcare says coverage decisions are made based on standard coverage criteria, medical necessity guidelines and the terms of member plans. AI is used to help inform providers, families and other caregivers about what sort of assistance and care a patient may need, whether in a health care facility or at home.
qs: Does AI decide what my insurance covers?
How does UnitedHealthcare make coverage decisions?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI for prior authorization?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to make prior authorization decisions?
atoms.text: No. UnitedHealthcare uses AI to gather clinical data and support clinical and administrative professionals throughout the decision-making process, but it does not employ AI to issue any adverse clinical determinations.
qs: Does AI deny prior authorization requests?
Does UnitedHealthcare use AI for prior auth?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI for clinical decisions?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to make clinical decisions?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare has developed AI solutions, powered by its own data sets, that help surface insights and information based on the latest medical knowledge, patient history and historical outcomes data. According to UnitedHealthcare, AI never replaces the health care provider's decision and only enables it.
qs: Does AI make medical decisions for my doctor?
How does AI support clinicians at UnitedHealthcare?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to recommend treatment?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to recommend courses of treatment?
atoms.text: Algorithms surface relevant insights and recommend potential treatment options to providers based on evidence-based clinical guidelines and outcomes data. However, UnitedHealthcare says all treatment decisions are made by clinicians, with AI used as a tool to assist and inform them.
qs: Does AI recommend my treatment?
Who makes treatment decisions at UnitedHealthcare?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI for reimbursement rates?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to determine hospital or provider reimbursement rates?
atoms.text: No. UnitedHealthcare states that the process it uses to determine the pricing of its reimbursement rates does not use AI.
qs: Does AI set provider payment rates?
How does UnitedHealthcare set reimbursement rates?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to determine length of coverage?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to determine length of coverage?
atoms.text: No. UnitedHealthcare uses AI as a guide to help inform providers, families and other caregivers about what types of interventions or care a patient may need, whether in a health care facility or at home.
qs: Does AI decide how long my coverage lasts?
Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to limit care duration?

atoms.title: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to reject claims?
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to reject medical claims?
atoms.text: No. UnitedHealthcare states that it does not use, and has never used, AI to make adverse decisions related to claims.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare use AI to deny claims?
Can AI reject my medical claim?

atoms.title: AI supports human care, not replaces it
atoms.q: Is UnitedHealthcare using AI to replace human care?
atoms.text: UnitedHealth Group says AI isn't replacing human care but helping make health care more connected, personalized and timely. It is applying AI across its UnitedHealthcare and Optum businesses to simplify how people find care and navigate the health system, with the result being more timely coordination and simpler experiences.
qs: Does AI replace human care at UnitedHealthcare?
How does UnitedHealth Group use AI to coordinate care?

atoms.title: Safeguards on UnitedHealthcare AI models
atoms.q: What limits does UnitedHealthcare place on its AI?
atoms.text: UnitedHealth Group, UnitedHealthcare and Optum say they are committed to using AI responsibly, designing and maintaining AI to prioritize accuracy, human review, privacy, security, ethics and transparency. The article states that AI models do not store or replicate member data, do not make coverage decisions and do not replace clinical decision-making.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare's AI store member data?
Does AI make coverage decisions at UnitedHealthcare?

atoms.title: Generative chat and AI-assisted calls
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare use AI to answer member questions?
atoms.text: Because about half of insured adults surveyed reported difficulty understanding at least one aspect of their health insurance, UnitedHealthcare introduced a generative chat messaging experience that summarizes benefits and coverage information in a conversational style. For complicated matters, the chat can connect a member to a human Advocate. On a call, an AI-powered assistant uses natural language processing to identify the reason for calling and direct the member to self-service or a live advocate.
qs: Can I chat with UnitedHealthcare about my benefits?
How does UnitedHealthcare's AI phone assistant work?

atoms.title: Smart Choice provider search
atoms.q: What is the Smart Choice provider search?
atoms.text: Smart Choice is a UnitedHealthcare provider search experience that uses AI modeling to prioritize provider search results based on quality criteria, the member's specific benefits and coverage, convenience to the member and personal preferences. It aims to reduce the time employees and their families spend sifting through care options and to help them make more informed choices.
qs: What is Smart Choice?
How does UnitedHealthcare rank providers in search results?

atoms.title: AI tools for Advocates
atoms.q: How does AI help UnitedHealthcare Advocates?
atoms.text: AI assists Advocates by surfacing real-time, member-specific information on their screens based on claims activity or previous calls, which streamlines authentication and personalizes support. Voice analytics help understand the member's questions and provide benefits, coverage and cost answers, then summarize the conversation for the member's file. The article states 71M calls to UnitedHealthcare Advocates were assisted by AI-enabled technology.
qs: How does AI help advocates answer my questions?
Why don't I have to repeat my history when I call back?

atoms.title: Optum Real and provider documentation time
atoms.q: What is Optum Real and what results has it shown?
atoms.text: Optum Real is powered by AI and automation and facilitates the real-time exchange of patient visit, claim and payment data between providers and payers like UnitedHealthcare that buy the program. Launched in 2025, more than 4,000 providers have used the solution, which has saved them 2M minutes on documentation across 360,000 visits. A 43% cut in note-taking time is also reported.
qs: What is Optum Real?
How much time has Optum Real saved providers?

atoms.title: Ambient AI for clinical notes
atoms.q: How is Optum using ambient AI with providers?
atoms.text: To ease administrative burden for providers, Optum is integrating ambient, conversational and generative AI to capture patient-provider conversations in real time and generate structured clinical summaries. This allows providers to spend less time typing and more time engaging with patients and coordinating their care.
qs: What does ambient AI do for doctors?
How can AI reduce paperwork for providers?

atoms.title: AI-assisted prescription refill pilot
atoms.q: What did the AI prescription refill pilot show?
atoms.text: AI is being used to help read and prioritize prescription refill requests, reducing the time nurses spend intaking requests or reaching out to patients. In a 16-week pilot with 27 providers, more than 25,000 refills were processed efficiently, with 30% approved in one click.
qs: How does AI help with prescription refills?
How many refills were processed in the AI pilot?

atoms.title: Predicting care needs with AI
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare use predictive analytics?
atoms.text: Predictive analytics using AI help UnitedHealthcare anticipate care gaps, flag preventive services due for renewal and give members information for timely interventions. For example, models can flag when an employee with diabetes is due for a routine checkup. The article cites a 2X increase in the diagnosis of medical conditions using risk-prediction scoring, with clinicians and Advocates reviewing AI predictions.
qs: Can AI flag when I'm due for a checkup?
How does UnitedHealthcare predict care gaps?

atoms.title: Care paths based on members like them
atoms.q: What are AI-suggested care paths?
atoms.text: AI is also used to proactively serve up optional services or care paths that members may find relevant, based on members like them with similar demographics and care journeys. The article describes this as part of making it easier to navigate the health system with timely, coordinated support.
qs: What is a care path suggestion?
Does UnitedHealthcare recommend services based on similar members?

atoms.title: Why AI coordination matters to employers
atoms.q: How can AI-enabled tools benefit employers?
atoms.text: For employers, AI-powered tools may translate to healthier, more satisfied workforces. When finding care feels as seamless as other daily experiences, employees may be more likely to address health concerns earlier and seek care from quality providers who may be more cost-effective. Streamlined care may also let employees spend less time on care and more time focused at work.
qs: How does AI care coordination help employers?
Can AI help employees get care sooner?

atoms.title: UnitedHealth Group Responsible AI program
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealth Group's Responsible AI program?
atoms.text: UnitedHealth Group and its businesses, UnitedHealthcare and Optum, established a comprehensive Responsible Artificial Intelligence (RAI) program. The program works to guide the development, deployment and maintenance of AI across the enterprise to ensure it is designed and used fairly and ethically.
qs: What is Responsible AI at UnitedHealthcare?
How does UnitedHealth Group govern its AI?

atoms.title: AI review board composition
atoms.q: Who reviews AI at UnitedHealthcare?
atoms.text: AI at UnitedHealth Group is continuously evaluated and monitored by a review board of senior leaders with diverse expertise, including clinicians, clinical ethicists, business leaders and experts in analytics, technology, legal, compliance, regulatory and privacy matters. The board reviews AI through the lens of six guiding principles.
qs: Who sits on UnitedHealth Group's AI review board?
Is UnitedHealthcare's AI monitored?

atoms.title: Principle: Reliability and quality
atoms.q: What does reliability and quality mean in UnitedHealth Group's AI principles?
atoms.text: Reliability and quality is the first of UnitedHealth Group's six AI principles. The organization emphasizes testing and monitoring AI solutions to ensure they perform reliably and meet quality expectations. This involves oversight to guarantee that AI solutions fulfill their intended purposes.
qs: How does UnitedHealth Group make sure its AI is reliable?
What are the AI guiding principles?

atoms.title: Principle: Fairness
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealth Group address AI fairness?
atoms.text: Under the Fairness principle, UnitedHealth Group is committed to assessing AI solutions for potential bias and ensuring they treat all individuals fairly. This includes evaluating the impact of AI on vulnerable groups and those at risk of exclusion from the health care system, which helps promote equity in health care delivery.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare test its AI for bias?
How does UnitedHealthcare promote fairness in AI?

atoms.title: Principle: Accountability
atoms.q: Who is accountable for AI at UnitedHealth Group?
atoms.text: Under the Accountability principle, UnitedHealth Group acknowledges its accountability for the AI solutions it implements. It establishes processes, governance structures and monitoring mechanisms to address issues or adverse outcomes promptly. AI solutions are not intended to replace clinical judgment but to support decision-making.
qs: Is UnitedHealthcare accountable for its AI outcomes?
Does AI replace clinical judgment at UnitedHealthcare?

atoms.title: Principle: Transparency
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealth Group approach AI transparency?
atoms.text: Transparency and explainability are critical components of UnitedHealth Group's approach to AI. The organization monitors the use of AI across its operations to understand how AI solutions are used and how they operate, which it says fosters trust and clarity in AI-driven processes.
qs: Is UnitedHealthcare transparent about AI use?
What does explainability mean for UnitedHealthcare AI?

atoms.title: Principle: Privacy and security
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealth Group protect data in AI?
atoms.text: UnitedHealth Group prioritizes safeguarding data privacy and security in the design, deployment and use of AI solutions. The organization adheres to its longstanding privacy and security practices, ensuring compliance with relevant laws, regulations and policy requirements.
qs: Is my data safe with UnitedHealthcare's AI?
How does UnitedHealth Group protect privacy when using AI?

atoms.title: Principle: Continuous improvement
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealth Group keep improving its AI practices?
atoms.text: Recognizing the rapidly evolving AI landscape, UnitedHealth Group commits to continuously improving its processes and practices. This includes staying abreast of industry best practices and regulatory guidance to ensure its AI solutions remain effective and responsible.
qs: Does UnitedHealth Group update its AI standards?
How does UnitedHealthcare keep AI practices current?

atoms.title: AI supports, not replaces, human-led work
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealth Group allow AI to replace human work?
atoms.text: UnitedHealth Group requires that AI is used in support of human-led work and not in replacement of it. The page explains that when it comes to health care, AI cannot fully account for the contextual awareness, empathy, ethical considerations, nuances, personal preferences and expertise that people working in the field can offer.
qs: Will AI replace people in health care decisions?
Why does UnitedHealth Group require human-led work with AI?

atoms.title: Why employers should vet carrier AI
atoms.q: Why should employers and brokers look at a carrier's AI governance?
atoms.text: The page tells employers, brokers and consultants to consider and understand how AI is leveraged and governed by benefits vendors and carriers before making selections. It says those considering UnitedHealthcare may feel more assured knowing AI is continuously evaluated and monitored by a review board.
qs: What should brokers check about a carrier's AI?
Should I ask insurers about AI governance?

atoms.title: Health spending and AI market growth
atoms.q: How large is U.S. health spending and the AI health care market?
atoms.text: The article states that U.S. health spending reached $4.9T in 2025, yet inefficiencies persist across the board. The use of AI in health care is projected to grow from $37B in 2025 to a $614B market by 2034. The article cites Menlo Ventures and Precedence Research for these figures.
qs: How much is the AI health care market projected to grow?
How much does the U.S. spend on health care?

atoms.title: AI with human oversight, not replacement
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare want AI to replace human oversight?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual executive says leveraging AI must be done responsibly. In his words, it is not about removing human oversight but about automating processes to provide pertinent information and data analysis faster, which can free up time for more human interaction. UnitedHealthcare cites a rigorous review process, an expert review board and constant human oversight.
qs: Does AI replace human oversight at UnitedHealthcare?
How does UnitedHealthcare govern its AI?

atoms.title: Types of artificial intelligence defined
atoms.q: What are the different types of AI?
atoms.text: The article defines AI as enabling machines to mimic human behavior. Machine learning (ML) uses statistical methods to help machines improve with experience. Deep learning is a type of ML that interprets multi-layer neural networks across large, complex datasets. Conversational AI is a type of deep learning able to respond to human language in natural dialogue.
qs: What is the difference between AI and machine learning?
What is conversational AI?

atoms.title: Generative, agentic and ambient AI
atoms.q: What are generative AI, agentic AI and ambient AI?
atoms.text: Generative AI is a type of deep learning capable of generating new content to address broad task requests. Agentic AI is a type of deep learning and generative AI capable of autonomous decision-making. Ambient AI is a type of machine learning that listens to conversations and observes environments to perform tasks like scribing clinical notes.
qs: What is agentic AI?
What is ambient AI in health care?

atoms.title: Disease prediction with AI
atoms.q: How does AI help with disease prediction?
atoms.text: AI can help identify the sickest or highest-risk individuals and support providers in taking timely action. Algorithms analyze evidence-based data to detect markers of undiagnosed conditions or increased risk, and clinicians review the predictions and recommend interventions. AI does not replace clinical judgment, it supports it. UnitedHealth Group data cites a 2X increase in the diagnosis of medical conditions using risk-prediction scoring.
qs: Can AI predict who is at high health risk?
Does AI replace a doctor's judgment?

atoms.title: AI-supported care coordination
atoms.q: How does AI support care coordination?
atoms.text: AI can help coordinate information sharing across providers and carriers, creating a more holistic view of an individual's coverage, medical history and care preferences. That can help providers or advocates navigate individuals to the most appropriate care or next-best action. The article reports that 71M calls to UnitedHealthcare Advocates were assisted by AI-enabled technology.
qs: How many UnitedHealthcare Advocate calls were assisted by AI?
How does AI help coordinate care?

atoms.title: AI for simpler benefit navigation
atoms.q: How can AI make navigating health benefits simpler?
atoms.text: By factoring in a member's health care journey, coverage and personal priorities, AI can enable more timely prompts, prioritized search results and relevant options that help members navigate the health system. This can reduce confusion and improve benefit understanding. The article notes more than 465 enhancements were made to the UnitedHealthcare app and myuhc.com in 2025.
qs: How does AI simplify health benefits?
How many updates did UnitedHealthcare make to its app in 2025?

atoms.title: AI for quicker issue resolution
atoms.q: How does AI help members get answers faster?
atoms.text: Conversational AI-powered chat tools help members get answers about coverage, costs and general inquiries. Integrated into tools used by providers, Advocates, brokers, consultants and employers, AI can give more visibility into member benefits and issues. The article reports a 56k reduction in UnitedHealth Group customer service calls from AI predicting common issues like prescriptions or payment problems.
qs: Can AI chat answer benefit questions?
How much did AI reduce customer service calls?

atoms.title: AI call routing and personalized support
atoms.q: How does AI route member calls?
atoms.text: When a member calls with a specific or complex question, AI can help understand the general reason for the call and route them to the right department for live support. It may also recommend relevant resources. The article reports that 10% of Optum Rx calls were resolved via self-service because AI predicted the caller's intent, with the rest routed to the right customer Advocate more efficiently.
qs: How does AI route calls to the right team?
What percent of Optum Rx calls were resolved by self-service?

atoms.title: AI-streamlined health care processes
atoms.q: What administrative tasks can AI streamline in health care?
atoms.text: AI can streamline processes by prioritizing prescription refill requests, flagging claims with missing or inaccurate information, generating report summaries and automating manual data entry. The article reports a 50% reduction in clinical documentation review time via Optum Real AI-powered technology, and says the efficiencies benefit members, providers, carriers, brokers, consultants and employers.
qs: What can AI automate in health insurance?
How much time did Optum Real save on documentation review?

atoms.title: Potential ROI of AI for employers
atoms.q: What return could employers see from carrier AI?
atoms.text: The article lists two potential returns for employers. Lower costs, through earlier diagnoses and interventions, reduced administrative burden and increased productivity as healthier employees tend to take fewer sick days. And improved employee retention, as workers experience a better health benefits journey with easier navigation, clearer cost and coverage information, timely personalized support and more coordinated care.
qs: What is the ROI of AI in employee health benefits?
How does AI help employee retention?

atoms.title: Six questions to ask a carrier about AI
atoms.q: What should employers ask a carrier about its AI use?
atoms.text: The article lists six questions for evaluating carriers: how AI simplifies and personalizes the member experience; what safeguards protect member data and ensure ethical use; how AI streamlines benefits enrollment and administration; how AI supports clinicians without making decisions for them; how AI speeds claims processing and what human oversight ensures claims are not decided solely by AI; and how the carrier compares to competitors.
qs: What questions should I ask a health insurer about AI?
How do I evaluate a carrier's AI standards?

atoms.title: Fortune AIQ 50 ranking
atoms.q: How was UnitedHealth Group ranked for AI adoption?
atoms.text: Fortune ranked UnitedHealth Group No. 1 in Health Care and No. 25 overall in its 2025 AIQ 50 list for its adoption and scaling of AI. The article's footnote says the polling ran from Aug. 29 to Sept. 19, 2025, and that Fortune and Time Inc. do not endorse products or services of UnitedHealth Group.
qs: Where did UnitedHealth Group rank on the Fortune AIQ 50?
Is UnitedHealth Group a leader in health care AI?

atoms.title: What a biosimilar is
atoms.q: What is a biosimilar drug?
atoms.text: A biosimilar is a biologic medical product that is highly similar to a reference product already approved by regulatory authorities. Biosimilars are developed to have no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity and potency compared with the original biologic (the reference drug). They are designed to provide the same therapeutic benefits as the reference product but are typically offered at a lower cost.
qs: What is a biosimilar?
Are biosimilars as safe as biologic drugs?

atoms.title: Biosimilars have saved the system nearly $445B
atoms.q: How much have biosimilars saved the health care system?
atoms.text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first biosimilar in 2015, and biosimilars have since contributed to health care system savings of nearly $445B. At last count, there were more than 70 FDA-approved biosimilars. Their efficacy is comparable to the original specialty drugs they are modeled after, leading to similar health outcomes.
qs: When was the first biosimilar approved?
How many biosimilars are FDA approved?

atoms.title: Employer concern over high-cost drugs
atoms.q: How concerned are employers about high-cost drugs and biosimilars?
atoms.text: Nine in 10 surveyed employers expressed concern about the future of high-cost drugs, and 27% indicated they were considering or planning to require employees to switch to biosimilars when available by 2025. The article notes pharmacy spend is expected to keep rising, with tariffs projected to increase it even further, with some estimates reaching as high as $51B.
qs: Are employers requiring biosimilar switches?
How might tariffs affect pharmacy costs?

atoms.title: Biologics and biosimilars vs brand and generics
atoms.q: How do biologics and biosimilars differ from brand and generic drugs?
atoms.text: Biologics and biosimilars are made from large molecules, which are difficult to develop and require sophisticated, more difficult production. Brand and generic medications are made from small molecules, are easy to develop and are mass-produced. Biosimilars can be a lower-cost alternative to specialty drugs but remain more costly than generics, while brand medications are typically more expensive than generics.
qs: Are biosimilars cheaper than generics?
Why are biologic drugs harder to make than generics?

atoms.title: Specialty drugs: under 2% of volume, 60%+ of spend
atoms.q: How much of pharmacy spending comes from specialty medications?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare data shows that specialty medications make up less than 2% of overall pharmacy volume yet account for more than 60% of total pharmacy spending. The U.S. biosimilars market is expected to grow 17.1% from 2025 to 2034, and currently available biosimilars treat conditions including inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, some cancers and diabetes.
qs: What share of pharmacy spend is specialty drugs?
What conditions do biosimilars treat?

atoms.title: Humira biosimilars are on standard PDLs
atoms.q: Has UnitedHealthcare added Humira biosimilars to its drug lists?
atoms.text: Yes. UnitedHealthcare has added biosimilars for Humira to its standard Prescription Drug Lists (PDLs) while it continues to monitor market dynamics and advocate for more accessible drug prices. The article notes Humira, which has a monthly list price in the thousands, may be cost-prohibitive for many employees, and that competition from biosimilar equivalents is helping drive down prices.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare cover Humira biosimilars?
Why are Humira biosimilars important for costs?

atoms.title: $1.66 PMPM employer savings with biosimilar strategies
atoms.q: How much can employers save with biosimilar management strategies?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare reports $1.66 PMPM in employer savings with biosimilar management strategies. Its stated philosophy is to select the most clinically appropriate therapies that provide the lowest net cost to members, whether that includes coverage for biosimilars, the innovator drug or a combination of the two.
qs: How much does biosimilar management save per member per month?
What is UnitedHealthcare's philosophy on biosimilar coverage?

atoms.title: Biosimilars and competition in drug pricing
atoms.q: How do biosimilars support affordability?
atoms.text: Optum Rx Chief Financial Officer Matthew Vesledahl calls biosimilars a game changer for affordability that level the playing field so more employees can access the drugs they need. UnitedHealthcare's Susan Maddux says supporting competition can help lower net costs for employers and out-of-pocket costs for employees, while ensuring manufacturers are incentivized to keep developing new medicines.
qs: Do biosimilars make drugs more affordable for employees?
Why does competition lower drug costs?

atoms.title: 4 tips to maximize biosimilar savings
atoms.q: What can employers do to get more value from biosimilars?
atoms.text: 1) Work with insurance carriers and pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to understand their position on biosimilars, including which medications they cover. 2) Invest in plan designs that include biosimilars in medical and pharmacy offerings. 3) Map out a communication plan to educate employees on how biosimilars, name brands and generics differ in cost and outcomes. 4) Offer employees incentives to switch from a reference drug to the biosimilar when available.
qs: How can employers encourage biosimilar use?
What should employers ask their PBM about biosimilars?

atoms.title: Obesity prevalence and cost
atoms.q: How common and costly is obesity in the U.S.?
atoms.text: With 2 in 5 adults and 1 in 5 children considered obese, obesity is prevalent in America and also expensive. Obesity and related conditions cost the U.S. health system nearly $173B a year. Combined with other chronic and metabolic conditions, such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease and some types of cancer, that cost rises to $4.9T.
qs: How much does obesity cost the U.S. health system?
What share of adults and children are obese?

atoms.title: Metabolic conditions drive employer spend
atoms.q: How much of employer health spend comes from metabolic conditions?
atoms.text: In 2023, 28% of UnitedHealthcare members had a metabolic condition, and those members accounted for 56% of their employer's total health care spend, 4x more than those without a metabolic condition. Sixty percent of surveyed employers said they are looking for more support from the health care industry in improving care management for costly conditions.
qs: What percent of employer health spend is from metabolic conditions?
Do employers want help managing costly conditions?

atoms.title: Don't treat GLP-1s as a single-point solution
atoms.q: Should employers rush to cover GLP-1 drugs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's Chief Data & Analytics Officer Craig Kurtzweil and Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rhonda Randall caution employers not to rush decisions about covering GLP-1s. They suggest a whole-person approach, noting that people taking these drugs are more successful at achieving and maintaining weight loss as part of a comprehensive lifestyle management program, and that employers get more value from coverage in that case.
qs: Should my company cover GLP-1 drugs?
Are GLP-1s more effective with lifestyle programs?

atoms.title: What GLP-1 drugs are and how they work
atoms.q: What are GLP-1 medications?
atoms.text: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medications were originally developed to help manage type 2 diabetes. They stimulate the body to produce more insulin when blood sugar levels start to rise, which helps lower glucose. Most are administered by injection, although oral versions are becoming more widely available. Drugs named include Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy, Zepbound and Mounjaro.
qs: What is a GLP-1 drug?
How do GLP-1 medications lower blood sugar?

atoms.title: GLP-1 spending up more than 500%
atoms.q: How much has U.S. spending on GLP-1 drugs grown?
atoms.text: Total U.S. spending on drugs like Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy, Zepbound and Mounjaro increased by more than 500% between 2018 and 2023, from $13.7B to $71.7B. Several, such as Wegovy and Zepbound, were approved for treating obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and heart attack or stroke prevention in people who have already had a cardiovascular event.
qs: How fast is GLP-1 spending growing?
What conditions are Wegovy and Zepbound approved for?

atoms.title: PMPM costs rose 91% after starting GLP-1s
atoms.q: How much do GLP-1 drugs raise per-member costs?
atoms.text: The average cost of GLP-1 drugs can exceed $1,000 per patient per month. Costs per member per month (PMPM) increased 91% between the 12 months before members started a GLP-1 and the 12 months after. ER visits also increased 10% among members after starting a GLP-1, which the article links partly to side effects such as nausea and other gastrointestinal issues.
qs: How much does a GLP-1 cost per month?
Do GLP-1 drugs increase employer costs?

atoms.title: 58% stop GLP-1s before benefit
atoms.q: How many patients stop taking GLP-1 drugs early?
atoms.text: 58% of patients stop taking GLP-1s before seeing a clinically meaningful health benefit. The article attributes low adherence partly to the months it can take to reach the full effective dose and to side effects such as nausea, diarrhea, constipation and vomiting. UnitedHealthcare's Kurtzweil says employers are not seeing a significant return on investment or improvements in employee health.
qs: Why do people stop taking GLP-1 drugs?
Do employers get a return on GLP-1 coverage?

atoms.title: Clinical caution about GLP-1 long-term effects
atoms.q: What long-term concerns exist about GLP-1 drugs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's Chief Medical Officer Dr. Rhonda Randall says carriers are still learning where GLP-1s are most effective and what their long-term side effects are, and she is concerned that people may lose more muscle mass than fat cells. This reinforces pairing the drugs with lifestyle changes and other weight loss support. GLP-1s for weight loss are currently injections, with pill forms in development.
qs: Do GLP-1 drugs cause muscle loss?
Are there pill versions of GLP-1 weight loss drugs?

atoms.title: How UnitedHealthcare evaluates new drugs
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare decide how to cover new drugs like GLP-1s?
atoms.text: Carriers are evaluating the efficacy and use cases of new drugs to determine how they should be covered, based on the latest clinical studies and medical evidence. Susan Maddux, chief pharmacy officer for UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual, says UnitedHealthcare constantly monitors drugs under development and potential new uses for approved ones, typically starting discussions to build a strategy even before approval.
qs: How does UnitedHealthcare decide on drug coverage?
Does UnitedHealthcare plan ahead for new drug approvals?

atoms.title: Total Weight Support program
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealthcare's Total Weight Support?
atoms.text: Total Weight Support is a UnitedHealthcare program that addresses multiple aspects of an employee's weight management, including pharmaceutical, clinical and behavioral support. It teaches sustainable lifestyle habits such as balanced diet and more physical activity, supports drug adherence and side-effect management if GLP-1s or other weight-loss medications are used, and provides digital tools and social support throughout the member journey.
qs: What is Total Weight Support?
Does UnitedHealthcare offer a weight loss program that supports GLP-1 users?

atoms.title: Employers should build comprehensive weight strategies
atoms.q: What should employers do about GLP-1 coverage pressure?
atoms.text: While employers may feel pressure from employees to cover GLP-1s, the article says it is imperative to consider the costs and adherence challenges. It advises employers to work with their carrier to build a benefits strategy that includes a comprehensive weight-loss approach addressing the many factors that can contribute to obesity and related conditions. Employers who cover them and later stop may also have to explain the decision.
qs: How should employers respond to employees asking for GLP-1 coverage?
What happens if an employer stops covering GLP-1s?

atoms.title: Emergent ER visits are rising
atoms.q: Are emergency room visits increasing?
atoms.text: Emergent visits increased 6% and accounted for two-thirds of all emergency department visits between the third quarter of 2024 and the second quarter of 2025, and this trend is expected to continue over the next decade. By 2035, overall emergency department visits are projected to grow 5%, largely driven by an anticipated 8% rise in emergent visits.
qs: How fast are ER visits growing?
What share of ER visits are emergent?

atoms.title: ER visits cost far more than other settings
atoms.q: How much more does the ER cost than urgent care?
atoms.text: The ER serves a critical function but comes with a much higher price tag than other care settings. About $8.3B is spent annually on ER trips that could have been treated more cost-effectively elsewhere. A non-emergent ER visit tends to cost UnitedHealthcare clients and members 10 times more than an urgent care visit.
qs: How much does a non-emergent ER visit cost compared with urgent care?
How much is spent on avoidable ER visits?

atoms.title: Low health care literacy raises ER use 3.7 times
atoms.q: How does health care literacy affect ER use?
atoms.text: Generally healthy people with low health care literacy were 3.7 times more likely to visit the ER than those with high health care knowledge. Low health care literacy means lacking understanding about how to access and use health care benefits. UnitedHealthcare says boosting health care knowledge may be critical to helping employees maximize benefits and manage costs.
qs: Why do people with low health literacy use the ER more?
How much more likely is ER use with low health literacy?

atoms.title: Why employees choose the ER
atoms.q: Why do employees go to the ER for non-emergencies?
atoms.text: Employees may go to the ER by default, assuming they can receive prompt treatment. Other reasons include a limited understanding of benefits coverage, a belief that treatment will be quicker, or insufficient access to alternative health care options nearby. UnitedHealthcare's Craig Kurtzweil notes these decisions are often made in the moment, which is why the employer as educator role is so important.
qs: Why do people choose the ER over urgent care?
What drives non-emergent ER visits?

atoms.title: Strategy 1: Educate employees on appropriate ER use
atoms.q: How can employers educate employees about where to go for care?
atoms.text: Employers can dedicate time in employee meetings or email communications to topics such as network versus out-of-network providers, how prior authorizations can give insight into upcoming costs, and where to go for care based on different needs. Education should continue throughout the plan year, not only at open enrollment. Best practices include varying communications by preference, listening to feedback, reviewing claims data, aligning messages to timely topics and diversifying tactics.
qs: What should employers teach employees about ER use?
How often should benefits education happen?

atoms.title: Case example: trucking company ER education campaign
atoms.q: Did an ER education campaign reduce non-emergent visits?
atoms.text: A trucking company with high ER usage and low virtual visit rates worked with UnitedHealthcare on an education campaign using direct mail, email and a magnet for the truck cabin listing appropriate care options. The goal was to divert non-emergent ER visits to urgent care and primary care. Preliminary results showed a 17% decrease in non-emergent visits.
qs: Is there an example of reducing ER visits through education?
What results came from the ER education campaign?

atoms.title: Strategy 2: Improve access to alternative care settings
atoms.q: How can employers improve access to alternatives to the ER?
atoms.text: ER use can fall when employers address access-to-care challenges, including nonmedical factors such as economic stability, education and neighborhoods. Where care options are limited, employers can adopt a network strategy that includes a robust virtual network or on-demand care. Wellness incentive programs that offer low- to no-cost preventive screenings can encourage employees to establish an in-person or virtual relationship with a primary care provider.
qs: How can employers reduce ER use in areas with few care options?
Does having a PCP reduce ER visits?

atoms.title: Strategy 3: Carrier support to navigate care
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare help members use the right care setting?
atoms.text: By analyzing member claim data, UnitedHealthcare Advocates can proactively identify at-risk members with complex conditions and provide one-on-one support, including directing them to appropriate sites of care or enrolling them in care management programs. Members enrolled in Complex Care Concierge saw a 10% drop in ER visits.
qs: What is Complex Care Concierge?
How do Advocates reduce ER visits?

atoms.title: Predictive model redirected 3,100 ER visits
atoms.q: How much did UnitedHealthcare's ER campaign save?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare scored members on their likelihood of using the ER for non-emergent care, using diagnosis and claims history, ER utilization, demographics, plan information and other variables. Members with a high likelihood were targeted with a 2024 communications campaign. The campaign redirected 3,100 ER visits and produced an estimated $7.6M in cost savings.
qs: How many ER visits were redirected in the campaign?
What savings come from ER redirection?

atoms.title: Post-ER-visit outreach process
atoms.q: What happens after a member visits the ER?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare has a post-ER-visit strategy in which Advocates reach out after a member seeks ER care. 1) Real-time Admit Discharge Transfer (ADT) alerts trigger outreach. 2) A registered nurse contacts the member within a short time of discharge. 3) The nurse answers post-visit questions, connects the member to a PCP or specialist for follow-up, and explains other site-of-care options for future needs.
qs: What is an ADT alert?
Does UnitedHealthcare follow up after an ER visit?

atoms.title: Lower total cost of care versus benchmarks
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare lower total cost of care?
atoms.text: A third-party study found UnitedHealthcare delivered a more than 11% lower total cost of care for employers compared with national benchmarks. Contributing to the savings were lower-than-average outpatient costs, likely driven by efforts to navigate members from higher-cost settings like the ER toward lower-cost settings when appropriate.
qs: How much lower is UnitedHealthcare's total cost of care?
What drives lower outpatient costs?

atoms.title: IRS announces 2025 HSA and HDHP limits
atoms.q: What did the IRS announce for 2025 HSA and HDHP limits?
atoms.text: The Internal Revenue Service announced inflation-adjusted 2025 minimum deductibles, out-of-pocket maximums and contribution limits for health savings accounts (HSAs) and qualified high deductible health plans (HDHPs). The changes are effective on the employer's benefit plan year beginning Jan. 1, 2025, or later.
qs: What are the 2025 HSA limits?
When do the 2025 HSA changes take effect?

atoms.title: 2025 HDHP minimum deductibles
atoms.q: What is the minimum deductible for an HSA-qualified HDHP in 2025?
atoms.text: For 2025, the minimum deductible is $1,650 for self-only coverage, a $50 increase from 2024. It is $3,300 for family coverage, a $100 increase, and $3,300 for an embedded individual deductible, also a $100 increase from 2024.
qs: What is the HDHP minimum deductible for family coverage in 2025?
How much did the HDHP minimum deductible rise in 2025?

atoms.title: 2025 HDHP out-of-pocket maximums
atoms.q: What is the 2025 out-of-pocket maximum for an HSA-qualified HDHP?
atoms.text: For 2025, the HDHP out-of-pocket maximum is $8,300 for self-only coverage, a $250 increase from 2024, and $16,600 for family coverage, a $500 increase. UnitedHealthcare advises being aware of the intersection of HSA and Affordable Care Act (ACA) rules; the 2025 ACA maximum is $9,200 for individual coverage, versus $9,450 in 2024.
qs: What is the 2025 HSA out-of-pocket maximum for families?
How do HSA and ACA out-of-pocket limits interact?

atoms.title: Embedded vs non-embedded OOP examples for 2025
atoms.q: How do embedded and non-embedded out-of-pocket maximums affect HSA/ACA compliance?
atoms.text: For one plan covering both self-only and family coverage with an embedded out-of-pocket maximum, the 2025 maximums are $8,300 for an individual and $16,600 for a family. With a non-embedded out-of-pocket maximum, the 2025 maximums are $8,300 for an individual and $9,200 for a family.
qs: What is the family OOP limit for a non-embedded HDHP in 2025?
What makes an HSA/ACA plan compliant?

atoms.title: 2025 HSA contribution limits
atoms.q: What are the 2025 HSA contribution limits?
atoms.text: For 2025, the HSA contribution limit is $4,300 for self-only coverage, an increase of $150 from 2024, and $8,550 for family coverage, an increase of $250. The annual catch-up contribution amount for individuals ages 55 or older remains $1,000.
qs: How much can I contribute to an HSA in 2025?
What is the HSA catch-up contribution for age 55 and older?

atoms.title: More than 40.1M Americans have diabetes
atoms.q: How many Americans have diabetes?
atoms.text: More than 40.1M Americans are living with diabetes, a condition that impairs the body's ability to regulate blood sugar through the interplay of genetics, hormonal factors, physical inactivity and diet. Around 90 to 95% of people with diabetes have type 2. Long-term complications raise the risk of heart disease, stroke, blindness, kidney failure and amputation due to nerve damage in the extremities.
qs: How many people in the U.S. have diabetes?
What percent of diabetes is type 2?
What complications come with type 2 diabetes?

atoms.title: Diabetes costs $413B a year
atoms.q: How much does diabetes cost the U.S. each year?
atoms.text: The annual medical and economic cost of diabetes is $413B, with the average per-member cost reaching $1,045. For employers, these numbers represent growing pressure on workforce health and organizational cost, but employers can also play a vital role in managing these pressures while supporting employees who have diabetes.
qs: What is the cost of diabetes to employers?
What is the average per-member cost of diabetes?

atoms.title: Whole-person approach to diabetes
atoms.q: How can employers take a whole-person approach to diabetes?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says employers can help manage the spike in diabetes by embracing a whole-person health approach. Dr. Rhonda Randall, Chief Medical Officer of UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual, notes that type 2 diabetes and its warning sign, prediabetes, are sweeping across the country, and that with lifestyle modification and clinical support this can be reversed.
qs: What is a whole-person approach to chronic conditions?
Can type 2 diabetes be reversed?

atoms.title: What the Level2 program is
atoms.q: What is the Level2 program from UnitedHealthcare?
atoms.text: Level2 from UnitedHealthcare is a clinical model, compatible with existing UnitedHealthcare health plans, built to change the cost trajectory of type 2 diabetes. It gives members the tools, guidance and care they need to work toward improving their condition while giving employers the financial confidence to act.
qs: What is Level2?
Does Level2 work with my UnitedHealthcare plan?

atoms.title: How Level2 works
atoms.q: How does the Level2 diabetes program work?
atoms.text: 1) After joining, participants receive a prescribed continuous glucose monitor (CGM) at no cost. 2) CGM data informs Level2 provider-led care teams of physicians, nurses, dietitians and coaches, who offer one-on-one personalized guidance. 3) Personalized care aims to help participants form healthier habits, with the goal of lowering average blood glucose, improving their condition and even pursuing remission as defined by the American Diabetes Association.
qs: Do Level2 participants get a glucose monitor?
Who is on a Level2 care team?

atoms.title: Level2 reconciles fees against outcomes
atoms.q: How does Level2 reduce financial risk for employers?
atoms.text: Because the cost and financial risk of adding a new program can be a barrier, Level2 aims to reduce that risk by reconciling 100% of program fees against actual clinical outcomes and actual medical and pharmacy claims. The Level2 team is also expanding capabilities to proactively help employees living with prediabetes or extra weight, which can be precursors to type 2 diabetes.
qs: Is Level2 guaranteed by results?
Does Level2 cover prediabetes?

atoms.title: Surest diabetes reversal program and ER results
atoms.q: How does Surest support members with type 2 diabetes?
atoms.text: The Surest health plan includes a diabetes reversal program that educates members dealing with a type 2 diabetes diagnosis. Surest also offers member support through its Clinical Advocacy team and provides upfront pricing and coverage choices. Surest members with type 2 diabetes had 13% fewer ER visits than non-Surest members, through effective early management and preventive care.
qs: Does Surest have a diabetes program?
How do Surest members with diabetes use the ER?

atoms.title: UHC Hub and Dario for diabetes support
atoms.q: What other diabetes support options can employers add?
atoms.text: UHC Hub gives employers a platform to select from a portfolio of vendors, including lifestyle and specialized health and wellness vendors. Dario delivers personalized digital health programs to help manage diabetes, blood pressure, weight, posture and mental wellness, and is available through UHC Store, a digital shop exclusive to UnitedHealthcare members via the UnitedHealthcare app and myuhc.com.
qs: What is Dario?
What is UHC Hub?

atoms.title: Gurley Leep results: 97% activation, 51% less insulin
atoms.q: What results did an employer see with Level2?
atoms.text: In a case study, Gurley Leep Automotive Family offered Level2 to employees with type 2 diabetes. The company saw 97% activation of the program, 91% of those employees connected to their CGM, and a 51% decrease in insulin usage among type 2 diabetic employees engaged in the program.
qs: What is the Level2 participation rate?
Did Level2 reduce insulin use?

atoms.title: Large client results after one year of Level2
atoms.q: What were the one-year results of Level2 for a large client?
atoms.text: For a larger UnitedHealthcare client, one year of Level2 data showed 12.8% per member, per month realized claims savings versus the projected 2024 cost trend, a 0.73 reduction in average glucose management indicator (GMI) among participants with a lab A1C within 6 months of joining, 20% lower inpatient admissions, and an 85 Net Promoter Score.
qs: What savings does Level2 deliver?
How much did Level2 lower glucose levels?

atoms.title: What a self-funded health plan is
atoms.q: What is a self-funded health plan?
atoms.text: In a self-funded (self-insured) plan, the employer takes on the financial risk of providing health benefits to employees and covered dependents, rather than the insurer. Employers pay if claims are higher than expected, but may save money compared with a fully insured plan, where savings stay with the insurer. Sixty-three percent of covered employees were in a self-funded or self-insured plan in 2024, per KFF.
qs: What does self-funded health insurance mean?
What percent of employees are in self-funded plans?

atoms.title: Myth: self-funded plans are only for large companies
atoms.q: Are self-funded health plans only for large companies?
atoms.text: No. Many large businesses choose self-funding because they can spread the risk of costly claims across many employees, but smaller and midsize employers are adopting it too. From 2010 to 2023, the percentage of small employers offering at least one self-insured plan grew from 13% to 16%, and medium-sized firms rose from 27% to 32%, according to EBRI research.
qs: Can a small business self-fund its health plan?
How many small employers offer self-insured plans?

atoms.title: Myth: self-funded plans are too risky
atoms.q: Are self-funded health plans too risky?
atoms.text: Employers shoulder the financial risk, and predicting exact claims is impossible, which can lead to higher or lower costs. A key advantage is that employers pay only for what employees use, and educating staff to make cost-effective choices, like choosing urgent care over the ER for minor issues, can keep costs down. Stop loss coverage offers protection against catastrophic claims.
qs: How do employers manage risk in self-funded plans?
What is stop loss coverage?

atoms.title: Myth: self-funded plans are too much work
atoms.q: Do self-funded health plans require a lot of administrative work?
atoms.text: Self-funded plans do require more effort than fully insured plans. Employers must handle significant administrative tasks like regulatory compliance and claims processing, though health plan representatives, brokers and consultants can often provide support. Insurers can also help employers customize benefits based on claims data, such as launching campaigns for a workforce with many employees with diabetes or dependents with behavioral health issues.
qs: How much work is it to run a self-funded plan?
Can brokers help administer a self-funded plan?

atoms.title: Myth: self-funded plans aren't cost-effective
atoms.q: Are self-funded health plans cost-effective?
atoms.text: Self-funded plans can be cost-effective because employers pay only for actual claims incurred rather than a fixed premium to an insurer. Employers also get detailed plan data to identify trends and optimize benefits, and stop loss insurance provides a safety net against catastrophic claims. Tailoring coverage to a workforce's needs can lead to better health outcomes and lower long-term costs.
qs: Does self-funding save employers money?
What data do self-funded employers receive?

atoms.title: When self-funding may not fit an employer
atoms.q: When might a self-funded plan not be the best option?
atoms.text: Self-funded health plans may not be for everyone. If a smaller employer has a workforce with higher health risks, a history of expensive claims, turbulence related to the business's financial health or large fluctuations in staffing, a self-funded plan may lead to steeper costs. In that case, a fully insured plan, or the happy medium of a level-funded plan, may be worth exploring.
qs: Which employers shouldn't self-fund?
Is level funded a middle ground between self-funded and fully insured?

atoms.title: Self-funding adds benefit design flexibility
atoms.q: How does self-funding give employers more flexibility?
atoms.text: With a self-funded health plan, employers have more flexibility in designing benefits to meet the unique needs of their workforce, which may help contribute to better outcomes. Access to detailed plan data, including claims and utilization patterns, lets employers customize and optimize benefits and better engage employees in decisions that may lead to lower costs and better health outcomes.
qs: Why do employers choose self-funded plans?
What data do self-funded employers use to design benefits?

atoms.title: 2026 and 2025 group plan OOPM limits
atoms.q: What is the out-of-pocket maximum for group health plans in 2026?
atoms.text: For the 2026 plan year, the out-of-pocket maximum (OOPM) for group health plans is $10,150 for self-only coverage and $20,300 for family coverage. For the 2025 plan year it is $9,200 for self-only and $18,400 for family. The annual OOPM requirement applies to most non-grandfathered group health plans.
qs: What is the 2026 out-of-pocket maximum for group plans?
What was the 2025 family out-of-pocket maximum?

atoms.title: 2026 OOPM rises 10.3%
atoms.q: How much did the ACA out-of-pocket maximum increase for 2026?
atoms.text: The 2026 out-of-pocket maximum (OOPM) represents a 10.3% increase over the 2025 OOPM parameters. Self-only coverage moves from $9,200 in 2025 to $10,150 in 2026, and family coverage moves from $18,400 to $20,300, for plans subject to the annual requirement.
qs: How big was the 2026 OOPM increase?
How much higher is the 2026 out-of-pocket max than 2025?

atoms.title: Which plans the OOPM requirement covers
atoms.q: Which group health plans must follow the annual OOPM requirement?
atoms.text: The annual out-of-pocket maximum requirement applies to most non-grandfathered group health plans, regardless of whether the plan is fully insured or self-funded (ASO). It does not apply to grandfathered, Transitional Relief or retiree-only plans.
qs: Does the OOPM apply to self-funded plans?
Are grandfathered plans subject to the out-of-pocket maximum?

atoms.title: What counts toward the OOPM
atoms.q: What cost-sharing counts toward the out-of-pocket maximum?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that the annual out-of-pocket maximum (OOPM) for group health plans includes copayments, deductibles and coinsurance amounts associated with both medical and pharmacy covered benefits, so pharmacy cost sharing counts toward the same limit as medical cost sharing.
qs: Do pharmacy costs count toward the out-of-pocket maximum?
What is included in the OOPM?

atoms.title: HSA-qualified HDHP limits are different
atoms.q: Do HSA-eligible high deductible plans have the same OOPM limits?
atoms.text: No. High-deductible health plans with health savings accounts (HSAs) have different limits, including out-of-pocket maximum, deductible and contribution limits. These limits are historically released in May, and the 2026 out-of-pocket, deductible and contribution limits will be communicated once available.
qs: When are HSA limits announced?
Is the HDHP out-of-pocket maximum different from the ACA OOPM?

atoms.title: What menopause is and its common symptoms
atoms.q: What is menopause and what symptoms can it cause?
atoms.text: Menopause is a biological process that marks the end of a woman's reproductive years, typically occurring between the ages of 45 and 55. The transition from perimenopause to post-menopause can bring physical and emotional symptoms, including hot flashes, night sweats, mood swings, fatigue and difficulty concentrating. These symptoms vary in intensity and duration and can affect a woman's ability to perform her job.
qs: What age does menopause usually happen?
What are common menopause symptoms?
How can menopause affect work performance?

atoms.title: Nearly 3 in 4 women say menopause affects work
atoms.q: How many women say menopause symptoms affect their work?
atoms.text: Nearly 3 in 4 women report that menopause symptoms impact some aspect of their work life, and decreased productivity can carry significant economic effects for organizations. UnitedHealthcare describes menopause as becoming a measurable workforce and productivity issue for employers because women in midlife represent a growing share of the workforce.
qs: What percentage of women say menopause affects work?
Why should employers care about menopause?
Does menopause reduce workplace productivity?

atoms.title: Midlife women remain a large share of the workforce
atoms.q: How many women in midlife are still working?
atoms.text: It is estimated that 86% of women ages 50-54 and 79% of women ages 55-60 are still active in the workplace. Women in these age groups represent 20% of today's workforce, which is why UnitedHealthcare says it is important for them to feel supported by their employers and for their specific health needs to be addressed.
qs: What share of the workforce are women in midlife?
How many women ages 50 to 60 are still working?

atoms.title: Women's health as a life-stage strategy
atoms.q: Why are employers rethinking women's health benefits?
atoms.text: Employers are rethinking women's health more broadly. Supporting women across life stages, from early adulthood through menopause, is increasingly a strategic lever for cost management, productivity and retention. UnitedHealthcare's Craig Kurtzweil notes that women's health discussions often focus on maternity or infertility-based services, while menopause has had a wide impact across the female population in UnitedHealthcare's book of business.
qs: Is menopause covered in women's health strategy?
How do employers support women across life stages?

atoms.title: Six strategies for supporting midlife women
atoms.q: What are the six ways employers can support women going through menopause?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare outlines six strategies employers can use to build a more inclusive culture and benefits plan for women navigating menopause: educate the workforce, provide flexible work arrangements, offer mental health support, provide access to robust women's health benefits, encourage open communication, and support overall health and well-being.
qs: How can employers support menopause at work?
What are menopause-friendly workplace strategies?

atoms.title: Educate managers and employees about menopause
atoms.q: How can employers educate their workforce about menopause?
atoms.text: The first step in supporting women going through menopause is to educate both management and employees. Many people, including women themselves, may not fully understand how menopause can affect daily life. Training sessions or workshops can help break down stigma and build a more empathetic workforce, and can cover how to recognize menopause symptoms and strategies for managing them.
qs: How do I train managers on menopause?
Why educate employees about menopause?

atoms.title: Flexible work arrangements for menopause symptoms
atoms.q: How can flexible work help employees with menopause?
atoms.text: Offering flexible work arrangements is described as one of the most effective ways to support women during menopause. Options include flexible start and end times, working from home, or taking short breaks during the day. For example, a woman with hot flashes may need to step away from her desk to cool down, and someone with fatigue may benefit from a schedule that allows for rest.
qs: What workplace flexibility helps with menopause?
Should employers offer flexible schedules for menopause?

atoms.title: Mental health support during menopause
atoms.q: What mental health resources help employees going through menopause?
atoms.text: Menopause can significantly affect mental health, with many women experiencing increased stress, anxiety and mood swings. Employers can offer access to behavioral health resources such as employee assistance programs (EAPs) or the Calm Health app, which offers personalized recommendations and support for women navigating menopause. These resources give women tools to manage their mental health and cope with menopause-related challenges.
qs: Does Calm Health support menopause?
How do EAPs help with menopause stress?

atoms.title: Women's health benefits that cover menopause care
atoms.q: What benefits should cover perimenopause and menopause?
atoms.text: Robust women's health benefits can be crucial for supporting women through perimenopause and menopause. That includes a large network of providers or virtual providers, and coverage of treatments such as hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and medications that help with hot flashes and osteoporosis. Through UHC Hub, employers can shop a portfolio of vendors selected by UnitedHealthcare, including offerings that provide personalized 24/7 virtual support and guidance for menopause.
qs: Is hormone replacement therapy part of menopause benefits?
What is UHC Hub for menopause support?

atoms.title: Open communication and overall wellness support
atoms.q: How can employers encourage open communication and overall wellness for menopause?
atoms.text: Employers can build a culture where women feel comfortable discussing menopause needs through regular check-ins, anonymous feedback mechanisms and managers trained to handle sensitive conversations with empathy. Employers can also support overall well-being through wellness programs, on-site fitness centers, clinics and pharmacies. UHC Store, available through the UnitedHealthcare app and myuhc.com, offers options including Embr Labs, Elektra Health and Ovia Health by Labcorp.
qs: What is UHC Store?
What vendors support menopause through UHC Store?
How can managers talk about menopause?

atoms.title: Menopause as a productivity and experience lever
atoms.q: Why is menopause support a performance and equity issue?
atoms.text: Menopause often coincides with peak career years, which makes support both an equity and a performance issue. As more women remain in the workforce longer, menopause is becoming a defining moment in the employee experience. Employers that take a proactive, life-stage approach to women's health may be better positioned to improve performance, retention and long-term cost trends.
qs: Does menopause support improve retention?
Why is menopause an employee experience issue?

atoms.title: How a fully insured plan works
atoms.q: What is a fully insured health plan and who pays the claims?
atoms.text: In a fully insured health plan, the employer pays a fixed premium to the health insurance carrier, which covers the cost of employee health care. When employees incur expenses, the carrier is responsible for paying the claims, not the employer. The financial risk and responsibility transfer to the carrier, which also handles much of the administrative work and regulatory compliance.
qs: What does fully insured mean for employers?
Who is responsible for claims in a fully insured plan?

atoms.title: Fully insured plans can cost more
atoms.q: Why can fully insured plans cost employers more?
atoms.text: Because the carrier assumes the risk, fully insured plans can be more costly for employers than other options. For example, the total of an employer's monthly premium payments over a year might exceed the actual claims made by employees. Even so, many employers choose fully insured plans because they provide consistent, predictable monthly costs.
qs: Are fully insured plans more expensive?
Why do employers still choose fully insured plans?

atoms.title: Fully insured fits employers who need support
atoms.q: When does a fully insured plan work well for employers who need support?
atoms.text: Fully insured plans work well for employers who lack the time or staff to manage benefits, especially small businesses. Employers can outsource the responsibility of meeting federal and state legal requirements to the carrier, typically choose from off-the-shelf benefits packages and hand off administration, compliance and claims payments to the carrier. UnitedHealthcare notes some customizations are still possible with a fully insured plan.
qs: Is fully insured better for businesses without HR staff?
Can fully insured plans be customized?

atoms.title: Fully insured fits unpredictable claims
atoms.q: When does a fully insured plan suit employers with unpredictable claims?
atoms.text: A fixed monthly premium can provide financial security if a workforce includes employees with cancer diagnoses or pregnancies, which can increase claims. UnitedHealthcare cites that by 2027 cancer is expected to comprise 30% of employer health spend, and that employers pay an average of around $14K annually for medical costs for an employee with diabetes.
qs: Should employers with high claims choose fully insured?
How much does diabetes cost an employer annually?

atoms.title: Fully insured fits risk-averse employers
atoms.q: Who benefits most from the fixed premium of a fully insured plan?
atoms.text: The employer and carrier typically agree on a fixed monthly premium at the start of the plan year, based on the workforce and the insurer's fees, and it stays the same all year so employers can budget with certainty. For risk-averse employers, especially smaller ones, this is often the best choice, whereas larger employers can spread the risk of high claims more easily.
qs: Why do small employers prefer fixed monthly premiums?
How does a fully insured premium stay predictable?

atoms.title: Alternatives to fully insured for risk-tolerant employers
atoms.q: What if an employer wants more control than a fully insured plan offers?
atoms.text: A fully insured plan can offer a predictable, cost-effective solution, even if it means less control over plan customization and provider networks.
