For employers willing to take on more risk in exchange for greater control, flexibility and potential cost savings, self-funded or level-funded plans may be more appropriate. UnitedHealthcare points to 7 characteristics to check for readiness for these funding types.
qs: When should an employer move from fully insured to self-funded?
What are the tradeoffs of fully insured plans?

atoms.title: Fully insured prices remain a predictable fixed cost
atoms.q: Are fully insured plans still predictable even though prices rose?
atoms.text: Greg Reidy, East Region CEO for UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual, says that even though fully insured prices have increased, they remain a predictable fixed cost for the employer. This often can offer more stability than a self-funded environment, where claim costs can have more variability, even as health care premiums continue to rise.
qs: Are fully insured premiums rising?
Is fully insured more stable than self-funded?

atoms.title: What the Benefit Ecosystem is
atoms.q: What is the UnitedHealthcare Benefit Ecosystem?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare Benefit Ecosystem is designed to move away from manually intensive, time-consuming, error-prone benefits administration. Benefits administrators can look forward to real-time integration, streamlined enrollment and automated processing for eligibility and renewal. It creates stronger connections between UnitedHealthcare and leading benefits administration platforms.
qs: What is the UnitedHealthcare Benefit Ecosystem?
How does UnitedHealthcare streamline benefits administration?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare API Marketplace access
atoms.q: How do brokers access the Benefit Ecosystem?
atoms.text: The way into the benefits administration platform is through the UnitedHealthcare Application Programming Interface (API) Marketplace. It acts as the door where external stakeholders can securely access and use available APIs, and on the front end only licensed and appointed brokers and consultants are allowed in.
qs: Who can use the UnitedHealthcare API Marketplace?
How do I connect a benefits platform to UnitedHealthcare?

atoms.title: Automation and real-time data sharing
atoms.q: What does the Benefit Ecosystem automate?
atoms.text: Easier benefits administration in the UnitedHealthcare Benefit Ecosystem begins with automation. Automated tasks help eliminate hours of work, information may be shared in real time when the customer needs it, and available API integration continues to grow based on the needs of the benefits administration firm.
qs: Does the Benefit Ecosystem share data in real time?
How much work does benefits automation save?

atoms.title: Benefit Ecosystem advantages for brokers and consultants
atoms.q: How does the Benefit Ecosystem help brokers and consultants?
atoms.text: For brokers and consultants, the Benefit Ecosystem simplifies setting up UnitedHealthcare policies on connected benefits administration platforms. It makes it easier to generate quotes, capture employee elections and enrollment, renew plans and more. It also reduces manual work for agency staff and helps eliminate errors.
qs: Can brokers quote UnitedHealthcare through a benefits platform?
How does the Benefit Ecosystem reduce errors?

atoms.title: Benefit Ecosystem value by audience
atoms.q: How does the Benefit Ecosystem help employers, benefits administrators and members?
atoms.text: For employers, it automates information entry for greater accuracy and fewer member and HR issues, helps simplify benefits management and speeds up data sharing. For benefits administrators, it helps enable instant access to data, increases operational efficiency and drives more value for clients. For members, it helps improve the enrollment experience, supports digital adoption and eases access to coverage information at the point of service.
qs: What does the Benefit Ecosystem do for HR teams?
How does the Benefit Ecosystem improve member enrollment?

atoms.title: Quoting API and Benefits details API
atoms.q: What do the Quoting API and Benefits details API do?
atoms.text: The Quoting API allows electronic quotes to be transmitted to the digital aggregator tool. The Benefits details API offers benefit and product-level details. Both are among the key enhancements designed to streamline the UnitedHealthcare benefits administration experience.
qs: What is the Quoting API?
Which API provides product-level benefit details?

atoms.title: Customer API and single sign-on
atoms.q: What do the Customer API interface and single sign-on provide?
atoms.text: The Customer API interface provides customer-level information such as eligibility rules and demographics. Single sign-on (SSO) allows access to member websites for benefits, claims, wellness, evidence of insurability and more. Both are key enhancements in the UnitedHealthcare Benefit Ecosystem.
qs: What customer information does the Customer API provide?
Does the Benefit Ecosystem support single sign-on?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare Sourcebook for enrollment content
atoms.q: What is the UnitedHealthcare Sourcebook?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare Sourcebook is described as a one-stop resource for enrollment content. It provides grab-and-go content for building a client's benefit administration experience, including direct links to provider directories, education content, ongoing member communications and more, gathered in one place and kept updated.
qs: Where can brokers find enrollment materials for UnitedHealthcare plans?
What is in the UnitedHealthcare Sourcebook?

atoms.title: Strategic alliances and how to get help
atoms.q: How can brokers learn more about Benefit Ecosystem alliances?
atoms.text: Brokers can contact benefit_ecosystem@uhc.com or their UnitedHealthcare representative for more information. The page lists strategic alliance fliers for benefits administration platforms Employee Navigator and ADP, plus Packaged Savings fliers for fully insured 2-99 groups and for PRIME and FACETS 2-99 groups.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare integrate with ADP or Employee Navigator?
Who do I contact about the Benefit Ecosystem?

atoms.title: Care management for chronic conditions
atoms.q: What are UnitedHealthcare care management and clinical programs for?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's care management and clinical programs are built to make decision-making easier and the path to a healthier life smoother for employees who manage a complex or chronic condition. The company says the programs may result in lower medical costs for everyone.
qs: What do care management programs do?
Can care management lower medical costs?

atoms.title: How care management identifies at-risk employees
atoms.q: How do UnitedHealthcare care management programs find employees who need support?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare care management programs use data and analytics to identify at-risk employees and opportunities for better whole-person health across multiple conditions. Support includes proactive outreach, nurses and case managers. Gaps in care are identified using data from medical claims, lab results, pharmacy, biometric screenings, health assessments and more.
qs: What data does UnitedHealthcare use to find care gaps?
Do care management programs use proactive outreach?

atoms.title: Standard Care Coordination for fully insured
atoms.q: What is Standard Care Coordination?
atoms.text: Standard Care Coordination is for UnitedHealthcare fully insured clients. It monitors and addresses 50+ conditions across an employee population for potential gaps in care. For employees identified as at risk, resources include a nurse team to answer questions and offer guidance, admission counselors to help with hospital length-of-stay and discharge planning, and access to condition-specific programs and more.
qs: What does Standard Care Coordination include?
How many conditions does Standard Care Coordination monitor?

atoms.title: Personal Health Support for self-funded
atoms.q: What is Personal Health Support?
atoms.text: Personal Health Support is for UnitedHealthcare self-funded clients. It screens up to 100% of an employer's population for 100+ acute and chronic conditions. Personalized support for at-risk members includes earlier identification of opportunities for better health, digital tools to help monitor conditions and progress, and access to an enhanced clinical team and condition-specific programs.
qs: What conditions does Personal Health Support screen for?
Is Personal Health Support for self-funded plans?

atoms.title: Standard Care Coordination vs Personal Health Support
atoms.q: How do Standard Care Coordination and Personal Health Support differ?
atoms.text: Standard Care Coordination serves fully insured clients and monitors 50+ conditions, with a nurse team, admission counselors and condition-specific programs. Personal Health Support serves self-funded clients and screens up to 100% of the employer's population for 100+ acute and chronic conditions, adding digital monitoring tools and an enhanced clinical team.
qs: Which care management program fits a self-funded employer?
How many conditions does each care program cover?

atoms.title: Condition-specific clinical programs
atoms.q: What are condition-specific clinical programs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare also offers condition-specific clinical programs, which provide focused support for clients whose populations may benefit from more specific condition management resources, such as cancer, kidney, congenital heart disease and more.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare have a cancer or kidney support program?
What are disease-specific clinical programs?

atoms.title: 96% to 97% satisfaction with clinical resources
atoms.q: How satisfied are employees with clinical resources?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare reports 96% to 97% satisfaction with clinical resources, citing 2019 Optum Net Promoter Score data and its book of business Consumer Health Survey (average FY 2020). It adds that disease-specific clinical programs help reduce inpatient admissions.
qs: How satisfied are members with UnitedHealthcare clinical programs?
Do clinical programs reduce hospital admissions?

atoms.title: Up to $14 PMPM savings with Personal Health Support
atoms.q: How much can Personal Health Support save per member per month?
atoms.text: Clients with Personal Health Support see per member per month savings of up to $14 on medical costs, depending on products offered. UnitedHealthcare bases this on 2020 book of business leading indicators and states that actual results will vary.
qs: What savings does Personal Health Support deliver?
How much is the PMPM medical cost reduction?

atoms.title: Support for children and adults with complex needs
atoms.q: What support exists for people with complex care needs?
atoms.text: Support programs for children and adults with complex care needs provide a single point of contact for all aspects of the health care system. This contact helps find specialty providers, maximize benefits, resolve unique insurance issues and more.
qs: Who helps with complex medical needs?
Can a single contact help me find specialty providers?

atoms.title: How UnitedHealthcare medical plans are built
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealthcare's approach to employer medical plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare medical plans are built with tailored network strategies and innovative benefit and plan designs to help meet the care and cost needs of employers and their employees. Plan designs are built for access, supported by the nation's largest proprietary network, and designed to guide employees to evidence-based, cost-efficient care.
qs: What makes UnitedHealthcare employer medical plans different?
Does UnitedHealthcare have a large proprietary network?

atoms.title: Plan designs that encourage health ownership
atoms.q: How do UnitedHealthcare plan designs encourage healthier choices?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare plan designs and popular benefits, such as $0 copays and virtual care access, are built to help promote healthier choices and encourage employees to take steps toward better health. Plans also include tools and resources to help employees understand their plan and navigate the health care system to get care at the right place, at the right time.
qs: Do UnitedHealthcare plans offer $0 copays?
What tools help employees understand their health plan?

atoms.title: Provider collaboration and Naviguard
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare work with providers to control costs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare works with providers through incentives, value-based arrangements and collaborative data sharing to help enable quality, cost-efficient care. Tools and resources like Naviguard aim to protect all parties from egregious billing, to ensure providers are paid quickly for their services and to keep out-of-network charges in check for members.
qs: What is Naviguard?
How does UnitedHealthcare keep out-of-network charges down?

atoms.title: Centers of Excellence shorten transplant stays
atoms.q: What results does UnitedHealthcare report for its Centers of Excellence program?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's Centers of Excellence (COE) program is designed to drive lower costs, fewer complications and shorter recovery times. As an example, the page cites a 22% shorter length of hospital stay for transplant patients compared to the national benchmark, based on a Milliman transplant cost estimate and an Optum book-of-business comparison.
qs: What are Centers of Excellence in health insurance?
How much shorter are hospital stays at Centers of Excellence?

atoms.title: Payment integrity and wasteful spending
atoms.q: How much health care spending is wasteful, and what does payment integrity save?
atoms.text: Experts estimate that 25% of all health care spending is wasteful, according to a 2019 JAMA study cited by UnitedHealthcare. Its payment integrity solutions use strategies such as focused claims reviews to help identify errors and fraud or abuse, which the page says has resulted in $34.86 average savings per member per month (2018 UnitedHealthcare ASO data).
qs: What is payment integrity in health insurance?
How much can payment integrity save per member per month?

atoms.title: Primary care engagement and lower costs
atoms.q: How does primary care engagement affect health care costs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare cites National Health Expenditures data showing that patients who regularly engaged with a primary care provider (PCP) had 10% lower costs than those who did not, and that PCPs can impact 62% of the health care dollar. UnitedHealthcare works with providers on site of care guidance, reducing unnecessary or duplicative testing and cost-effective prescribing.
qs: Do patients with a primary care provider have lower costs?
How much of the health care dollar do PCPs influence?

atoms.title: Range of UnitedHealthcare medical plan options
atoms.q: Which medical plan options does UnitedHealthcare offer employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists a selection of medical plan options: Choice and Choice Plus; UnitedHealthcare Navigate and UnitedHealthcare Charter; Surest; Tiered benefits; NexusACO; UnitedHealthcare FlexWork; UnitedHealthcare Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding; a Preventive Plan; and International benefits. Options range from broad open access networks to more focused access.
qs: What medical plans does UnitedHealthcare offer to employers?
What is NexusACO?

atoms.title: Flexible features in many medical plans
atoms.q: Can UnitedHealthcare medical plans include out-of-network coverage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's medical plan placemat shows options ranging from broad open access networks to more focused access. Many plans have flexible design features that allow for out-of-network coverage and additional savings opportunities for employers and employees. Brokers can use the portfolio tool to design benefit packages for their clients.
qs: Do UnitedHealthcare group plans cover out-of-network care?
Is there a summary of all UnitedHealthcare medical plans for brokers?

atoms.title: Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding
atoms.q: What are Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding plans are designed for more flexibility and simplicity. Because they are based on participants' actual medical claims, plans may get a surplus refund at year-end if claims are lower than expected. Benefits include more savings (exemption from many ACA regulations and state premium taxes), more stability (fixed monthly costs and safeguards against high claims) and more flexibility (plan designs, wellness programs and telemedicine at no additional cost).
qs: What is All Savers Alternate Funding?
What are the benefits of level funded plans?

atoms.title: UnitedHealth Premium designation program
atoms.q: What is the UnitedHealth Premium program?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealth Premium designation program uses evidence-based measures to prioritize high-performing providers. Providers earn blue hearts for consistent delivery of quality care, and only then are they measured on their ability to manage costs efficiently. Designations appear in UnitedHealthcare online physician directories at myuhc.com, are for informational purposes only and should not be the sole basis for choosing a physician.
qs: What do the blue hearts mean on UnitedHealthcare provider listings?
How does UnitedHealthcare choose Premium providers?

atoms.title: Open access network size
atoms.q: How large is UnitedHealthcare's open-access national network?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare open-access plan featured on the medical plans page offers a large national network with more than 1 million doctors and over 6,000 hospitals, based on UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual network statistics ending Q2 2020. The page presents this alongside a flier on UnitedHealthcare Choice Plus.
qs: How many doctors are in UnitedHealthcare's open access network?
Which UnitedHealthcare plan has a large national network?

atoms.title: What UnitedHealthcare Level Funded plans are
atoms.q: What is a level funded health plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Level Funded plans are designed to give employers a different way to balance cost savings with benefits employees want. They offer employers predictability, with the potential of upfront savings and a surplus refund. A fixed monthly rate covers claims and plan administration, much like a fully insured plan.
qs: What does level funded mean?
How is level funded different from fully insured?

atoms.title: Surplus refund potential at year-end
atoms.q: Can a level funded plan get money back?
atoms.text: Level Funded plans are based on the medical and pharmacy claims of plan participants. If those claims are lower than expected, the employer's health plan may get a surplus refund at year-end. The page notes that employers should consult a tax and/or legal advisor about any restrictions or obligations, and that surplus refunds are available only where allowed by law.
qs: Do level funded plans give refunds if claims are low?
When is a level funded surplus refund paid?

atoms.title: Fixed monthly payment protected by stop loss
atoms.q: Do level funded plan costs change month to month?
atoms.text: No. Level Funded plans lock in a fixed monthly payment for the plan year, regardless of actual plan participant medical and pharmacy claims. Stop loss insurance protects employers from unexpected high claims.
qs: Is the monthly cost fixed on a level funded plan?
What protects a level funded employer from big claims?

atoms.title: Two kinds of stop loss insurance
atoms.q: What are individual and aggregate stop loss insurance?
atoms.text: A level-funded plan includes two kinds of stop loss insurance. Individual stop loss protects the plan if claims costs are higher than expected for a particular plan participant. Aggregate stop loss protects the plan if claims costs are higher than expected across the entire group. Stop loss pays covered medical and pharmacy claims costs above expected levels.
qs: What is aggregate stop loss?
What is the difference between individual and aggregate stop loss?

atoms.title: Level funded surplus applies to next year
atoms.q: What happens to savings if claims are low on a level funded plan?
atoms.text: In a level funded plan, if medical and pharmacy claims costs are lower than expected at the end of the plan year, the savings do not stay with the insurance company as they do with a fully insured plan. Instead, the plan earns a surplus refund that the employer can apply to the following year's plan, where allowed by law.
qs: Who keeps savings in level funded vs fully insured?
Can a surplus refund be applied to next year's plan?

atoms.title: ACA exemptions in level funded plans
atoms.q: How do level funded plans affect ACA compliance and taxes?
atoms.text: Because Level Funded plans are a type of self-funded plan, employers may be exempt from many state premium taxes and Affordable Care Act (ACA) regulations, including adjusted community rating. UnitedHealthcare lists exemption from many ACA regulations, lower state premium taxes, potential savings and more flexibility as advantages.
qs: Are level funded plans exempt from ACA rules?
Do level funded plans pay state premium taxes?

atoms.title: Plan designs and networks for level funded
atoms.q: What plan designs and networks are available with Level Funded?
atoms.text: Employers can customize a Level Funded benefits package from dozens of plan designs, networks and specialty options. Portfolios include HSA, PPO and EPO plans, with network options such as the nation's largest proprietary network of 1.7M physicians and health care professionals and 7,000+ hospitals (UnitedHealthcare internal analysis, June 30, 2023).
qs: Can level funded plans include an HSA plan?
How large is the Level Funded provider network?

atoms.title: Wellness, reporting and bundling with level funded
atoms.q: What extras come with UnitedHealthcare Level Funded?
atoms.text: Level Funded plans include wellness programs and services designed to help plan participants get healthier at no additional cost. Employers also get up-to-date reporting on claims costs and network utilization, plus digital tools to help simplify plan management. They may also save when bundling a UnitedHealthcare specialty plan, like vision and dental, with a medical plan.
qs: Do level funded plans include wellness programs?
Can I bundle dental and vision with level funded medical?

atoms.title: Level funded gaining popularity with small businesses
atoms.q: Are level funded plans common among small businesses?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's video states that level-funded health plans have grown in popularity among small businesses nationwide, citing the Kaiser Family Foundation Employer Health Benefits Surveys of 2019 and 2024, which define a small business as a group with 3-199 employees. UnitedHealthcare offers separate Level Funded fliers for groups of 2-50 and for groups of 51+.
qs: Why are small businesses choosing level funded plans?
Is there a level funded flier for groups over 50?

atoms.title: Advocacy simplifies health care
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealthcare's advocacy solution for employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare puts advocacy solutions in place that are designed to help lower costs and improve outcomes, and to provide employers and their employees with compassionate support to make health care easier. Its Advocate4Me service connects members with an experienced advocate who can guide them through their health journey.
qs: What is Advocate4Me?
How does UnitedHealthcare help employees navigate health care?

atoms.title: How an Advocate4Me interaction works
atoms.q: What happens when a member contacts an Advocate4Me advocate?
atoms.text: 1) The member reaches out for any reason and connects with an experienced advocate. 2) The advocate sees a snapshot view of the member's health care experience in a dashboard. 3) If the advocate spots an opportunity, they can recommend a care path and resources, such as a wellness program or a clinical program for managing a chronic condition.
qs: What does an Advocate4Me advocate see about a member?
Can an advocate refer me to a clinical program?

atoms.title: Advocate satisfaction and referral results
atoms.q: How satisfied are members with UnitedHealthcare advocates?
atoms.text: According to UnitedHealthcare Advocate4Me performance reporting from 2021, 39% of clinical program enrollees are referred by advocates, and advocates have a 91% overall satisfaction rating. The company notes that results are not guaranteed.
qs: What is the satisfaction rating for UnitedHealthcare advocates?
How many clinical program enrollees come from advocate referrals?

atoms.title: A one-stop resource for health care needs
atoms.q: What kinds of help can advocates provide?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's advocacy solutions are designed as a one-stop resource providing end-to-end support for many health care needs, from behavioral and clinical to pharmaceutical and financial. Advocates can also help with benefits, claims and more.
qs: Can an advocate help with a claims question?
What can UnitedHealthcare advocates help with?

atoms.title: Proactive, personalized member support
atoms.q: How do advocates support members proactively?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare advocates anticipate member needs, help them get the most out of their benefits and connect them to relevant programs that can help manage a condition or improve their lifestyle. They use powerful data and insights and are backed by a coordinated, interdisciplinary team of experts behind the scenes.
qs: Do UnitedHealthcare advocates reach out proactively?
Who is behind a UnitedHealthcare advocate?

atoms.title: Support for families with special needs
atoms.q: What support is available for families of children with specialized needs?
atoms.text: Families with children with specialized needs have access to dedicated and focused 1-on-1 support through UnitedHealthcare advocacy. Advocates work closely with employees who may need additional support. A separate sell sheet covers supporting families of children with special needs.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare offer help for parents of kids with special needs?
What is dedicated 1-on-1 support for complex care?

atoms.title: Advocacy benefits for employers vs employees
atoms.q: How do advocacy solutions benefit employers and employees?
atoms.text: Employers may see fewer employee complaints and issue escalations, lower medical expenses, and increased employee satisfaction and productivity. Employees may get a simplified, proactive and personalized experience, a familiar voice that is easy to connect with, the ability to make more informed decisions throughout a health journey, and the opportunity for better health outcomes and lower medical costs.
qs: What do employers gain from offering advocacy services?
What do employees get from an advocate?

atoms.title: Single point of contact for complex care
atoms.q: What does support for complex care provide?
atoms.text: Support for families with complex care needs provides access to a single point of contact connected to aspects of the health care system. This contact helps find specialty providers, maximize benefits, resolve unique insurance issues and more.
qs: Who can help me find a specialist and sort out insurance issues?
What is a single point of contact for complex care?

atoms.title: Advocate services are not for emergencies
atoms.q: Can Advocate4Me be used for emergencies?
atoms.text: No. UnitedHealthcare states that advocate services should not be used for emergency or urgent care needs; in an emergency, members should call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room. Wellness nurses, coaches and other representatives cannot diagnose problems or recommend treatment and are not a substitute for a doctor's care. Advocate services are not an insurance program and may be discontinued at any time.
qs: Should I call an advocate in an emergency?
Can an advocate diagnose a health problem?

atoms.title: Digital tools help employees use benefits
atoms.q: What are UnitedHealthcare's digital tools for employees?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's digital tools are designed to help employees better understand and make the most of their benefits, from finding network care to comparing costs to connecting with a provider. The tools adapt to support members when and where they need it, like keeping key plan information always within reach and offering personalized search.
qs: What digital tools does UnitedHealthcare give employees?
How do UnitedHealthcare digital tools help members use benefits?

atoms.title: myuhc.com personalized experience
atoms.q: What does myuhc.com personalize for members?
atoms.text: myuhc.com delivers a personalized experience for members, including recommendations for programs or health actions, as well as plan- and geographic-specific provider search and coverage information.
qs: What is personalized on myuhc.com?
Does myuhc.com tailor provider search to my plan?

atoms.title: Plan information in one place on myuhc.com
atoms.q: What plan information can employees see on myuhc.com?
atoms.text: Through myuhc.com, employees can access plan and benefits information, HSA, HRA and FSA financial accounts, prescription information and more, all in one place.
qs: Can I see my HSA on myuhc.com?
What can employees do on myuhc.com?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare app 24/7 access for employees
atoms.q: What can employees access in the UnitedHealthcare app?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare app gives employees 24/7 access to health plan information. Employees can see care, cost, claims and pharmacy information, and even a digital version of their health plan ID card.
qs: What is in the UnitedHealthcare app for employees?
Does the app include a digital ID card?

atoms.title: Video chat with a doctor from the app
atoms.q: Can employees video chat with a doctor from the UnitedHealthcare app?
atoms.text: Employees can start a video chat with a doctor right from the UnitedHealthcare app in a few simple clicks, connecting with a provider 24/7.
qs: Can I see a doctor by video in the UnitedHealthcare app?
Is virtual care available 24/7 through the app?

atoms.title: Provider search prioritizes quality and alerts out-of-network
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare's personalized search guide members to providers?
atoms.text: Per the digital experience video, personalized search prioritizes quality network providers while making sure the least invasive care paths are suggested first and alerting members if they veer out of network. The goal is to connect the member with the right provider faster, in person or virtually.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare warn members when a provider is out of network?
How does UnitedHealthcare's search suggest care?

atoms.title: 29% higher satisfaction with myuhc.com
atoms.q: How satisfied are members with myuhc.com?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare video states 29% higher satisfaction with myuhc.com, sourced to the UnitedHealthcare New Member Survey, 2019. The video says the digital tools are designed to provide the same quality guidance that UnitedHealthcare advocates provide.
qs: How much higher is satisfaction with myuhc.com?
Do members prefer digital tools to calling an advocate?

atoms.title: Americans check smartphones 52 times a day
atoms.q: Why does UnitedHealthcare emphasize mobile health engagement?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare cites that Americans check their smartphones an average of 52 times a day, which it describes as dozens of opportunities to help engage employees with their health. The figure comes from the 2018 Global Mobile Consumer Survey, U.S. Edition, by Deloitte.
qs: How often do Americans check their phones?
Why does a health plan use a mobile app?

atoms.title: Broker and employer materials on digital tools
atoms.q: What materials can brokers share with clients about digital tools?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers three PDF resources for brokers to share with clients: a brochure on innovation and insights, a brochure on myuhc.com details for employees that outlines benefits for employee engagement, and a benefit breakdown of employer-based digital tools that gives a snapshot of the information employees can access.
qs: Where can brokers find UnitedHealthcare digital tool brochures?
Is there a flier explaining why employees should register for myuhc.com?

atoms.title: Growing demand for virtual care
atoms.q: How much demand is there for virtual care among consumers and employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare cites a 2021 survey in which nearly 90% of Americans said they wanted to continue using virtual care for non-urgent health needs. It also cites the Business Group on Health 2023 survey: 57% of employers were looking to add even more virtual health solutions in 2023, and 74% believe virtual health will have a significant impact on how care is delivered in the future.
qs: Do employers plan to add more virtual health benefits?
What share of Americans want to keep using telehealth?

atoms.title: Virtual primary care growth
atoms.q: How fast are virtual primary care offerings growing among employers?
atoms.text: Anticipated employer offerings of virtual primary care are expected to grow from 32% in 2022 to 69% in 2025, according to the Business Group on Health 2023 survey cited by UnitedHealthcare. The company says it is ahead of the curve, with virtual primary care available in most open access plans.
qs: Is virtual primary care included in UnitedHealthcare open access plans?
How common is virtual primary care in employer plans?

atoms.title: Three commitments behind virtual health
atoms.q: What commitments guide UnitedHealthcare's virtual health offerings?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says its virtual health solutions support three commitments. They help people navigate a fragmented system, since members can find virtual care via myuhc.com, the UnitedHealthcare app or an advocate. They enhance benefits through internal and external collaboration. They also help reduce total cost of care, since virtual care is often less expensive than in-person care.
qs: How do members find virtual care with UnitedHealthcare?
Is virtual care cheaper than in-person care?

atoms.title: Virtual urgent and primary care offerings
atoms.q: What virtual urgent and primary care options does UnitedHealthcare offer?
atoms.text: For some of employees' most common needs, from urgent care to wellness exams, UnitedHealthcare offers virtual primary care to build the patient-provider relationship virtually, 24/7 Virtual Visits for care when and where it is needed, and virtual specialists curated for employers' clients.
qs: What are 24/7 Virtual Visits?
Can employees see a specialist virtually?

atoms.title: Virtual behavioral health solutions
atoms.q: What virtual behavioral health services are available through UnitedHealthcare?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's virtual behavioral health solutions are designed to make care more accessible across a continuum of needs. They include virtual visits for behavioral health care, an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) available around the clock, an Emotional Health Line, virtual behavioral therapy and coaching, and an on-demand self-help app.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare offer virtual therapy and coaching?
What is the Emotional Health Line?

atoms.title: Dentist Virtual Visits through DialCare
atoms.q: What do Dentist Virtual Visits from DialCare Teledentistry include?
atoms.text: Dentist Virtual Visits from DialCare Teledentistry let employees connect with a licensed dentist anytime, anywhere. Benefits include two virtual visits per year at no cost-share and 24/7 access to consultations for nonemergency dental conditions, second opinions, treatment options and clinically necessary prescriptions from state-licensed, fully credentialed dentists. Dentist virtual visits are currently unavailable in Maine or Texas.
qs: How many virtual dentist visits are free per year?
Is teledentistry available in Texas?

atoms.title: Condition-specific virtual care and monitoring
atoms.q: What condition-specific virtual care does UnitedHealthcare offer?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare describes advanced digital therapeutics that give employees new ways to get and stay healthier. They include Level2 Specialty Care, remote monitoring solutions for chronic conditions and at-home screening kits through Health Screening Solutions.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare offer remote monitoring for chronic conditions?
What at-home screening kits are available?

atoms.title: 24/7 Virtual Visits network and limits
atoms.q: What are the limits of 24/7 Virtual Visits?
atoms.text: 24/7 Virtual Visits are delivered by a Designated Virtual Network Provider via video, or audio-only where permitted by state law. Unless otherwise required, benefits are available only when services are delivered through a Designated Virtual Network Provider. The service is not intended for emergency or life-threatening conditions, and may not be available at all times, in all locations or for all members.
qs: Can I use 24/7 Virtual Visits for an emergency?
Do virtual visits have to be with a designated network provider?

atoms.title: Virtual primary care licensing and limits
atoms.q: What restrictions apply to virtual primary care?
atoms.text: Virtual primary care is provided by a provider via video, chat, email or audio-only where permitted under state law. Services are available only if the provider is licensed in the state where the member is located at the time of the appointment. It is not intended for emergency or life-threatening conditions, and certain prescriptions may not be available.
qs: Can a virtual primary care doctor see me while I'm traveling?
Can all prescriptions be written in a virtual visit?

atoms.title: EAP scope and confidentiality
atoms.q: What can an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) do and not do?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that EAP material is for informational purposes only. EAP staff cannot diagnose problems or suggest treatment, and the EAP is not a substitute for a doctor's care. Health information is kept confidential in accordance with the law. The EAP is not an insurance program and may be discontinued at any time, and legal consultation is not provided for issues that may involve legal action against UnitedHealthcare or its affiliates.
qs: Is EAP counseling confidential?
Can an EAP diagnose a condition?

atoms.title: Virtual health guided by human insights
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealthcare's philosophy on virtual health?
atoms.text: In its video on virtual health, UnitedHealthcare says unlocking the potential of virtual health requires human insight, not only new platforms and technology. From virtual visits to remote monitoring and digital tools, it aims to connect people to care that is affordable, supportive and simple to access, saying its approach does not replace the human element but amplifies it.
qs: How does UnitedHealthcare approach virtual health?
Does virtual health replace human care?

atoms.title: Pharmacy benefits aim to lower costs
atoms.q: What do UnitedHealthcare pharmacy benefits aim to do for employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare pharmacy benefits are designed to make medications more affordable and accessible. The company describes them as critical to lowering costs for employers and improving health outcomes for their employees.
qs: What are UnitedHealthcare employer pharmacy benefits for?
How do pharmacy benefits lower employer costs?

atoms.title: Lowering drug costs for employees and families
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare help lower prescription costs for employees?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare works to make prescription drugs more affordable and increase adherence through streamlined prior authorizations, digital pricing tools and strategic Prescription Drug List (PDL) design. These approaches are aimed at lowering costs for employees and their families.
qs: What is a Prescription Drug List?
How does UnitedHealthcare make prescriptions cheaper for employees?

atoms.title: Decision support at the point of care
atoms.q: What decision support does UnitedHealthcare give providers and pharmacists?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare provides critical decision support to providers and pharmacists at the point of care. The goal is to help lower costs and ensure that the right drugs are used in a patient's care plan.
qs: How does UnitedHealthcare support prescribers at the point of care?
What is point-of-care decision support for drugs?

atoms.title: Common medical and pharmacy data platform
atoms.q: Why does UnitedHealthcare use a common medical and pharmacy data platform?
atoms.text: A common medical and pharmacy data platform is designed to deliver a simpler plan experience for clients and to lower their costs on both the pharmacy and medical side. UnitedHealthcare and Optum Rx partner to provide integrated carve-in medical and pharmacy solutions.
qs: What does integrated medical and pharmacy mean?
What is a carve-in pharmacy benefit?

atoms.title: PreCheck MyScript saves $111 per script
atoms.q: What is PreCheck MyScript and how much does it save?
atoms.text: PreCheck MyScript is designed to make it easier for physicians to access each patient's specific PDL and cost information, identify lower cost alternatives and see any prior authorization requirements. UnitedHealthcare says it saves members an average of $111 per script, based on an Optum Rx analysis of full-year 2021 trial claim and production claim data.
qs: What is PreCheck MyScript?
How much does PreCheck MyScript save per prescription?

atoms.title: Savings on specialty infusions
atoms.q: How does UnitedHealthcare manage high-cost specialty medications?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare uses site of care redirection and specialty virtual visits to help employees better understand their medications. When infusions are shifted to a nonhospital setting, it reports 30% to 50% savings per infusion, based on an Optum Specialty Pharmacy 2018 internal analysis.
qs: What is site of care redirection?
How much can nonhospital infusion save?

atoms.title: Opioid prescription results
atoms.q: What results has UnitedHealthcare reported on opioid prescribing?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare describes a multi-dimensional approach to the opioid epidemic. It reports 94% compliance with first-fill opioid scripts with a 7-day or fewer supply and a 48% reduction in total opioid prescriptions, citing UnitedHealthcare data from April 2023.
qs: How is UnitedHealthcare addressing opioid prescriptions?
What percent of first-fill opioid scripts are 7 days or fewer?

atoms.title: PDL management and medication sourcing strategy
atoms.q: What pharmacy strategies does UnitedHealthcare use to improve outcomes?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's strategic approach to PDL management, site of care redirection, medication sourcing and more helps deliver pharmacy benefits built to lower costs, streamline experiences and improve adherence. Its integrated approach is also described in a brochure on the power of an integrated pharmacy solution.
qs: How does UnitedHealthcare manage pharmacy costs for employers?
Where can brokers get information on integrated pharmacy?

atoms.title: Dental coverage may help lower medical costs
atoms.q: Why offer a dental plan alongside medical coverage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says that because improving oral health may impact overall health, a dental plan may help lower employers' medical costs as well. Employers of all sizes can choose from a variety of dental plan designs, bundled with a UnitedHealthcare medical plan or standalone.
qs: Can dental coverage lower medical costs?
Can an employer buy dental separately from medical?

atoms.title: Dental plan design choices
atoms.q: What dental plan types does UnitedHealthcare offer employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers dental plan designs including PPO, Exclusive Network and Value plans. They can be bundled with a UnitedHealthcare medical plan or purchased standalone, and are available to employers of all sizes.
qs: What types of dental plans can an employer choose?
Does UnitedHealthcare have a PPO dental plan for employers?

atoms.title: Preventive care and pregnancy dental benefits
atoms.q: What oral health benefits do UnitedHealthcare dental plans include?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare dental benefits include 100% coverage for preventive care, plus additional cleanings and nonsurgical gum treatments during and 3 months after pregnancy. Integrated health management strategies are designed to help employees return to preventive or periodontal care. The page notes this applies when preventive or periodontal care is completed after contact from UnitedHealthcare.
qs: Are extra dental cleanings covered during pregnancy?
Is preventive dental care covered at 100%?

atoms.title: Provider choice and teledentistry access
atoms.q: What dental provider network do employees get?
atoms.text: Employees can choose from a national, quality provider network designed to meet their care needs, including general and pediatric dentistry, orthodontia, periodontal, endodontic or oral surgery. It also includes 24/7 teledentistry for urgent needs.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare dental include orthodontia providers?
Is there 24/7 dental care access?

atoms.title: Digital Dental Assistant app
atoms.q: What does the UnitedHealthcare Digital Dental Assistant app do?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's Digital Dental Assistant app is part of its digital dental support for employer groups. The app helps make it easier for employees to find a dentist, schedule appointment reminders, get health tips and more.
qs: How do I find a dentist with UnitedHealthcare dental?
Is there an app for UnitedHealthcare dental plans?

atoms.title: Jet Dental pop-up clinics and DialCare
atoms.q: What are Jet Dental pop-up clinics and DialCare teledentistry?
atoms.text: Jet Dental provides onsite cleanings and exams at an employer's worksite through pop-up clinics. DialCare teledentistry provides 24/7 advice, follow-up care, second opinion and prescription services when medically necessary. UnitedHealthcare says these services help make it easier for employees to get dental care anytime, anywhere.
qs: Can dental cleanings happen at the workplace?
What does DialCare teledentistry offer?

atoms.title: PPO/open access vs In-Network Only dental
atoms.q: How do UnitedHealthcare PPO/open access and In-Network Only dental plans differ?
atoms.text: PPO/open access plans are available nationally for fully insured groups of 2 or more, with self-funded options for larger groups, a national network with a 38% average network discount, 100% in-network preventive care and out-of-network coverage available. In-Network Only plans (31 states) offer a 36% average network discount and in-network coverage only. Neither requires a primary care dentist or specialist referral.
qs: What is the network discount on a UnitedHealthcare dental PPO?
Does an in-network only dental plan cover out-of-network care?

atoms.title: Exclusive Network dental plans
atoms.q: What are UnitedHealthcare Exclusive Network dental plans?
atoms.text: Exclusive Network plans are available in 9 states for fully insured groups of 2 or more. They are for employers who want to simplify the dental care experience with the benefits of a DHMO plan but without the typical pain points. They offer 100% in-network preventive care, in-network coverage only, no deductible, no annual maximum and no waiting periods.
qs: Do any dental plans have no annual maximum?
What is an Exclusive Network dental plan?

atoms.title: Value dental plans and discounts
atoms.q: What is a UnitedHealthcare Value dental plan?
atoms.text: Value dental plans are available in 19 states and offer a national network with a 34% average network discount. They include 100% preventive care and diagnostics in network, and out-of-network coverage is available. Discounts of 20% to 50% apply to services such as fillings, crowns, whitening and orthodontia; the page notes these discounts are not insurance and members pay for services directly.
qs: Are Value dental plan discounts insurance?
What discounts does a UnitedHealthcare Value dental plan give?

atoms.title: Eye exams and overall health
atoms.q: Why do vision benefits matter for overall health?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare cites research that employees are 4 times more likely to visit their eye care provider than their primary care provider. Conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure, and even some kinds of cancer, may be first discovered in a routine eye exam. A quality vision plan may help employees get and stay healthier, with the goal of lowering costs for everyone.
qs: Can an eye exam detect diabetes or high blood pressure?
Why should employers offer vision coverage?

atoms.title: Broad vision network and retailers
atoms.q: Which eye care providers are in the UnitedHealthcare Vision network?
atoms.text: Employees get an array of eye care choices, including private practices, online options and popular retailers such as Warby Parker, GlassesUSA, Costco, Sam's Club, America's Best, Walmart, Target and LensCrafters.
qs: Can I use UnitedHealthcare Vision at Costco or Warby Parker?
Does UnitedHealthcare Vision include online glasses retailers?

atoms.title: Maternity and pediatric vision benefits
atoms.q: What additional vision benefits apply during pregnancy and childhood?
atoms.text: Because vision may change frequently during pregnancy and childhood, UnitedHealthcare vision plans include additional maternity and pediatric benefits. These include coverage for a second eye exam per plan year and new glasses if vision changes reach a certain threshold in a plan year.
qs: Does vision insurance cover a second eye exam during pregnancy?
Are new glasses covered if a child's vision changes?

atoms.title: Discounts on frames, lenses and contacts
atoms.q: What discounts do UnitedHealthcare Vision members get?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Vision plans give employees savings of 20% to 60% off retail frames and lenses. In addition to those savings, employees may also qualify for discounted contact lenses and laser vision correction.
qs: How much off frames and lenses do vision plan members get?
Is laser vision correction discounted?

atoms.title: Bundling vision to lower overall costs
atoms.q: How can employers lower costs by bundling vision with other plans?
atoms.text: Fully insured employers with group sizes between 2 and 100 may see additional savings when they offer UnitedHealthcare Vision alongside their UnitedHealthcare medical and/or other specialty plans through the uBundle and Packaged Savings programs. Employers should reach out to their UnitedHealthcare representative for more details.
qs: What is uBundle?
Can I save by bundling vision with medical?

atoms.title: uBundle vs Packaged Savings
atoms.q: How do uBundle and Packaged Savings compare?
atoms.text: uBundle serves groups averaging 51 to 100 employees underwritten by Small Business underwriting and may save up to 3.5% of medical premiums in the first year. Packaged Savings serves 2 to 99 eligible employees and provides administrative credits of up to $7 per employee per month. Both require fully insured customers who offer a UnitedHealthcare medical plan with eligible specialty plans, and availability varies by state.
qs: What group sizes qualify for Packaged Savings?
What is the maximum savings for uBundle?

atoms.title: Eligible specialty plans for savings programs
atoms.q: Which specialty plans qualify for uBundle and Packaged Savings?
atoms.text: For uBundle, eligible specialty plans are dental, vision and financial protection products: Basic Life, Supplemental Life, Short-term Disability, Long-term Disability and Supplemental Health Plans (Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity). For Packaged Savings, eligible plans are dental, vision and financial protection limited to Basic Life and Short-term Disability.
qs: Which life and disability plans count toward Packaged Savings?
Does hospital indemnity qualify for uBundle?

atoms.title: State and carrier exclusions for savings programs
atoms.q: Where are uBundle and Packaged Savings not available?
atoms.text: uBundle is not available in CA, CO, HI, NY, RI or VT. Packaged Savings is not available in NY, RI or WA. For both programs, business underwritten or administered by Oxford Health Plans and Sierra Health Services Inc. is excluded. Minimum participation requirements may apply, and programs may not be available in all states or for all group sizes.
qs: Is uBundle available in California?
Is Packaged Savings offered in Washington?

atoms.title: Online tools for managing vision benefits
atoms.q: Where can employees manage their UnitedHealthcare vision benefits?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers online tools and resources through myuhcvision.com, described as a one-stop shop where employees can manage their vision benefits. Brokers can also share a vision benefits overview brochure and a report on screen time and children's health with their clients.
qs: Where do I log in to manage my UnitedHealthcare vision plan?
Is there a report on screen time and kids' eyes?

atoms.title: Wellness programs for whole-person well-being
atoms.q: What do UnitedHealthcare wellness programs cover?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare describes its wellness programs and services as a diverse set of solutions that support an individual's overall well-being, not just physical health. The company states they are proven to improve member health and lower costs.
qs: What wellness programs does UnitedHealthcare offer employers?
Do wellness programs lower health costs?

atoms.title: Real Appeal weight loss program
atoms.q: What is Real Appeal?
atoms.text: Real Appeal is a UnitedHealthcare weight loss program that delivers better health opportunities to members' doorsteps, including a complimentary kit of weight loss resources and online coaching. UnitedHealthcare reports it has helped more than 900,000 participants, with an average of 3.4% body weight loss per person.
qs: What does Real Appeal include?
How much weight do Real Appeal participants lose on average?

atoms.title: 88% lost weight with Real Appeal
atoms.q: What percentage of Real Appeal participants lost weight?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare reports that 88% lost weight with Real Appeal. The figure comes from its book of business through May 2022 and a cohort of participants at risk who were in the program 26+ weeks and attended 9+ ILIs (N > 50,000).
qs: How effective is Real Appeal?
What does 88% weight loss with Real Appeal mean?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare Rewards incentive program
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealthcare Rewards?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Rewards is an incentive program that rewards employees with dollars for tracking steps or sleep, getting an annual checkup and more. Employees choose their activities as well as how to spend their earnings. The company reports that 94% of first-time participants earned a reward and 70% have paired a device to engage in weekly and daily challenges (UHC Rewards book of business, 2023).
qs: How do employees earn UnitedHealthcare Rewards?
What percent of first-time Rewards users earn a reward?

atoms.title: One Pass Select fitness benefit
atoms.q: What is One Pass Select?
atoms.text: One Pass Select is a subscription-based program that helps employees prioritize health and wellness through a low-cost, extensive nationwide gym network and digital fitness offerings. UnitedHealthcare reports 76% engagement and an average 20% savings on retail gym memberships.
qs: What is One Pass Select?
How much does One Pass Select save on gym memberships?

atoms.title: Quit For Life tobacco cessation program
atoms.q: What is Quit For Life?
atoms.text: Quit For Life is a clinically proven tobacco cessation program that gives participants a personal action plan, confidential coaching and other resources to help them quit tobacco. UnitedHealthcare reports that 50% quit tobacco, and that over 30+ years the program has helped more than 6 million participants, with 93% participant satisfaction.
qs: How does Quit For Life help people stop smoking?
What is the quit rate for Quit For Life?

atoms.title: How Quit For Life defines quit success
atoms.q: How is quit-rate success measured in Quit For Life?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's Quit For Life results are measured among responders to a survey at 6 months post-program enrollment, with quit-rate success defined as 30+ days of abstinence from all forms of tobacco. The figures use employer book-of-business cumulative results from 2006 through Q1 2024.
qs: What counts as quitting in the Quit For Life program?
When is Quit For Life success measured?

atoms.title: Employee Assistance Program support
atoms.q: What does the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offer?
atoms.text: The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is designed for support when employees and their families are feeling anxious and do not know where to turn. A no-cost call connects them to an EAP specialist who will listen to their concerns and refer them to expert care and resources if needed.
qs: Is the EAP free for employees?
Who answers an EAP call?

atoms.title: Boosting wellness benefit engagement
atoms.q: Why do in-demand wellness benefits see low engagement?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare notes that in-demand wellness benefits are seeing low engagement and says employers play a vital role in getting employees to use their benefits. It says encouraging engagement through education and incentives is a win-win for all, and links to an article on how employers can boost wellness benefit engagement.
qs: How can employers get employees to use wellness benefits?
Why is wellness program engagement low?

atoms.title: Employer medical costs projected to rise 8.5%
atoms.q: How much are employer medical costs projected to increase in 2026?
atoms.text: Employer medical costs are projected to increase 8.5% in 2026, driven by regulatory changes, an aging workforce and rising chronic conditions. Specialty drug usage, catastrophic claims and behavioral health needs further contribute to higher expenses. UnitedHealthcare says employers should consider a strategic, comprehensive cost management approach to reduce health care spending while maintaining benefit quality.
qs: How much will employer health costs rise in 2026?
What is driving employer health care cost increases?

atoms.title: Strategic approach to cost management
atoms.q: What does UnitedHealthcare's cost management approach include?
atoms.text: A strategic approach to cost management can help employers address economic challenges and rising health care expenses. UnitedHealthcare's approach includes health plan designs that provide upfront cost information, encourage cost-effective care and reduce out-of-pocket costs, and it focuses on protecting employers' financial goals while meeting employees' health needs and budgets.
qs: How can employers reduce health care spending?
What plan designs lower out-of-pocket costs?

atoms.title: Surest shows copays before care
atoms.q: How does the Surest plan help control costs?
atoms.text: The Surest plan allows members to view and compare copays in advance without worrying about deductibles and coinsurance. UnitedHealthcare says this helps members choose low-cost, high-value options and delivers savings for employers and employees.
qs: Can members see copays before they get care with Surest?
Does Surest have deductibles or coinsurance?

atoms.title: Broad networks and chronic condition management
atoms.q: How do networks and chronic condition programs affect employer costs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare plans include broad national networks of health care providers and facilities recognized for delivering high-value care. The page also says effective prevention and management of chronic conditions through clinical and care management programs is important, because chronic conditions account for significant portions of employers' total health care spending.
qs: Why do chronic conditions drive employer health costs?
How do provider networks help control costs?

atoms.title: About 25% of spending is wasteful
atoms.q: How much health care spending is wasteful or unnecessary?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that approximately 25% of health care spending is considered wasteful or unnecessary. Payment integrity solutions help ensure employers and employees pay only for care and services rendered. The company says it uses a strategic approach delivering lower total cost of care compared to market competitors.
qs: What percent of health care spending is wasteful?
What is payment integrity?

atoms.title: Funding models and network configurations
atoms.q: What funding types and networks does UnitedHealthcare offer for cost management?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says that understanding and recommending the right medical plan and network configuration helps clients maximize health insurance value at the lowest possible cost. It offers fully insured, level funded and self-funded medical plans with various network configurations meeting most employer needs.
qs: What funding options does UnitedHealthcare offer employers?
How do I choose the right network for a client?

atoms.title: Care and clinical management lower costs
atoms.q: How do care and clinical management programs lower costs?
atoms.text: Complex and chronic conditions and their accompanying costs call for clinical and care management programs that help employees navigate their care journey. UnitedHealthcare says targeted programs deliver more efficient and cost-effective care, improve health outcomes and ultimately reduce costs.
qs: Do clinical programs reduce employer health costs?
Why do complex conditions need care management?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare pays 98% of claims received
atoms.q: What percent of claims does UnitedHealthcare pay?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare pays 98% of all claims received for eligible members when claims are submitted timely, contain complete and accurate information and are not duplicate submissions. Payment integrity solutions resolve claims issues before members pay, potentially saving money for employers and employees.
qs: How many claims does UnitedHealthcare pay?
What conditions must a claim meet to be paid?

atoms.title: What whole-person health means
atoms.q: What is a whole-person approach to employee health benefits?
atoms.text: Focusing only on the medical side of an employee's health does not offer a complete picture. A whole-person approach addresses an individual's physical, mental, financial and overall health and well-being needs. UnitedHealthcare says it has the breadth of products and solutions to help ensure an employer's benefits strategy addresses all the factors that may influence employee health and well-being.
qs: What does whole-person health mean?
Why do employers take a whole-person approach to benefits?

atoms.title: Employees see well-being as connected
atoms.q: Do employees see physical and mental well-being as connected?
atoms.text: According to the survey cited in UnitedHealthcare's whole-person health video, 95% of surveyed employees said physical, mental, emotional and social well-being are all connected. By addressing pharmacy, financial and behavioral health needs and more, UnitedHealthcare says employers can take a holistic approach that may lead to a healthier, more productive workforce and significant cost savings.
qs: What share of employees say mental and physical health are connected?
Can whole-person benefits improve productivity?

atoms.title: Medical and pharmacy rank as top benefits
atoms.q: Which benefits do employers rank as most important?
atoms.text: Surveyed employers rank medical benefits as the No. 1 most important benefit to offer employees and pharmacy benefits as No. 2, according to UnitedHealthcare Whole-Person Health Research conducted between February 20, 2024 and April 25, 2024. UnitedHealthcare says it offers a variety of medical plans and targeted clinical programs that treat the whole person, not just the condition at hand.
qs: What do employers consider the most important benefit?
How important is pharmacy coverage to employers?

atoms.title: Integrated medical and pharmacy benefits
atoms.q: Why manage medical and pharmacy benefits together?
atoms.text: Around 55% of an employer's total drug spend applies to specialty medications, and many drugs are covered under both benefits. In an integrated model, UnitedHealthcare reviews medical and pharmacy claims to better advocate for employees on when to use their medical benefit and when to use their pharmacy benefit. When managed together, care can be more coordinated, with better outcomes, lower costs and simpler experiences.
qs: What share of drug spend is specialty medication?
How does integrating medical and pharmacy lower costs?

atoms.title: Mental health conditions affect employees and productivity
atoms.q: How common are mental health disorders among working-age adults?
atoms.text: Approximately 15% of working-age adults currently live with a mental health disorder, and depression and anxiety alone drain $1T from the global economy annually through lost productivity, according to the World Health Organization. UnitedHealthcare says behavioral health benefits can help ensure employees and their families have access to mental health support, with a guided experience to find needed care.
qs: What percent of working adults have a mental health disorder?
How much do depression and anxiety cost the economy?

atoms.title: Dental, vision and hearing are essential benefits
atoms.q: Are dental, vision and hearing benefits essential?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says dental, vision and hearing benefits are not extras but essential benefits, because a person's mouth, eyes and ears often serve as indicators of overall health and well-being. It says specialty benefits may help detect early signs of serious conditions and reduce long-term costs.
qs: Why should employers offer dental, vision and hearing coverage?
Can dental and vision exams detect serious conditions?

atoms.title: Financial stress and employee well-being
atoms.q: How does financial stress affect employees at work?
atoms.text: Personal financial concerns can affect employees' mental health, productivity and focus at work. U.S. employees spend more than 8 hours a week managing personal finances, and half of that occurs during work hours, according to Harvard Business Review. UnitedHealthcare offers integrated solutions such as flexible spending accounts and financial protection benefits to help employees manage financial health.
qs: How much time do employees spend on personal finances at work?
Can an FSA improve employee financial wellness?

atoms.title: Wellness programs and fewer sick days
atoms.q: Do wellness programs reduce sick days?
atoms.text: Making healthier lifestyle choices may help reduce the likelihood of developing a chronic illness while also improving quality of life. UnitedHealthcare cites a Wellhub study stating that 89% said employees take fewer sick days as a result of their well-being program. UnitedHealthcare says it has wellness programs designed to foster healthier, more productive workforces.
qs: Do employee well-being programs reduce absenteeism?
What percent of employers say wellness programs reduce sick days?

atoms.title: What Medicaid is
atoms.q: What is Medicaid?
atoms.text: Medicaid is a program that helps adults with low income. It also can help children, pregnant women, older adults and people with disabilities who need medical care. UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offers low-cost or no-cost Medicaid plans, and people can search for Medicaid plans by state.
qs: What is Medicaid?
Who does Medicaid help?
Does UnitedHealthcare offer Medicaid plans?

atoms.title: Dual Special Needs plans (D-SNP) overview
atoms.q: What is a Dual Special Needs plan?
atoms.text: If you have both Medicare and Medicaid, a Dual Special Needs plan (D-SNP) might be right for you. D-SNPs give you extra benefits like dental, vision care and more at little to no extra cost. These plans are available in some states. With a D-SNP, you could get more benefits and features than with Original Medicare.
qs: What is a D-SNP?
What plan do I get if I have both Medicare and Medicaid?
Do dual plans offer dental and vision?

atoms.title: New Medicaid renewal rules start in 2027
atoms.q: Are Medicaid renewal requirements changing in 2027?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan tells members to stay up to date on new Medicaid renewal requirements. Starting in 2027, some adults may be required to renew Medicaid coverage 2 times per year and meet work requirements. Members are directed to a page that explains what steps they may need to take to keep their coverage.
qs: Do I have to renew Medicaid twice a year?
What changes for Medicaid in 2027?
Will I need to meet work requirements for Medicaid?

atoms.title: Medicaid, D-SNP, ACA and CHIP compared
atoms.q: What is the difference between Medicaid, D-SNP, ACA Marketplace plans and CHIP?
atoms.text: Medicaid provides health insurance for some low-income people, children, pregnant women, the elderly and people with disabilities. A D-SNP is for people eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid. ACA Marketplace plans are for people who buy their own health insurance for themselves and their families. CHIP offers low-cost or no-cost coverage for infants, children and teens who don't have health insurance.
qs: What types of plans does UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offer?
Should I get Medicaid, CHIP or an ACA plan?
Which plan is for people with both Medicare and Medicaid?

atoms.title: What CHIP is
atoms.q: What is the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP)?
atoms.text: Kids need regular checkups and medical care. If an infant, child or teen doesn't have health insurance, the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) offers low-cost or no-cost coverage. UnitedHealthcare Community Plan links to a dedicated CHIP page for parents and guardians who want to learn more.
qs: What is CHIP?
How can I get health insurance for my child?
Is there low-cost coverage for kids?

atoms.title: ACA Marketplace plans for self-purchased coverage
atoms.q: Where do I go if I buy my own health insurance?
atoms.text: If you buy your own health insurance for you and your family, the health care Marketplace is for you. The Marketplace is where ACA health plans are sold. UnitedHealthcare offers Individual & Family plans in 23 states, according to the Community Plan page.
qs: What is the health insurance Marketplace?
In how many states does UnitedHealthcare offer ACA plans?
Where are ACA health plans sold?

atoms.title: Medicaid eligibility is set by each state
atoms.q: Does Medicaid eligibility depend on where I live?
atoms.text: Medicaid typically covers children, pregnant women, elderly adults and people with disabilities and eligible low-income adults. Medicaid is managed by each state, so eligibility requirements can change from state to state. Medicaid is described as a way to get health care at a lower cost or sometimes at no cost.
qs: Are Medicaid rules the same in every state?
Who typically qualifies for Medicaid?
Why does Medicaid eligibility change by state?

atoms.title: Required and optional Medicaid benefits
atoms.q: What benefits does Medicaid cover?
atoms.text: The federal government requires states to provide certain medical benefits to people who are eligible for Medicaid. States can choose to provide additional, optional benefits like hospital visits and stays, doctor's office visits, prenatal care and delivery, nursing home services, home health services, early childhood screenings and emergency medical transportation.
qs: What does Medicaid cover?
Does Medicaid cover nursing home services?
Are there optional Medicaid benefits?

atoms.title: How to enroll in Medicaid
atoms.q: How do I enroll in Medicaid?
atoms.text: To enroll in Medicaid, you'll need to apply through the Medicaid agency in your state. UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offers an enrollment page that explains how to get started, and a short plan-eligibility questionnaire that helps people see what type of plan may be a good fit.
qs: How do I sign up for Medicaid?
Where do I apply for Medicaid?
Do I apply through UnitedHealthcare or my state?

atoms.title: Caregiver resources for dual-eligible loved ones
atoms.q: Does UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offer resources for caregivers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan points caregivers to resources for those who care for people with both Medicaid and Medicare. The caregiver support section is linked from the Community Plan home page for anyone looking after a family member or friend who has both types of coverage.
qs: Where can caregivers find help?
Are there resources for people caring for someone with Medicare and Medicaid?

atoms.title: Arizona Long Term Care plan overview
atoms.q: What is the UnitedHealthcare Community Plan Arizona Long Term Care plan?
atoms.text: The Long Term Care plan is for people of all ages who have a long-term disability due to age, illness or injury. The goal is to offer services in a community setting instead of nursing home placement when possible. Members get member empowerment services to help with daily activities that the page says only UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offers. You qualify based on income and health needs.
qs: What is Arizona Long Term Care?
Can I get care in the community instead of a nursing home in Arizona?

atoms.title: Qualifying for the Arizona plan and counties served
atoms.q: How do I qualify for the Arizona Long Term Care plan?
atoms.text: To be a member of UnitedHealthcare Community Plan Long Term Care, you must be enrolled in the Arizona Long Term Care System, which is part of the Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS). The plan is available in Apache, Coconino, Gila, Maricopa, Mohave, Navajo, Pinal and Yavapai counties. Enrollment specialists can be reached at 1-800-293-3740 (TTY 711), 8:00 am to 5:00 pm local time, Monday to Friday.
qs: Which Arizona counties have the UnitedHealthcare Long Term Care plan?
Do I need AHCCCS to join the Long Term Care plan?

atoms.title: Home care and supplies for Arizona LTC members
atoms.q: What home care benefits does the Arizona Long Term Care plan include?
atoms.text: The plan includes the care and equipment needed to recover safely at home. Benefits include personal care to aid healing after illness or injury, home meal delivery if you can't safely make meals, in-home medical and safety equipment and supplies such as hospital beds, oxygen tanks, walkers and wheelchairs, nurse visits after surgery or illness, and respite care, which gives caregivers time away from a loved one who is ill or has special care needs.
qs: Does the Arizona LTC plan provide respite care?
Are home-delivered meals covered in Arizona Long Term Care?

atoms.title: Personal care home visits and modifications
atoms.q: What happens during a personal care home visit?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare conducts home visits for those needing extra help to stay at home. During the visit the team seeks to understand your personal needs, provides minor home modifications such as ramps and bathroom safety devices, sets up emergency monitoring if needed, and arranges for personal care attendants.
qs: Will the plan install a wheelchair ramp?
How do I get a personal care attendant in Arizona?

atoms.title: Case management and asthma and COPD support
atoms.q: How does case management work in the Arizona Long Term Care plan?
atoms.text: Case managers work directly with you and your family to coordinate and personalize the services you need, explain medical terms in plain language and coordinate doctor appointments. They think beyond medical needs and make sure you have support at home. For members with asthma or COPD, a case manager provides a customized treatment plan and medicine to help manage flare-ups, reduce symptoms and stay active.
qs: Does the plan help with asthma or COPD?
What does a case manager do in Arizona Long Term Care?

atoms.title: Dental, vision and hearing limits in Arizona LTC
atoms.q: What dental, vision and hearing coverage does Arizona Long Term Care include?
atoms.text: Checkups and dental care are covered for members through age 20. For members 21 and older, emergency dental care has a $1,000 per year limit and routine preventive and therapeutic services have a $1,000 per year limit for ALTCS members. Eye exams, frames and lenses including replacement and repair are covered for members under age 21, and hearing exams, therapy, tests and hearing aids are covered for members up to age 21.
qs: Is adult dental covered by Arizona Long Term Care?
What is the dental limit for ALTCS members over 21?

atoms.title: Free smartphone through MyHealthLine
atoms.q: Can Arizona Long Term Care members get a free phone?
atoms.text: If you qualify for the UnitedHealthcare MyHealthLine program, you can get a smartphone and a monthly service plan at no cost, or a service plan for your current phone. The program is meant to help members stay connected with easy and dependable access to health care services.
qs: Does Arizona Medicaid give free cell phones?
What is MyHealthLine?

atoms.title: How to get non-emergency rides in Arizona
atoms.q: How do I get a ride to medical appointments with the Arizona Long Term Care plan?
atoms.text: The plan provides trips to and from medical appointments and the pharmacy. Non-emergency transportation is provided for AHCCCS covered services. Call 1-888-889-0358 (TTY/TDD 711) at least 72 hours before your health care visit. If you need a ride to urgent care or you are being discharged from a hospital, you can call anytime. Public transportation is also available if you prefer.
qs: How far ahead do I need to book a medical ride in Arizona?
Does the plan pay for rides to the pharmacy?

atoms.title: Nurse line and behavioral health crisis numbers
atoms.q: Who can I call for health questions or a crisis in Arizona?
atoms.text: A trained nurse is available anytime, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, at 1-877-440-0255 (TTY/TDD 711). Mental health care is covered with no copay for required care, including behavioral therapy, substance abuse treatment and medications. Behavioral health crisis lines vary by county, for example 602-222-9444 or 1-800-631-1314 in Maricopa County, and the Arizona statewide crisis hotline is 1-844-534-HOPE (4673) or 988.
qs: What is the Arizona crisis hotline number?
Is there a 24-hour nurse line for Arizona members?

atoms.title: How to file a grievance or appeal in Arizona
atoms.q: How do I file a grievance or appeal with UnitedHealthcare Community Plan in Arizona?
atoms.text: If you have concerns about your medical care, first talk with your case manager, PCP or treating provider. If you are unhappy with the plan, your doctor or any part of your health care, you can file a grievance (complaint) by phone or in writing. If the plan denied a service you think you should receive, you can file an appeal, which can be written or verbal. For either, call Member Services at 1-800-293-3740. More information is in your Member Handbook.
qs: How do I appeal a denied service?
How do I file a complaint about my Medicaid plan?

atoms.title: The monthly food, OTC and utility credit
atoms.q: What is the Food, OTC and Utility Bill Credit in a dual health plan?
atoms.text: With a dual health plan, you could get a monthly credit to help with everyday needs like food, over-the-counter (OTC) products and utilities.
