atoms.text: Medicaid and CHIP members need to renew their coverage every year. In some cases, adults may need to renew 2 times per year and meet work requirements. Yearly renewals are how states check that enrollees still meet the requirements to get Medicaid benefits. This process is called Medicaid recertification or redetermination, and is also called re-enrolling in Medicaid or Medicaid renewal.
qs: How often do I renew Medicaid?
What is Medicaid recertification?

atoms.title: Who can qualify for Medicaid?
atoms.q: Who can qualify for Medicaid?
atoms.text: In all states, Medicaid provides health coverage for some low-income people, families and children, pregnant women, the elderly, and people with disabilities. In some states, Medicaid covers all low-income adults below a certain income level. The exact requirements depend on where you live, so check your state Medicaid website for its eligibility requirements.
qs: Who qualifies for Medicaid?
Do all low-income adults qualify for Medicaid?

atoms.title: Can I get Medicaid, Social Security and Medicare?
atoms.q: Can I get both Medicaid and Social Security? What about Medicare?
atoms.text: Yes, as long as you meet the qualifications for Medicaid in your state. Whether or not you get Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) doesn't change your Medicaid eligibility. Getting SSDI automatically qualifies you for Medicare, but there is a waiting period; you'll likely need to wait 2 years after you qualify for the Social Security disability benefit before you can get Medicare.
qs: Can I have Medicaid and get SSDI?
How long is the wait for Medicare after SSDI?

atoms.title: How to apply and what to have ready
atoms.q: What do I need to apply for Medicaid, and how do I enroll?
atoms.text: You'll need to fill out an application through the state agency that manages the Medicaid program in your state. Different states have different requirements, but you will likely need personal information (household members' names, birth dates and Social Security numbers, plus proof of citizenship), financial information (rent or mortgage, expenses, vehicle information, bank statements, pay stubs) and medical information (proof of disability or records of a lasting condition, recent medical bills).
qs: What documents do I need for Medicaid?
How can I enroll in Medicaid?

atoms.title: When are the Medicaid enrollment periods?
atoms.q: When are the Medicaid enrollment periods?
atoms.text: You can apply for Medicaid or CHIP (the Children's Health Insurance Program) at any time throughout the year. Eligible people can apply whenever their circumstances call for it, rather than waiting for a set enrollment window.
qs: Is there an open enrollment for Medicaid?
Can I apply for Medicaid anytime?

atoms.title: Can I change my Medicaid plan?
atoms.q: How can I change my Medicaid plan?
atoms.text: Medicaid in each state is run by the state government. While certain states may offer different types of Medicaid plans, each plan is typically for a certain type of person, such as children, families or low-income adults. It's not likely you can switch to a different Medicaid plan unless your life situation changes, for example if you get married or become pregnant.
qs: Can I switch Medicaid plans?
What life events let me change my Medicaid plan?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan serves 43 states and D.C.
atoms.q: Where does UnitedHealthcare offer Medicaid health plans?
atoms.text: As of January 2025, UnitedHealthcare Community Plan serves members who qualify for Medicaid or for both Medicaid and Medicare in 43 states and the District of Columbia. UnitedHealthcare offers Medicaid plans in Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, Washington and Wisconsin. Plans are not available in all counties.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare offer Medicaid in my state?
How many states have UnitedHealthcare Community Plan?

atoms.title: D-SNP states served by UnitedHealthcare
atoms.q: In which states does UnitedHealthcare offer Dual Special Needs plans?
atoms.text: As of January 2025, UnitedHealthcare offers Dual Special Needs plans (D-SNPs) in Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin and Wyoming. Not available in all counties.
qs: Is there a UnitedHealthcare D-SNP in my state?
Which states have UnitedHealthcare dual plans?

atoms.title: Mandatory versus optional Medicaid benefits
atoms.q: What services does Medicaid cover?
atoms.text: Each state manages its own Medicaid program, so coverage can change from state to state. Federal law requires some mandatory benefits, which include inpatient hospital care, short-term skilled nursing or rehabilitation care, doctor services, outpatient hospital or clinic care, laboratory and X-ray services, short-term home health care, ambulance service and prescription drugs for people not covered by Medicare. Optional benefits some states offer may include eye exams and glasses, hearing tests and aids, dental care, preventive screenings, extra physical therapy, non-emergency transportation and chiropractic care.
qs: Does Medicaid cover hearing aids or glasses?
What is the difference between mandatory and optional Medicaid benefits?

atoms.title: Can I have Medicaid and private insurance?
atoms.q: Can I have Medicaid and private insurance?
atoms.text: Medicaid is managed at the state level by each state government. However, state governments do not actually provide health insurance themselves. They contract with private insurance companies like UnitedHealthcare to provide health coverage for beneficiaries of Medicaid and other government health care programs. UnitedHealthcare's government-sponsored health plans operate under the name UnitedHealthcare Community Plan.
qs: Does a private company run Medicaid plans?
What is UnitedHealthcare Community Plan?

atoms.title: How does Medicaid work with other insurance?
atoms.q: How does Medicaid work with other insurance?
atoms.text: In most cases, Medicaid is the payer of last resort. That means Medicaid will pay after any other payer has paid its share of the services. If you have Medicare or any type of private health coverage, Medicaid will always be the secondary payer. Providers bill the primary payer first, and Medicaid pays what's left over, which is why Medicaid enrollees must say if they have other sources of coverage.
qs: Does Medicaid pay after Medicare?
What does payer of last resort mean?

atoms.title: Does Medicaid cover deductibles and premiums?
atoms.q: Does Medicaid cover deductibles?
atoms.text: In most cases, Medicaid pays the full cost for covered services, so people with Medicaid do not have to pay a monthly premium or any deductibles. There are some exceptions and rules vary by state. In certain cases, if someone has Social Security benefits, a small amount may be taken from those benefits to help cover the cost of Medicaid coverage.
qs: Do I pay a premium for Medicaid?
Does Medicaid have a deductible?

atoms.title: What Medicare is
atoms.q: What is Medicare?
atoms.text: Medicare is a national health insurance program run by the federal government. It's for people age 65 and older, and also some people under age 65 with certain disabilities. Medicare is separate from Medicaid, which states and the federal government fund together.
qs: What is Medicare?
Who is eligible for Medicare?

atoms.title: SSI and CHIP defined
atoms.q: What are Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and CHIP?
atoms.text: Supplemental Security Income (SSI) is a monthly cash benefit paid by the federal Social Security Administration and the state to low-income elderly, blind and disabled residents; SSI benefits are not the same as Social Security benefits. CHIP, the Children's Health Insurance Program, provides low-cost insurance for children whose families do not meet the income requirements for Medicaid. CHIP may also cover pregnant women in some states, but does not cover adults caring for children who qualify for CHIP.
qs: What is SSI?
Does CHIP cover parents?

atoms.title: Medicaid is a federal and state program
atoms.q: What is Medicaid?
atoms.text: Medicaid is a federal and state program that provides health care coverage to people who qualify. Each state runs its own Medicaid program, but the federal government has rules that all states must follow. The federal government also provides at least half of the funding for their Medicaid requirements. Coverage is based on income and the value of what you own.
qs: What is Medicaid?
Who pays for Medicaid?
Is Medicaid run by the federal government or the state?

atoms.title: States can offer more than federal minimums
atoms.q: Can states offer more than the federal government requires under Medicaid?
atoms.text: Based on federal regulations, states create and run their own Medicaid program to best serve residents who qualify. States may choose to provide more services than the federal government requires, and they may also choose to provide coverage to larger groups of people. Each state decides the full range of benefits that it covers under Medicaid.
qs: Why do Medicaid benefits differ by state?
Can my state add extra Medicaid benefits?

atoms.title: Medicaid began with the Social Security Act of 1965
atoms.q: When did Medicaid start?
atoms.text: Medicaid began as part of the Social Security Act of 1965. The original law gave states the option of receiving federal funding to help provide health care coverage to children whose families have a low income, their caregiver relatives, people who are blind and people who are disabled. Over time, the federal government has strengthened the rules and requirements for state Medicaid programs.
qs: When was Medicaid created?
What was the original purpose of Medicaid?

atoms.title: Who Medicaid serves
atoms.q: Who does Medicaid serve?
atoms.text: Medicaid programs serve specific groups of people, including pregnant women with low income, children of low-income families, children in foster care, people with disabilities, seniors with low income, and parents or caregivers with low income. States can also choose to expand eligibility to other groups, such as people with low income who may or may not have children.
qs: Who can get Medicaid?
Are foster children covered by Medicaid?
Can adults without children get Medicaid?

atoms.title: Medicaid, D-SNP and CHIP plan types
atoms.q: What types of Medicaid-related plans are available?
atoms.text: Depending on the state, there may be several types of low-cost or no-cost plans. Medicaid is managed by each state and may have its own state name. Dual Eligible Special Needs plans (D-SNP) cover people who qualify for both Medicare and Medicaid, and most give more benefits than Original Medicare. The Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) offers low-cost or no-cost coverage for infants, children and teens.
qs: What is the difference between Medicaid, D-SNP and CHIP?
Which Medicaid plan is for children?
What plan covers both Medicare and Medicaid?

atoms.title: Medicaid and CHIP enrollment numbers
atoms.q: How many people are enrolled in Medicaid and CHIP?
atoms.text: According to the Medicaid.gov August 2020 Enrollment Report, 76.4 million individuals were enrolled in Medicaid and CHIP. Of those, 69.7 million individuals were enrolled in Medicaid and 6.6 million individuals were enrolled in CHIP.
qs: How many Americans are on Medicaid?
How many children are enrolled in CHIP?

atoms.title: Mandatory Medicaid benefits
atoms.q: What are the mandatory Medicaid benefits?
atoms.text: Federal law requires states to provide certain benefits, called mandatory benefits. They include inpatient and outpatient hospital services, early and periodic screening, diagnostic and treatment services (EPSDT), nursing facility services, home health services, physician services, rural health clinic and federally qualified health center services, laboratory and X-ray services, family planning, nurse midwife services, transportation to medical care and tobacco cessation counseling for pregnant women.
qs: What does Medicaid have to cover?
Is transportation to medical care a required Medicaid benefit?

atoms.title: Optional Medicaid benefits
atoms.q: What are optional Medicaid benefits?
atoms.text: States may choose to offer other benefits, called optional benefits. These include prescription drugs, clinic services, physical and occupational therapy, speech and hearing services, podiatry, optometry, dental services, dentures, prosthetics, eyeglasses, chiropractic services, private duty nursing, personal care, hospice, case management, self-directed personal assistance services and health homes for enrollees with chronic conditions.
qs: Does Medicaid cover dental or eyeglasses?
Which Medicaid benefits are optional?

atoms.title: All states include some prescription drug coverage
atoms.q: Does Medicaid cover prescription drugs?
atoms.text: Prescription drug coverage is an optional benefit under federal Medicaid law. But, as of 2020, all states include some form of prescription drug coverage under their Medicaid program. In general, most enrollees within a state Medicaid program will get prescription drug coverage.
qs: Are prescriptions covered by Medicaid?
Do all states cover drugs under Medicaid?

atoms.title: Medicaid home and community-based services
atoms.q: What home and community-based services (HCBS) does Medicaid cover?
atoms.text: Medicaid programs may cover Home- and Community-Based Services (HCBS) to help people stay living at home and active in their community. Examples include personal care like showering, transportation, skilled nursing care, occupational, speech and physical therapy, diet and nutrition management, home-delivered meals and home chores and housekeeping. The level of support is typically based on the individual's needs.
qs: Does Medicaid pay for in-home care?
What is HCBS?
Can family members provide Medicaid home care services?

atoms.title: How to apply for Medicaid
atoms.q: How do I apply for Medicaid?
atoms.text: Because each state manages its own Medicaid program, eligibility varies from one state to another. 1) If you have questions about qualifying, contact your state Medicaid agency. 2) Or apply online at the website for your state Medicaid agency to see if you qualify. 3) Answer a few quick questions on the plan-eligibility tool to see what type of plan may be a good fit. Benefits change depending on where you live.
qs: How do I apply for Medicaid?
Can I apply online for Medicaid?

atoms.title: What MLTSS is in New Jersey
atoms.q: What is Managed Long Term Services and Supports (MLTSS)?
atoms.text: Managed Long Term Services and Supports (MLTSS) programs are focused on serving frail, elderly and disabled individuals. The program combines traditional health care benefits, such as doctor visits, hospital stays and labs, with long term services and supports that provide help in the home or community with daily living activities. The plan is available statewide in New Jersey.
qs: What is NJ FamilyCare MLTSS?
Does MLTSS cover both medical care and help at home?

atoms.title: Added benefits for MLTSS members
atoms.q: What extra benefits do MLTSS members get beyond NJ FamilyCare?
atoms.text: NJ FamilyCare is a comprehensive health insurance program. In addition to NJ FamilyCare services, MLTSS members also receive care management, home and vehicle modifications, home delivered meals, personal emergency response systems, mental health and addiction services, assisted living, community residential services and nursing home care.
qs: Does NJ MLTSS cover assisted living?
What services come with MLTSS in New Jersey?

atoms.title: Who is eligible for MLTSS
atoms.q: Who is eligible for NJ FamilyCare MLTSS?
atoms.text: Members who have been assessed for long-term services and supports and have met both the financial and clinical eligibility requirements established by the State for MLTSS are eligible to receive care management and supportive services. The purpose of MLTSS is to enable individuals who are at the nursing home level of care to receive person-centered services in the least restrictive and most integrated setting.
qs: How do I qualify for MLTSS in New Jersey?
Do I need a nursing-home level of care for MLTSS?

atoms.title: NJ FamilyCare, copayments and related terms
atoms.q: What do NJ FamilyCare, copayments, Medicaid/MLTSS and SSI mean?
atoms.text: NJ FamilyCare is a state health insurance program for people with low income who meet certain eligibility requirements, and programs can vary from state to state. Co-payments are amounts you pay directly to the provider for a service, and certain NJ FamilyCare beneficiaries are required to pay them. Medicare is a federal health insurance program for people 65 or older, disabled persons or those with end-stage renal disease, and eligibility is not based on income. SSI stands for Supplemental Security Income.
qs: What is NJ FamilyCare?
Do NJ FamilyCare members pay copayments?

atoms.title: How to reach NJ FamilyCare MLTSS support
atoms.q: How do I contact UnitedHealthcare about NJ FamilyCare MLTSS?
atoms.text: To request a member handbook or provider directory, call Member Services at 1-800-941-4647 (TTY 711). The NJ FamilyCare plan specialists can answer questions and help you enroll at 1-800-941-4647, available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. To speak with Care Management for MLTSS, call 1-800-645-9409 (TTY 711).
qs: What is the phone number for NJ FamilyCare MLTSS care management?
How do I enroll in NJ FamilyCare with UnitedHealthcare?

atoms.title: NJ MLTSS handbooks and special support programs
atoms.q: What member handbooks are available for NJ MLTSS?
atoms.text: Member resources include the English and Spanish member handbooks, and a member handbook insert for community-based palliative care last updated 05/22/2026. The page also lists a Housing Support member handbook (last updated 06/26/2025) and a Nutrition Support member handbook (last updated 07/01/2025). Members get access to a member-only website where they can chat with a nurse online and more.
qs: Is there a housing support handbook for NJ MLTSS members?
Where do I find the NJ FamilyCare member handbook?

atoms.title: Finding dentists and pharmacies for MLTSS
