To find an in-network dentist, members follow a link to another website and select NJ UnitedHealthcare Community Plan. The page also lists the New Jersey Smiles Program directory with county-by-county dental provider lists for all 21 counties.
qs: Where is the MLTSS preferred drug list?
How do I find a dentist for NJ FamilyCare MLTSS?

atoms.title: Plans UnitedHealthcare offers in Tennessee
atoms.q: What health plans does UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offer in Tennessee?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan offers many plans to Tennessee residents. It covers adults, people with disabilities, expecting moms and children in Tennessee with its TennCare Medicaid plans. Plan types include Medicaid, Dual Special Needs plans, the Children's Health Insurance Program and Individual & Family ACA plans in the Bronze, Silver and Gold metal levels.
qs: What UnitedHealthcare plans are available in Tennessee?
Does UnitedHealthcare offer TennCare?

atoms.title: TennCare Medicaid plan
atoms.q: Who is the TennCare Medicaid plan from UnitedHealthcare for?
atoms.text: The TennCare Medicaid plan is for pregnant women, children, adults and people who are elderly or have a disability and who meet income requirements. It covers well and sick care plus extra support for those who need it. TennCare is described as health insurance for people with low incomes, with costs that are low and based on ability to pay. The plan is available wherever you live in Tennessee.
qs: Who qualifies for TennCare?
Is the TennCare plan available statewide?

atoms.title: TennCare Long-Term Services and Supports
atoms.q: What are TennCare Long-Term Services and Supports (LTSS)?
atoms.text: Long-Term Services & Supports (LTSS) are medical and/or personal care and supportive services needed by people who have lost some capacity to perform activities of daily living, such as bathing, dressing, eating, transfers and toileting, and/or activities essential to daily living such as housework, preparing meals, taking medications, shopping and managing money. TennCare CHOICES serves adults 21 and older with a physical disability and seniors 65 and older; Employment and Community First CHOICES serves people of all ages with an intellectual or developmental disability.
qs: What is LTSS in Tennessee?
Who is eligible for TennCare CHOICES?

atoms.title: Getting screened for CHOICES or ECF CHOICES
atoms.q: How do I apply for TennCare CHOICES long-term services?
atoms.text: If you think you need long-term services and supports, call UnitedHealthcare at 1-800-690-1606. A short screening may be done over the phone to help decide if you may qualify for CHOICES. If the screening shows you don't appear to qualify, you'll get a letter explaining how you can finish applying. For Employment and Community First (ECF) CHOICES, you can refer yourself or your loved one for the program.
qs: How do I get screened for CHOICES?
How do I refer my family member to ECF CHOICES?

atoms.title: Tennessee CoverKids (CHIP)
atoms.q: What is Tennessee CoverKids?
atoms.text: Tennessee CoverKids is the state's Children's Health Insurance Program. It provides free, comprehensive health coverage for qualifying children age 18 and younger and pregnant women. It covers preventive health services, doctor visits, hospital visits, vaccinations, well-child visits, developmental screenings and mental health, and pregnant women get prenatal, delivery and postpartum care. Children also get vision and dental care.
qs: What does CoverKids cover?
Is CoverKids free?

atoms.title: 2026 Dual Special Needs plan extras in Tennessee
atoms.q: What extra benefits do Tennessee Dual Special Needs plans include?
atoms.text: Tennesseans on a UnitedHealthcare Dual Special Needs plan get benefits beyond those of Original Medicare or Tennessee Medicaid. For 2026 the page lists a monthly credit to buy healthy food and OTC products or pay utility bills, a $0 copay on covered generic and brand-name prescriptions including home delivery, and an allowance for covered types of preventive and comprehensive dental. D-SNPs are for people who get both Medicaid and Medicare, and members keep their TennCare benefits.
qs: What does a Tennessee dual plan include in 2026?
Do dual plans in Tennessee have $0 copays for prescriptions?

atoms.title: Behavioral health coverage matches physical health
atoms.q: How does the TennCare plan cover behavioral health?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says behavioral health is as important as physical health, so it has the same coverage for both. Required care is 100% covered with no copay, including mental health treatment, substance use treatment and medications. Members can also use the Calm Health app at no cost for mental health screening, self-guided digital programs and emotional well-being support, accessed through the UnitedHealthcare app under Coverage & Benefits.
qs: Is mental health covered by TennCare with UnitedHealthcare?
Is there a free mental health app for Tennessee members?

atoms.title: Well and sick care and Healthy First Steps
atoms.q: What well and sick care does the Tennessee Medicaid plan include?
atoms.text: Member benefits include well visits (preventive checkups, shots and lab tests), Healthy First Steps, a program to help you and your baby stay healthy, a 24-hour NurseLine staffed by registered nurses, routine shots and vaccines, and lab tests and X-rays. For pregnancy care the plan also lists choice of an OB/GYN in network, prenatal visits and a choice of birth centers across Tennessee.
qs: Does Tennessee Medicaid have a 24-hour nurse line?
What pregnancy benefits does TennCare include?

atoms.title: Vision, dental and hearing limits in Tennessee
atoms.q: What vision, dental and hearing coverage does the TennCare plan have?
atoms.text: Vision is covered with limits and not covered for pregnant women age 19 and older; for children under 19 it includes 1 vision exam per calendar year, 1 set of lenses per calendar year and 1 set of frames every 2 calendar years. Dental is for children under age 19 only on the Community Plan. Hearing includes an annual screening, with hearing aids limited to 1 per ear per calendar year up to age 5, then 1 per ear every 2 years.
qs: How many eye exams does TennCare cover per year?
Are hearing aids covered under TennCare?

atoms.title: TennCare CHOICES and its three groups
atoms.q: What is TennCare CHOICES in Long-Term Services and Supports?
atoms.text: TennCare CHOICES is for adults age 21 and older with a physical disability and seniors age 65 and older. It offers Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) to help a person live in their own home or the community, and also provides nursing home care when needed. Group 1 is for people of all ages receiving nursing home care. Group 2 is for people who qualify for nursing home care but choose home care. Group 3 is for people who don't qualify for nursing home care but need home care to stay at home safely. To see if you qualify, call 1-800-690-1606.
qs: What are the CHOICES groups?
Can I get home care instead of a nursing home in Tennessee?

atoms.title: Employment and Community First (ECF) CHOICES
atoms.q: What is Employment and Community First CHOICES?
atoms.text: Employment and Community First CHOICES is for people of all ages who have an intellectual or developmental disability (I/DD), including people with significant disabilities. Services help people gain as much independence as possible and live with family or in the community, not in an institution. Residential services are available for adults who do not live with family. The program can help explore working and learn skills for work, finding a job and keeping a job, whether part-time, full-time or self-employment.
qs: What is ECF CHOICES?
Does Tennessee Medicaid help people with disabilities find jobs?

atoms.title: ECF CHOICES benefit Groups 4 through 8
atoms.q: What are ECF CHOICES Groups 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8?
atoms.text: Group 4 (Essential Family Supports) is for families caring for a child under 21 with I/DD living at home. Group 5 (Essential Supports for Employment and Independent Living) is for adults 21 and older with I/DD who don't qualify for nursing home level of care. Group 6 (Comprehensive Supports) is for adults 21 and older who would qualify for nursing home care. Group 7 (Intensive Behavioral Family Supports) is for a small number of children under 21 with severe behavior needs. Group 8 (Comprehensive Behavioral Supports) is for a small number of adults moving into the community from a highly structured setting.
qs: Which ECF CHOICES group is for children with I/DD?
What is Group 6 in ECF CHOICES?

atoms.title: CHOICES home and community-based service limits
atoms.q: What are the service limits for CHOICES HCBS?
atoms.text: CHOICES HCBS limits listed on the page include: personal care visits up to 2 per day at least 4 hours apart; attendant care up to 1080 hours per calendar year (up to 1400 hours for people who need help with chores or errands too); home-delivered meals up to 1 meal per day; adult day care up to 2080 hours per calendar year; in-home respite up to 216 hours per year; inpatient respite up to 9 days per year; assistive technology up to $900 per year; and minor home modifications up to $6,000 per project, $10,000 per year and $20,000 per lifetime.
qs: How many hours of attendant care does CHOICES cover?
What is the home modification limit under CHOICES?

atoms.title: Katie Beckett program for children
atoms.q: What is Tennessee's Katie Beckett program?
atoms.text: Tennessee's Katie Beckett program is for children under the age of 18 with significant disabilities or complex medical needs who are not Medicaid eligible because of their parent's income or assets. The program has two parts, A and B, and provides services and/or help paying for medical care that private insurance does not cover.
qs: What is the Katie Beckett waiver?
Can my child get help if our income is too high for Medicaid?

atoms.title: What a CHOICES care coordinator does
atoms.q: What does a care coordinator do for TennCare CHOICES members?
atoms.text: A Care Coordinator provides information about CHOICES and answers questions, helps you get the right kind of long-term services and supports in the right setting, coordinates your physical health, behavioral health and long-term services needs, helps fix problems with your care, and communicates with your providers. The care coordinator also checks at least once a year that you still need the level of care provided in a nursing home or, for Group 3, are still at risk of going into a nursing home.
qs: Who coordinates my long-term care in TennCare?
How often is my level of care reviewed in CHOICES?

atoms.title: ECF CHOICES support coordinator role
atoms.q: What does a support coordinator do in ECF CHOICES?
atoms.text: A Support Coordinator helps you identify the services and supports you need, explore employment options and ways to be part of your community, understand all of the services, providers and settings you can choose from, choose your services, providers and settings, and write your support plan based on your choices and preferences. The coordinator also makes sure you get the services in your support plan. If you aren't sure who your Support Coordinator is, call 1-800-690-1606.
qs: What is a support plan in ECF CHOICES?
Who is my support coordinator?

atoms.title: Adult dental limits in CHOICES
atoms.q: What adult dental coverage do CHOICES members have?
atoms.text: CHOICES Groups 1, 2 and 3 and ECF CHOICES Groups 4, 5, 6 and 8 include adult dental services, covering basic dental care for adults age 21 and older including exams, cleanings and fillings. Limits are up to $5,000 per calendar year and no more than $7,500 over three calendar years in a row. Children under 21 already have dental care through TennCare.
qs: Does TennCare CHOICES cover dental for adults?
What is the yearly dental limit for CHOICES members?

atoms.title: How to arrange a TennCare medical ride
atoms.q: How do I get transportation to a medical appointment with TennCare?
atoms.text: Call 1-866-405-0238 (TTY 711) to set up a ride, at least 2 business days before the appointment whenever possible. Have your Medicaid ID card ready, know your provider's address and the date and time, and tell the transporter about special needs like a wheelchair. If your return time wasn't scheduled, call to say you're ready to be picked up. In an emergency call 911. Eligible members may also use the Mileage Reimbursement Program, effective April 1, 2025, of up to $.70 per mile.
qs: How do I schedule a ride to the doctor with TennCare?
Does TennCare reimburse mileage?

atoms.title: Behavioral health access and crisis lines
atoms.q: How do TennCare members get behavioral health help and authorization?
atoms.text: Required mental health care is 100% covered with no copay and includes therapy, substance abuse treatment and medications. TennCare members in Middle Tennessee can call 1-800-690-1606 (TTY 711) to be matched with a provider; all services must be authorized, so you must call before receiving services. An Emergency Crisis Service team helps members obtain emergency care 24 hours a day at 1-800-867-6758, and the Tennessee REDLINE offers addiction information and referrals at 1-800-889-9789.
qs: Who do I call for a mental health emergency with TennCare?
Do behavioral health services need authorization?

atoms.title: Enrollment help and eligibility for CHOICES
atoms.q: How do I enroll in the TennCare LTSS plan?
atoms.text: TennCare eligibility depends on a number of different criteria, and members are directed to the State of Tennessee's Eligibility Categories page. The TennCare Medicaid plan specialists can answer questions and help you enroll by calling 1-800-690-1606 (TTY 711), 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The plan is available in the listed Tennessee counties, which include Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, Shelby and many others.
qs: How do I enroll in CHOICES?
Is the TennCare CHOICES plan available in my county?

atoms.title: What supplemental health insurance is
atoms.q: What is supplemental insurance?
atoms.text: Supplemental health insurance provides help with, or supplements, a health plan by providing additional benefits that can help with out-of-pocket expenses such as deductibles, coinsurance and copays, or even cover routine dental or vision products. UnitedHealthcare notes that a medical insurance plan is not going to cover everything, so completing coverage with supplemental plans can help protect against unexpected costs.
qs: What does supplemental health insurance do?
Do I need supplemental insurance on top of my medical plan?
What costs does supplemental insurance help with?

atoms.title: Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare supplemental plans
atoms.q: Who provides UnitedHealthcare supplemental insurance plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's supplemental plans, such as dental, vision or fixed benefit health insurance plans, can help cover medical expenses not covered by a medical plan. These plans are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company, a UnitedHealthcare company, and help round out other health insurance coverage. Shoppers can enter a ZIP code to find a plan or call 1-855-972-1023 (TTY 711).
qs: Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare dental and vision plans?
What is Golden Rule Insurance Company?
How do I find supplemental plans by ZIP code?

atoms.title: Dental insurance versus dental savings memberships
atoms.q: What is the difference between dental insurance and a dental savings membership?
atoms.text: Dental insurance plans offer coverage for many common dental care services. Dental savings memberships are an alternative to insurance that helps people save on qualified services from participating providers. UnitedHealthcare states that dental discount memberships are not insurance.
qs: Is a dental savings membership the same as dental insurance?
Dental insurance vs dental discount plan?
What is a dental savings membership?

atoms.title: What vision insurance helps cover
atoms.q: What does vision insurance help pay for?
atoms.text: Vision insurance plans can help people cover and budget for vision care expenses such as routine eye exams, prescription glasses and/or contact lenses. UnitedHealthcare lists vision insurance among its supplemental options alongside dental insurance and fixed benefit health insurance.
qs: Does vision insurance cover eye exams and glasses?
What is vision insurance for?

atoms.title: Fixed benefit health insurance overview
atoms.q: What is fixed benefit health insurance?
atoms.text: Fixed indemnity insurance, also marketed as fixed benefit health insurance, is meant to help ease some common hospital and doctor out-of-pocket costs with cash benefits paid for qualified medical services. UnitedHealthcare states that the product provides limited benefits, is a supplement to health insurance, and is not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the Affordable Care Act (ACA).
qs: What is a fixed indemnity plan?
Is fixed benefit insurance a replacement for major medical coverage?
How do fixed benefit plans pay?

atoms.title: Limited-benefit warning for fixed indemnity products
atoms.q: Does a fixed indemnity plan satisfy ACA minimum essential coverage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that fixed indemnity products provide limited benefits and are a supplement to health insurance, not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the Affordable Care Act. Lack of major medical coverage or other minimum essential coverage may result in an additional payment with taxes. These products pay benefits in a stated amount regardless of the actual expenses incurred, and not all plans on the page are fixed benefit plans.
qs: Can a fixed indemnity plan replace my health insurance?
Will I owe a tax payment if I only have a supplemental plan?

atoms.title: More supplemental options beyond dental and vision
atoms.q: What other supplemental plans does UnitedHealthcare offer?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists several more options: accident insurance helps with costs of qualifying accidental injuries and pays regardless of other coverage; critical illness insurance pays lump sum cash benefits for qualifying serious illnesses; hospital insurance pays a fixed cash amount per day for hospital stays; international travel insurance covers medical emergencies, lost passports or baggage and travel assistance; term life insurance pays beneficiaries a lump sum on death; and mental health virtual therapy is offered for one monthly cost.
qs: What types of supplemental insurance are available?
What does accident insurance versus critical illness insurance cover?
What is hospital insurance versus term life insurance?

atoms.title: Why combine supplemental plans
atoms.q: Why combine insurance plans and non-insurance health products?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says combining insurance plans and non-insurance health products is a way to build a mix of healthcare options that meet a person's needs. A shopper could also save money compared to buying the plans individually.
qs: Is it cheaper to bundle dental, vision and other plans?
Why would I combine supplemental insurance plans?

atoms.title: Three reasons to choose supplemental insurance
atoms.q: Why choose supplemental insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare gives three reasons to consider supplemental plans. Get complete coverage: fill gaps with help paying out-of-pocket costs not covered by a regular medical plan. Protect your finances: cash benefit plans that pay a lump sum can give peace of mind if a critical illness or accident happens. Customize for your needs: with a variety of plans, shoppers can match coverage to their age, family and situation.
qs: What are the benefits of supplemental insurance?
How can supplemental plans protect my finances?

atoms.title: Is supplemental insurance worth buying
atoms.q: Is it worth it to buy supplemental insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says that because supplemental plans cover many different needs, a person may decide one or more is definitely worth the price for themselves and their family. The page frames supplemental plans as a way to help protect a person and their family when something major happens to their health.
qs: Is supplemental health insurance worth the money?
Should I buy supplemental insurance?

atoms.title: Dental and vision in Medicare, Medicaid, employer plans
atoms.q: Do Medicare, Medicaid or employer plans include dental and vision?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare points out that dental, vision and supplemental coverage may be included with some Medicare plans, like Medicare Advantage or Medicare Supplement (Medigap) plans. Dental, vision and other extra benefits are included with some, but not all, Medicaid plans. Employers can also offer specialty plans such as dental, vision and supplemental options to give employees added benefits.
qs: Does Medicare Advantage include dental and vision?
Do Medicaid plans cover dental and vision?
Can my employer offer dental and vision plans?

atoms.title: What accident insurance is
atoms.q: What is accident insurance?
atoms.text: Accident insurance is also known as supplemental accident insurance or personal accident insurance. With accident coverage, cash benefits help pay for expenses related to a qualifying accident. UnitedHealthcare says that can include things like ambulance care, physical therapy, lost wages and more.
qs: What does accident insurance pay for?
What is personal accident insurance?
Does accident insurance pay for lost wages?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare accident plans and underwriter
atoms.q: Who offers UnitedHealthcare accident insurance plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare branded accident plans are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company and offer a variety of cash-benefit options. These plans help pay for expenses related to accidental injuries. Plans can be viewed by state using a ZIP code, or by calling 1-866-671-0378.
qs: Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare accident insurance?
How do I get an accident insurance quote?

atoms.title: Is accident insurance worth it
atoms.q: Is accident insurance worth it?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare notes that accidents often happen when least expected, and while medical insurance may cover some related costs, extra expenses can add up and lead to financial strain. With accident insurance, the cash benefit payout can help pay for these expenses. The page points to a savings survey as context for why extra cash can matter.
qs: Do I need accident insurance if I have health insurance?
Is it worth buying accident insurance?

atoms.title: Share of adults without emergency savings
atoms.q: How many U.S. adults lack emergency savings?
atoms.text: According to Bankrate's 2023 annual emergency savings report, cited by UnitedHealthcare, 22% of U.S. adults claim they have no emergency savings and 57% are not comfortable with what they have for emergency savings. UnitedHealthcare uses this to show why a cash benefit payout from accident insurance can help when extra expenses add up.
qs: What percent of Americans have no emergency savings?
Why do people buy accident insurance?

atoms.title: Accident cash benefits can be spent as you choose
atoms.q: How can I use an accident insurance cash benefit?
atoms.text: With an accident insurance plan, the policyholder decides how to use the cash benefit. The page lists expense categories that the benefit can help pay for, and notes the benefit is paid in a stated amount regardless of the actual expense incurred.
qs: What can I spend an accident insurance payout on?
Does accident insurance pay a set amount?

atoms.title: Services an accident plan can help cover
atoms.q: What does an accident insurance plan cover?
atoms.text: An accident insurance plan can help pay for services directly related to an accidental injury, including ambulance service, hospital emergency room care, physical therapy and urgent care center service. Injuries listed include burns, concussions, dislocations, fractures and lacerations. Most services must occur within a certain number of hours and days from the accident, limits may apply, and covered services vary by plan and state.
qs: Does accident insurance cover fractures and concussions?
Does accident insurance cover the ER and ambulance?
Is there a time limit to get treated after an accident?

atoms.title: Accident plans are limited-benefit supplements
atoms.q: Is accident insurance a substitute for health insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that accident insurance products provide limited benefits and are supplements to health insurance, not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the Affordable Care Act (ACA). Lack of major medical coverage or other minimum essential coverage may result in an additional payment with taxes. The products pay benefits in a stated amount regardless of the actual expense incurred.
qs: Can accident insurance replace my health plan?
Is accident insurance ACA compliant?

atoms.title: Accident insurance has no network limits
atoms.q: Do I have to use a network with accident insurance?
atoms.text: A footnote on UnitedHealthcare's accident insurance page states there are no network limitations for these accident insurance plans, but a person may be bound to certain networks and providers with their major medical plan.
qs: Do I need to go in network for accident insurance benefits?
Can I see any doctor with accident insurance?

atoms.title: Pairing accident insurance with short term plans
atoms.q: Can I add accident insurance to a short term insurance plan?
atoms.text: According to UnitedHealthcare, all products require separate applications, and separate policies or certificates are issued unless the product is a rider or optional benefits. Short term plans have a limited duration, are not renewable, are medically underwritten and do not cover preexisting conditions. They do not meet minimum essential coverage requirements, so signing up may result in a tax penalty, and their expiration does not trigger an ACA special enrollment opportunity.
qs: Can I buy accident insurance with short term health insurance?
Does short term insurance cover preexisting conditions?
Does losing short term coverage give me a special enrollment period?

atoms.title: What critical illness insurance is
atoms.q: What is critical illness insurance?
atoms.text: Critical illness insurance plans are also called critical care insurance or critical illness coverage. These plans provide a lump-sum cash benefit to help cover expenses related to a qualifying serious illness.
qs: What is critical illness coverage?
What does critical illness insurance pay?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare critical illness plans and underwriter
atoms.q: Who offers UnitedHealthcare critical illness plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare branded critical illness plans are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company. They provide a cash benefit to help cover expenses related to a serious illness or condition. Plans can be viewed by state using a ZIP code, or by calling 1-866-671-0376.
qs: Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare critical illness insurance?
How do I get a critical illness quote?

atoms.title: Why someone might need critical illness coverage
atoms.q: Why would I need a critical illness insurance plan?
atoms.text: A critical illness can happen to anyone at any time, without warning, and it can also cause financial strain. A person may be unable to work for a time, and medical bills and other unexpected expenses can add up. A medical health insurance plan may cover some health care costs but often will not cover them all, which is where a critical illness plan can help.
qs: Do I need critical illness insurance?
How can critical illness insurance help if I can't work?

atoms.title: How critical illness cash benefits can be used
atoms.q: What can I use a critical illness benefit for?
atoms.text: With a critical illness insurance plan, the policyholder can use the cash-benefit funds as they see fit. UnitedHealthcare says this includes paying everyday living expenses while out of work, among other expenses listed on the page.
qs: Can I use critical illness money for rent and bills?
How is the critical illness payout spent?

atoms.title: How a critical illness lump sum is paid
atoms.q: How does a critical illness plan pay benefits?
atoms.text: With UnitedHealthcare critical illness insurance, a lump sum is paid by the Golden Rule Insurance Company critical illness plan, up to the maximum lifetime benefit. The benefit is paid for expenses related to covered conditions. Waiting periods may apply, and some critical illnesses may pay only a portion of the benefit.
qs: Is there a waiting period for critical illness insurance?
Is there a lifetime maximum on critical illness benefits?

atoms.title: Conditions a critical illness plan can cover
atoms.q: What conditions does critical illness insurance cover?
atoms.text: Covered conditions can include heart attack, life-threatening cancer, loss of hearing, speech or vision, loss of independent living, advanced Alzheimer's disease, major organ transplant, paralysis, coma, renal failure, stroke, carcinoma in situ and coronary artery bypass graft. Critical conditions covered vary by plan, and plan design and availability vary by state.
qs: Does critical illness insurance cover cancer?
Does critical illness insurance cover stroke or heart attack?
What illnesses are covered by critical illness insurance?

atoms.title: Loss of independent living definition
atoms.q: What does loss of independent living mean on a critical illness plan?
atoms.text: On UnitedHealthcare's critical illness page, loss of independent living refers to the permanent inability to perform 2 or more of the 6 activities of daily living for a period of at least 90 days, as defined in the policy. The activities listed are bathing, continence, dressing, eating, toileting, and transfer and mobility.
qs: What are the activities of daily living in critical illness insurance?
How is loss of independent living defined?

atoms.title: Most households can replace under a month of income
atoms.q: How much income can most American households replace from savings?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that most American households are savings limited, meaning they can replace less than one month of their income through liquid savings. The page says critical illness coverage can give families financial help in hard times. The page cites Gen Re's 2021 U.S. critical illness market survey.
qs: How long could the average family live on savings if they couldn't work?
How do critical illness benefits work?

atoms.title: Critical illness first-diagnosis rule and benefit variation
atoms.q: When are critical illness benefits paid?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare notes that critical illness benefits are paid upon first diagnosis in the covered person's lifetime in most states, and are subject to preexisting conditions. Amounts available may vary by state and by the primary insured's issue age. The page also advises consulting a tax advisor for details on the federal and state tax issues that apply.
qs: Does critical illness insurance pay on first diagnosis?
Do preexisting conditions affect critical illness coverage?
Are critical illness payouts taxable?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare dental plans for individuals and families
atoms.q: What dental insurance plans does UnitedHealthcare offer?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare branded dental plans for individuals and families are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company. Shoppers can choose plans that include basic dental coverage for general dental care, or explore coverage that includes major dental care, such as dental implants. Plans can be viewed by state using a ZIP code, or by calling 1-866-487-9301.
qs: What dental plans does UnitedHealthcare sell to individuals?
Does UnitedHealthcare dental insurance cover implants?
How do I find dental plans in my state?

atoms.title: Dental insurance plans compared with savings memberships
atoms.q: Should I choose a dental insurance plan or a dental savings membership?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers two ways to manage dental costs. Dental insurance plans range from basic coverage to major dental care, such as dental implants. Dental savings memberships are an alternative to insurance that gives access to savings on common services from participating providers. UnitedHealthcare states that dental discount memberships are not insurance.
qs: Dental insurance or dental discount membership?
What is the difference between a dental plan and a savings membership?

atoms.title: Preventive dental care coverage
atoms.q: How is preventive dental care typically covered?
atoms.text: Preventive dental care is often covered with no deductible or waiting period. UnitedHealthcare says this most often includes routine cleanings for all covered persons and fluoride treatments for those under the age of 16 on the plan.
qs: Are dental cleanings covered by dental insurance?
Is there a waiting period for preventive dental care?
Does dental insurance cover fluoride treatments?

atoms.title: Basic and major dental services
atoms.q: What are basic and major dental services?
atoms.text: Basic dental services often include simple fillings or emergency treatment for dental pain, and are subject to a deductible and coinsurance. Major services can include retainers and root canals; these are often subject to the plan's deductible, coinsurance and waiting periods. Preventive care, by comparison, is often covered with no deductible or waiting period.
qs: Are fillings basic or major dental work?
Does dental insurance cover root canals?
Do major dental services have a waiting period?

atoms.title: Dental network and direct payment to dentists
atoms.q: Do I need to file claims with a dental plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare dental plans give access to a wide dental network, with a choice of dental providers that often includes offices in both private and retail settings. Plans pay in-network dentists directly, which makes payments easy to manage and means members do not need to submit claim forms.
qs: Do I have to submit claim forms with dental insurance?
Does dental insurance pay my dentist directly?
Are retail dental offices in the network?

atoms.title: Dental coverage with no age limits
atoms.q: Are there dental plans for seniors or people on Medicare?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says its dental coverage has no age limits, with options available for every member of a family and every stage of life. Medicare does not include dental benefits, so the company offers plans designed specifically for seniors who are on Medicare.
qs: Does Medicare cover dental?
Are there dental plans for seniors?
Is there an age limit for dental insurance?

atoms.title: Why dental benefits can matter for health and cost
atoms.q: Why should I have dental coverage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare gives three reasons to have dental benefits. Better oral health: people with dental coverage are more likely to get routine dental care. Cost savings: if a person waits until there is a problem, dental care often gets more expensive and involved. Supports overall health: without preventive dental care, major health problems such as heart disease and diabetes appear more often.
qs: Is dental insurance worth it?
How does dental care affect overall health?
Why get preventive dental care?

atoms.title: Dental HMO versus dental indemnity plans
atoms.q: What is the difference between dental HMO and dental indemnity insurance?
atoms.text: A dental HMO (Health Maintenance Organization) has lower premiums, fixed copays for services, a restricted provider network that must be used, and no annual maximum. A dental indemnity plan has higher premiums, freedom to choose any dentist, coinsurance payments, an annual benefit maximum and no network discounts. UnitedHealthcare branded dental plans from Golden Rule Insurance Company are Dental PPO plans.
qs: What types of dental insurance are there?
Is UnitedHealthcare dental insurance a PPO or HMO?
What is dental indemnity insurance?

atoms.title: Why choose UnitedHealthcare dental plans
atoms.q: What are the advantages of UnitedHealthcare dental plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare highlights four features of its dental plans. Multiple plans with different benefit levels to fit different budgets; preventive care on day 1 of the plan with no waiting period; a nationwide network of dentists who offer dental work to members at negotiated lower rates; and, in most states, vision and hearing benefits are also available.
qs: Do UnitedHealthcare dental plans have a waiting period for cleanings?
Can I add vision and hearing to a dental plan?
How large is the UnitedHealthcare dental network?

atoms.title: Dental plans sold alongside vision and cash-benefit plans
atoms.q: Can I get other supplemental coverage with a dental plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare points shoppers who want more than dental coverage to its supplemental plans, such as vision and cash-benefit plans, that offer coverage for expenses not covered by a medical plan. A plan finder is available to answer a few questions and show which insurance options may be available.
qs: What other plans can I buy with dental insurance?
Does UnitedHealthcare sell vision with dental?

atoms.title: What Dental Savings Complete is
atoms.q: What is Dental Savings Complete?
atoms.text: Dental Savings Complete, provided by Dental Benefit Providers, Inc., is a membership for discounts on qualified dental services and more. Even with dental insurance, a member may be able to save on services not covered under the dental plan. The membership also includes savings on hearing and vision materials, plus access to prescription discounts offered through Optum Perks.
qs: What is Dental Savings Complete?
Can I use a dental discount membership if I have dental insurance?
Does Dental Savings Complete include prescription discounts?

atoms.title: How a dental savings membership works
atoms.q: What is a dental savings membership and how do I pay?
atoms.text: A dental savings membership provides access to dental discounts. Members can pay monthly or annually, and there is no waiting period. After enrolling (a one-time enrollment fee may apply), a member receives a membership ID card to get discounts on qualified dental services at participating providers. For each qualified service, the member pays the discounted rate that is part of the membership.
qs: How does a dental discount plan work?
Is there an enrollment fee for Dental Savings Complete?
Can I pay for a dental savings plan monthly?

atoms.title: Services that may be discounted
atoms.q: What services are discounted with Dental Savings Complete?
atoms.text: Services that may be discounted include dental (cleanings, crowns, fillings, orthodontics, X-rays and pediatric dentistry), vision (glasses, contacts and access to laser vision correction offered through QualSight), hearing (hearing aids and hearing-aid related visits) and pharmacy (access to prescription drug discounts through Optum Perks).
qs: Are braces or orthodontics discounted with a dental savings plan?
Does Dental Savings Complete cover hearing aids?
What dental services get a discount?

atoms.title: No copays, deductibles or annual limits
atoms.q: Does Dental Savings Complete have deductibles or annual limits?
atoms.text: Dental savings memberships such as Dental Savings Complete have no copays, deductibles, annual limits or maximums, according to UnitedHealthcare. They are usually available for individuals or families, and members pay the discounted rate for each qualified service at participating providers.
qs: Is there an annual maximum on a dental discount plan?
Do dental savings plans have deductibles?

atoms.title: Using a membership with or without dental insurance
atoms.q: Can I use Dental Savings Complete if I already have dental insurance?
atoms.text: A dental savings membership is described as great for people who do not have dental insurance. People who do have insurance can still get discounts on qualifying services that are not covered under their insurance plan. The membership has no waiting period and includes discounts on glasses, contacts and hearing aids.
qs: Can I have dental insurance and a dental discount plan?
Is there a waiting period for dental savings memberships?

atoms.title: How to use Dental Savings Complete
atoms.q: How do I start using Dental Savings Complete?
atoms.text: 1) Enroll in Dental Savings Complete and receive an ID card, which may take up to 72 hours. 2) Make an appointment with a participating dentist. 3) Show the card and get the discounted rate at the time of service.
qs: How long does it take to get a Dental Savings Complete card?
How do I use a dental discount card?
How do I enroll in Dental Savings Complete?

atoms.title: Dental discount program versus dental insurance
atoms.q: Is a dental discount program different from low-cost dental insurance?
atoms.text: According to the page's disclosures, Dental Savings Complete is not insurance. It provides discounted services from participating providers and does not make payments to providers. Members are obligated to pay for all services but receive a discount, and the range of discounts varies by provider and service. Dental Benefit Providers, Inc. is the Discount Plan Organization.
qs: Is a dental savings plan insurance?
Does a dental discount plan pay my dentist?
Do all dental savings discounts work the same way?

atoms.title: Cancellation period and provider list
atoms.q: Can I cancel Dental Savings Complete and see participating providers?
atoms.text: Dental Savings Complete contains a thirty-day cancellation period. A list of participating providers, including each provider's name, city, state and specialty in the member's service area, is made available before and after membership. Details are available by calling 877-205-3342 or on the provider search page named on the page. The page also refers readers to the Dental Savings Complete brochure.
qs: Can I cancel a dental savings membership?
How do I find participating dentists for Dental Savings Complete?

atoms.title: Dental Savings Complete administration and Massachusetts note
atoms.q: Who administers Dental Savings Complete?
atoms.text: Dental Savings Complete is administered by Dental Benefit Providers, Inc. of Columbia, Maryland, which is also the Discount Plan Organization. UnitedHealthcare notes that the product does not meet the minimum creditable coverage requirements under Massachusetts law (MGL c.111M and 956 CMR 5.00). Questions can be directed to 1-888-578-8535.
qs: Does Dental Savings Complete count as minimum creditable coverage in Massachusetts?
Who runs Dental Savings Complete?

atoms.title: What fixed benefit health insurance is
atoms.q: What is fixed benefit health insurance?
atoms.text: Fixed benefit health insurance, sometimes referred to as hospital and doctor fixed indemnity insurance, pays a preset amount to the policyholder or the provider for specific covered medical services. It is also sometimes called indemnity insurance or fee for service insurance. The benefit stays the same no matter what the total bill was and no matter what other insurance pays.
qs: What is a fixed indemnity plan?
How do fixed benefit health plans pay?
Is fixed indemnity the same as fee for service insurance?

atoms.title: Why buy fixed benefit health insurance
atoms.q: Why would I buy fixed benefit health insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says unexpected medical bills can disrupt even the most stable household budgets. Fixed benefit health insurance can help ensure extra medical costs do not come with extra worries. The plans are designed to give traditional health insurance a boost by paying a preset payment when a person receives a qualified medical service specified in the plan.
qs: Is fixed benefit health insurance worth it?
How does fixed benefit insurance help with medical bills?

atoms.title: How fixed benefit plans pay benefits
atoms.q: How do I use a fixed benefit health plan?
atoms.text: To use benefits: the policyholder or provider submits a covered expense, and the fixed benefit for that service is paid no matter what other insurance coverage the person has. No deductible has to be met before benefits are received. The plan lets members choose their doctor or health facility.
qs: Do I have to meet a deductible for a fixed benefit plan?
How do I get paid by a fixed benefit plan?
Does fixed benefit insurance pay if my health plan also pays?

atoms.title: Provider choice and year-round enrollment
atoms.q: Can I choose any doctor and apply any time with fixed benefit insurance?
atoms.text: With a fixed benefit plan, a person can go to any doctor or health care facility they want. They may save money with discounted rates for services if they use providers in the plan's network, which varies by state. Applications can be made year-round, not just during an enrollment period or because of special circumstances.
qs: Can I buy fixed benefit insurance outside open enrollment?
Do I have to use network doctors with a fixed benefit plan?

atoms.title: Is fixed benefit insurance an ACA plan
atoms.q: Is fixed benefit health insurance an Affordable Care Act (ACA) plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that fixed benefit health insurance provides limited benefits and is a supplement to health insurance, not a substitute for the minimum essential coverage required by the ACA. Lack of major medical coverage may result in an additional payment with taxes. This fixed indemnity product provides benefits in a stated amount regardless of the actual expenses incurred.
qs: Does a fixed benefit plan meet ACA requirements?
Will I be penalized for only having fixed indemnity insurance?

atoms.title: Network note for people with major medical plans
atoms.q: Should I consider my medical plan's network when using a fixed benefit plan?
atoms.text: A footnote on UnitedHealthcare's page says that people with a major medical plan may need to stay with certain networks and providers to get the most coverage out of that plan. They should take that into consideration when choosing where they get care, even though a fixed benefit plan lets them go to any doctor or facility.
qs: Can I see out-of-network doctors with a fixed benefit plan?
Does fixed benefit insurance change how I use my health plan?

atoms.title: Fixed benefit plan details to check in the brochure
atoms.q: What limits apply to fixed benefit plan benefits?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare notes that some benefits increase the longer a person has the plan. Some plans may have waiting periods for wellness or preventive services. Intensive care or critical care hospitalization benefits are subject to a maximum number of days per confinement, and if more than one surgery occurs in a day, the highest tiered amount is paid. A drug discount card, where included, is for prescription discounts only and is not insurance.
qs: Is there a waiting period for wellness visits on a fixed benefit plan?
Does fixed benefit insurance include a prescription discount card?
Is the ICU benefit limited by days?

atoms.title: Fixed benefit plan contact and shopping options
atoms.q: How do I shop for fixed benefit health insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lets shoppers view fixed benefit health insurance plans by state using a ZIP code. Shoppers can also call 1-877-914-3210 with questions. The page also offers a video, titled as a way to learn more about fixed benefit health insurance, and links to other supplemental plans such as dental, vision and cash-benefit plans.
qs: How do I buy a fixed benefit plan?
Is there a phone number for fixed benefit health insurance?

atoms.title: What hospital indemnity insurance is
atoms.q: What is hospital indemnity insurance?
atoms.text: Hospital indemnity insurance is also called hospitalization insurance or hospital insurance. These plans pay the policyholder or the provider benefits when care requires a stay in a hospital, whether planned or unplanned, or for other covered medical services depending on the policy. They offer coverage options designed to help manage the financial impact of a hospital stay.
qs: What is hospital indemnity insurance?
What does hospitalization insurance pay for?
Is hospital insurance the same as hospital indemnity?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare hospital insurance plans
atoms.q: Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare hospital insurance?
atoms.text: Hospital insurance plans from UnitedHealthcare are hospital indemnity plans underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company. They pay a fixed benefit for covered medical expenses and include a range of options designed to help prepare a budget for unexpected costs related to a hospital stay. People can call 1-866-487-9299 to learn about plans in their state.
qs: Who offers hospital indemnity plans?
What number do I call about hospital insurance plans?

atoms.title: Nearly 34 million hospital admissions each year
atoms.q: How many people are admitted to hospitals each year?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare cites the American Hospital Association's Fast Facts on U.S. Hospitals 2024 in stating that nearly 34 million patients are admitted to the hospital each year. The page presents hospital indemnity insurance as a way to help prepare a budget in the event a hospital stay happens to a person or their family.
qs: How common are hospital stays?
Why buy hospital indemnity insurance?

atoms.title: How a hospital indemnity plan adds to medical coverage
atoms.q: How does hospital indemnity insurance supplement my medical plan?
atoms.text: A hospital indemnity plan can add to medical coverage by providing a cash benefit to help cover expenses related to a hospital stay. Medical costs can quickly add up when care in a hospital setting is needed. The page lists example expenses the cash benefit can help cover.
qs: What costs does a hospital indemnity plan help with?
Does hospital insurance work with my health insurance?

atoms.title: How to use hospital indemnity benefits
atoms.q: How do I claim a hospital indemnity benefit?
atoms.text: To access benefits: 1) Complete a claim form. 2) Submit the claim form along with any other required information for covered items, checking plan details for specific coverage. 3) Receive a benefit check to use as you see fit. With some plans, there may be an option to receive a discount on covered services if you use certain providers and have the plan pay that provider directly.
qs: How do I file a hospital indemnity claim?
How do I get paid from hospital insurance?
Can the plan pay my hospital directly?

atoms.title: Lump-sum payment and calendar-year maximums
atoms.q: How are hospital indemnity benefits paid?
atoms.text: Hospital indemnity benefits are paid in a lump sum directly to the policyholder or to the provider. Amounts are fixed and determined by the policy, regardless of the amount of expenses incurred. A footnote adds that benefits may be paid directly to the hospital or other health care facility if the policyholder makes an assignment of benefits, within calendar-year maximums.
qs: Does hospital indemnity insurance pay me or the hospital?
Does hospital insurance pay based on my actual bill?

atoms.title: Hospital insurance has no network limits
atoms.q: Do I have to stay in network to use hospital indemnity benefits?
atoms.text: A footnote on UnitedHealthcare's hospital insurance page states there are no network limitations for UnitedHealthcare branded hospital insurance plans, but a person may be bound to certain networks and providers with their major medical plan.
qs: Do I need to stay in network for hospital insurance benefits?
Can I go to any hospital with hospital indemnity coverage?

atoms.title: What combining insurance plans means
atoms.q: What does it mean to combine or bundle insurance plans?
atoms.text: Grouping health insurance, sometimes called bundling plans, means finding plans that work together so a person has coverage for the care they need. In addition to medical insurance, a person might consider a combination of supplemental insurance, including dental insurance, vision insurance, fixed indemnity insurance (also called fixed benefit health insurance), accident insurance and more.
qs: What is bundling health insurance?
Can I combine dental, vision and accident plans?

atoms.title: How to shop for plans that work together
atoms.q: How do I choose health plans that work well together?
atoms.text: When shopping for plans, first consider all the insurance plans you already have, if any. Then think about your needs by considering the kind of out-of-pocket health expenses you have had in the past, as well as any supplemental plans you may want, such as international travel coverage.
qs: How do I decide which supplemental plans to buy?
What should I consider before adding insurance plans?

atoms.title: Why add other plans to your coverage
atoms.q: Why add supplemental plans to my main coverage?
atoms.text: Additional plans can round out coverage to include benefits for services such as routine doctor visits, hospitalization, dental, vision and accidental injuries, helping cover some out-of-pocket costs that main insurance may not cover. A person might also pay less for common health costs like dental visits or eye care than paying out of pocket without insurance. Memberships, like dental savings memberships, are an alternative to insurance.
qs: Why would I need more than a medical plan?
Can supplemental plans lower what I pay for dental and eye care?

atoms.title: Benefits of combining different plan types
atoms.q: What are the benefits of combining insurance plans?
atoms.text: By combining different types of plans, a person is likely to have access to a larger range of services, quality care without being limited by cost, and more preventive care, which can help detect issues earlier. It can also help reduce costs related to emergency care and unexpected events. UnitedHealthcare adds that it is typically simpler and more convenient to manage policies in one place.
qs: Is it easier to manage multiple plans in one place?
How does combining plans help with costs?

atoms.title: Short term health plus dental pairing
atoms.q: Does short term health insurance pair well with dental insurance?
atoms.text: Short-term limited duration insurance can fill a temporary gap in medical coverage until a long-term solution is found. Dental insurance covers common dental care. Together, UnitedHealthcare says, a person can find medical care and keep teeth healthy, which is important for overall health. Short term health insurance does not qualify as minimum essential coverage under the ACA, is medically underwritten and does not cover preexisting conditions.
qs: Can I buy dental with short term health insurance?
Does short term insurance cover preexisting conditions?

atoms.title: ACA marketplace plan plus fixed benefit insurance
atoms.q: Can fixed benefit insurance help before I meet my ACA plan deductible?
atoms.text: Fixed benefit health insurance, a type of fixed indemnity insurance, can help a person worried about paying for healthcare until they meet the deductible on an ACA marketplace plan. When the plans are paired, the cash benefit from the fixed benefit plan can be used to help pay for qualified medical costs, even before the deductible is met, and it can also help pay for copays or coinsurance.
qs: How can I pay for care until I meet my deductible?
Can I use fixed benefit cash for copays and coinsurance?

atoms.title: TriTerm Medical plus dental pairing
atoms.q: What is TriTerm Medical and how does it pair with dental?
atoms.text: TriTerm Medical insurance is a type of short term health insurance available in select states that can last for nearly 3 years, giving time to find a more permanent healthcare solution. UnitedHealthcare suggests pairing it with a dental plan to provide healthcare coverage for the body and smile.
qs: What is TriTerm Medical insurance?
How long can TriTerm Medical last?

atoms.title: Fixed benefit health insurance plus vision
atoms.q: How do fixed benefit health insurance and vision insurance work together?
atoms.text: Fixed indemnity insurance, also known as fixed benefit health insurance, pays set cash benefit amounts for covered hospital and doctor expenses. Vision insurance provides coverage for routine eye exams and coverage for eyeglass lenses and frames. Combined, UnitedHealthcare says they help provide healthcare benefits for a person's unique health needs, covering out-of-pocket medical expenses and routine eye care.
qs: Should I combine vision with a fixed indemnity plan?
What does vision insurance cover for eyeglasses?

atoms.title: Dental plus vision with no maximum age limits
atoms.q: Are there dental and vision plans without age limits?
atoms.text: Dental and vision are some of the most common plans to complement medical coverage. UnitedHealthcare suggests considering dental and vision plans with no maximum age limits, which it says is ideal for people on Medicare or whose employer does not offer insurance. These plans provide benefits such as preventive eye care and dental exams. The primary insured must be 18 years of age or older.
qs: Can I get dental and vision if I'm on Medicare?
Is there a maximum age for dental and vision plans?

atoms.title: Accident insurance plus dental pairing
atoms.q: Why pair accident insurance with dental insurance?
atoms.text: Accident insurance provides coverage for accidental injuries. Dental insurance covers cleanings and X-rays that may offset more expensive problems. UnitedHealthcare says that with these plans a person can stay on top of regular dental care while adding some help for the unexpected.
qs: Is accident plus dental a good combination?
What does dental insurance cover that accident insurance doesn't?

atoms.title: Short-term health plus mental health virtual therapy
atoms.q: Can I pair a short-term plan with virtual therapy?
atoms.text: A short-term health plan offers temporary coverage while waiting for main insurance to start. UnitedHealthcare suggests pairing it with a mental health virtual therapy membership, a Teladoc Health service that is not insurance, so a person can take steps to keep body and mind healthy. A membership for unlimited virtual therapy means a person can access mental health care without insurance.
qs: Can I get therapy without insurance while on short-term coverage?
What is mental health virtual therapy membership?

atoms.title: Underwriters and separate applications for bundled plans
atoms.q: Do I apply separately for each plan when bundling?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare states that Short Term Medical, Health ProtectorGuard, Dental, Vision and Accident plans are underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company. All products require separate applications, and separate policies or certificates are issued. Each company is a separate entity and is not responsible for another's financial or contractual obligations.
qs: Do I need separate applications for dental and vision?
Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare short term and dental plans?

atoms.title: Mind Your Health virtual therapy overview and price
atoms.q: What is Mind Your Health virtual therapy and what does it cost?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health, provided by Teladoc Health, offers access to unlimited online therapy with licensed professionals for $169.99 per month, as mental health care without insurance. UnitedHealthcare says virtual therapy is a great option for people seeking flexible, convenient mental health care. There is a 72-hour wait to access the membership, and members must be 18 or older.
qs: How much does Mind Your Health cost?
Can I get therapy without insurance?
Who provides Mind Your Health?

atoms.title: Mind Your Health is not insurance
atoms.q: Is Mind Your Health insurance?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health is not health insurance, and members are encouraged to maintain adequate insurance from a responsible provider. It is designed to complement, and not replace, the care received from a primary care physician. Mind Your Health by Teladoc Health and UnitedHealthcare are not affiliated, and each entity is responsible for its own contractual and financial obligations.
qs: Is virtual therapy covered by insurance?
Does Mind Your Health replace my primary care doctor?

atoms.title: What Mind Your Health gives members access to
atoms.q: What does Mind Your Health include?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health offers access to a range of virtual therapists, mental health resources and digital tools. A member's personalized plan could include a mix of telehealth therapy, coaching and online content, plus self-guided tools and activities to work on between sessions. Therapists create the personalized plans based on the member's goals.
qs: What kind of therapy does Mind Your Health offer?
Does Mind Your Health include coaching?

atoms.title: Common issues Mind Your Health providers treat
atoms.q: What mental health issues can Mind Your Health help with?
atoms.text: Common issues that Mind Your Health providers treat include anxiety and stress, depression and negative thought patterns, feeling overwhelmed, not feeling like yourself, sleep issues, relationship conflicts, trauma and PTSD, mood swings, and medication management by virtual psychiatrists.
qs: Can I get therapy for anxiety online?
Does virtual therapy help with depression or trauma?
Can I get medication management through virtual care?

atoms.title: How to schedule a Mind Your Health visit
atoms.q: How do I set up therapy sessions with Mind Your Health?
atoms.text: Once enrolled in Mind Your Health, setting up therapy sessions takes a few steps. 1) Set up an account and answer a few brief questions about preferences and needs. 2) Choose a therapist and pick the dates and times that work best. 3) Meet online at the confirmed time to start the visit.
qs: How do I book a virtual therapy appointment?
Can I choose my own therapist in Mind Your Health?

atoms.title: Eligibility and availability limits for Mind Your Health
atoms.q: Who can use Mind Your Health and when are visits available?
atoms.text: Members must be 18 years or older, and mental health visits are not available to minors. There is a 72-hour wait to access the membership. Mental health visits are scheduled rather than available 24/7, all mental health specialists may not be available in all states, and the service may not be available in certain states.
qs: Can minors use Mind Your Health?
Is Mind Your Health available in every state?
Is there a waiting period for Mind Your Health?

atoms.title: Prescribing limits for Mind Your Health providers
atoms.q: Can Mind Your Health providers prescribe medication?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health physicians are an independent network of doctors who advise, diagnose and prescribe at their own discretion. They do not prescribe DEA controlled substances, nontherapeutic drugs and certain other drugs that may be harmful because of their potential for abuse. Mind Your Health does not guarantee that a prescription will be written.
qs: Can virtual therapists prescribe controlled substances?
Will I get a prescription from Mind Your Health?

atoms.title: Mind Your Health is not for crisis situations
atoms.q: Where do I go for a mental health crisis?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health virtual therapy is not designed to help in a crisis situation. People in crisis should seek help immediately: call or text 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, for emotional distress or suicidal thoughts, or call 911 for immediate, life-threatening needs, including medical crisis, fire, crime or natural disasters.
qs: Who do I call in a mental health crisis?
Is virtual therapy for emergencies?
What is 988?

atoms.title: Resources for existing UnitedHealthcare members
atoms.q: Where can UnitedHealthcare members find mental health programs?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health is offered as mental health care without insurance. For current UnitedHealthcare members, the page directs them to the company's mental health programs and services page. People who want to speak with a licensed insurance agent about membership options can call 888-578-8535.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare have mental health programs for members?
How do I speak to an agent about Mind Your Health?

atoms.title: What term life insurance is
atoms.q: What is term life insurance?
atoms.text: Term life insurance is a life insurance policy that pays cash benefits to help loved ones in the event of the policyholder's death. Term life policies from Golden Rule Insurance Company also feature an optional Critical Illness Benefit that pays cash benefits upon diagnosis of a qualifying illness.
qs: What is term life insurance?
Does term life insurance include critical illness coverage?

atoms.title: How term life insurance works
atoms.q: How does term life insurance pay out?
atoms.text: Term life insurance pays designated beneficiaries a lump sum if the policyholder dies within the selected policy term. If an optional Critical Illness Benefit is added and the policyholder is diagnosed with a qualifying illness, a cash benefit is paid to the policyholder according to the policy terms and can be used as wished. The amount paid from the Critical Illness Benefit is subtracted from the term life policy benefit.
qs: Who gets the money from a term life policy?
Does a critical illness payout reduce my life insurance benefit?

atoms.title: How beneficiaries can use term life benefits
atoms.q: What can my beneficiaries do with a term life payout?
atoms.text: When a person chooses a term life insurance plan, the policy benefits are paid to the beneficiary or beneficiaries, who can use the payment as they wish. The page lists example expenses the payment can help with. UnitedHealthcare describes the plan as designed to help protect a family's finances.
qs: How is term life money used by a family?
Do beneficiaries have restrictions on how to spend the benefit?

atoms.title: Qualifying illnesses for the Critical Illness Benefit
atoms.q: Which illnesses qualify for the term life Critical Illness Benefit?
atoms.text: With term life coverage from Golden Rule Insurance Company, a person can add a Critical Illness Benefit that pays a cash benefit upon diagnosis of a qualifying illness: heart attack, life-threatening cancer, loss of hearing, speech or vision, major organ transplant, paralysis, coma, renal failure, stroke, carcinoma in situ or coronary artery bypass graft. Waiting periods may apply, and the optional benefit requires an additional premium.
qs: What illnesses does the term life critical illness rider cover?
Does the term life critical illness benefit cost extra?

atoms.title: Reasons to choose UnitedHealthcare term life
atoms.q: What are the features of UnitedHealthcare term life insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists four features: a lump-sum benefit paid upon the policyholder's death; no medical exam required (the product is medically underwritten); multiple terms and benefit levels to choose from; and coverage available until age 75. Products vary by state.
qs: Does term life insurance require a medical exam?
Until what age can I have term life coverage?
Can I choose a term length and benefit amount?

atoms.title: Continuing term life coverage up to age 75
atoms.q: What happens when my term life policy term ends?
atoms.text: A footnote on UnitedHealthcare's term life page states that after the initial term, the coverage can be continued on a year-by-year basis up to age 75. Evidence of insurability is not required, but the premium rate will increase each year.
qs: Can I renew term life insurance after the term ends?
Does term life premium go up each year after the initial term?

atoms.title: Do I need life insurance
atoms.q: Do I need life insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare says that if a person has a family, having a term life insurance plan may be an important way to help keep the family secure. Having a term life policy is a way to help provide financial support to loved ones if the policyholder unexpectedly dies. The page asks readers whether their family would be financially secure in the event of their death.
qs: Should I buy term life insurance?
Why does my family need term life insurance?

atoms.title: Term life contact number and underwriter
atoms.q: How do I learn about UnitedHealthcare term life plans in my state?
atoms.text: Term life insurance from UnitedHealthcare is underwritten by Golden Rule Insurance Company. Shoppers can call 1-866-639-4610 to learn more about term life insurance plans in their state, and a plan finder is available to see which insurance options may be available.
qs: What number do I call for term life insurance?
Who underwrites UnitedHealthcare term life?

atoms.title: SafeTrip travel insurance overview
atoms.q: What is UnitedHealthcare Global SafeTrip travel insurance?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Global SafeTrip supports travelers with trip protection that helps manage unexpected interruptions, delays, cancellations and accidents, whether traveling internationally or within the United States. It can be paired with travel medical insurance, which supports health needs when outside the country.
qs: What is SafeTrip travel insurance?
Does UnitedHealthcare offer travel insurance?
Can I pair trip protection with travel medical insurance?

atoms.title: SafeTrip's three travel insurance plan types
atoms.q: What SafeTrip travel plans are available?
atoms.text: SafeTrip offers three plan types. International Travel Medical Plus combines international medical coverage and travel protection, including trip cancellation, interruption, delay and baggage coverage, plus medical and security assistance. International Travel Medical is emergency medical insurance for trips outside the United States, with up to $1 million for the medical expense limit and coverage for medical evacuation and medical assistance. Travel Protection is available for U.S. domestic travel only, with trip cancellation, interruption, delay and baggage coverage and full AD&D coverage.
qs: What is the difference between SafeTrip plans?
Which SafeTrip plan covers medical care abroad?
Is there a SafeTrip plan just for U.S. trips?

atoms.title: Extreme sports, equipment and rental car add-ons
atoms.q: What add-on coverage can I add to SafeTrip travel insurance?
atoms.text: SafeTrip travelers can add insurance for extreme sports coverage, sporting equipment delay or loss, and rental car damage. UnitedHealthcare describes this as special coverage for a special trip, and links to a dedicated page that explains the travel insurance add-ons.
qs: Can I add rental car coverage to travel insurance?
Does SafeTrip cover extreme sports?

atoms.title: What travel insurance is
atoms.q: What is travel insurance?
atoms.text: Travel insurance is coverage that eases worry when something goes wrong away from home, whether a person is traveling for fun, work, volunteering or another reason. UnitedHealthcare notes there is plenty that can go wrong away from home, and travel insurance lets travelers focus on the important things knowing they are covered.
qs: What does travel insurance do?
Why do I need travel insurance?

atoms.title: Four benefits of SafeTrip travel insurance
atoms.q: What benefits does SafeTrip travel insurance provide?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists four benefits. Protect your investment: reimbursement for expenses related to trip delays, cancellations and baggage loss. Get the care you deserve: staff can help find the right doctor easily and quickly. Stay covered abroad: international travel medical coverage can reimburse small medical costs or cover larger medical expenses. Enjoy 24/7 access to help: travelers can call the in-house Emergency Response Center (ERC) anytime.
qs: Is there 24/7 assistance with SafeTrip?
What does SafeTrip's Emergency Response Center do?

atoms.title: SafeTrip by the numbers
atoms.q: How large is SafeTrip's support and provider network?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare describes SafeTrip as offering around-the-clock support and a global provider network. Its page lists four figures for SafeTrip: 24/7 support, 150+ countries, 2.4 million+ providers and 45+ years of experience.
qs: How many countries does SafeTrip cover?
How many providers are in the SafeTrip network?
How long has SafeTrip been around?

atoms.title: SafeTrip resources and sales contact
atoms.q: How do I contact SafeTrip about a plan or group travel?
atoms.text: People with questions, who need help choosing a plan or who are covering a large group can contact the SafeTrip information and sales team toll free at 1-800-732-5309, internationally at 1-410-453-6380, or by email at safetrip_info@uhcglobal.com. The page also links to plan comparison, trip types, claims filing and a partner page.
qs: What is the SafeTrip phone number?
Who do I call to buy group travel insurance?

atoms.title: When to choose domestic versus international SafeTrip plans
atoms.q: Which SafeTrip plan type fits domestic or international trips?
atoms.text: Travel Protection plans are available for U.S. domestic travel only, while International Travel Medical and International Travel Medical Plus plans are meant for trips outside the United States. SafeTrip also directs readers to a plan comparison page and a trip types page to help decide which plan fits a journey.
qs: Do I need a different plan for travel inside the U.S.?
How do I choose a SafeTrip plan?

atoms.title: Extreme sports activities add-on
atoms.q: What does the SafeTrip extreme sports add-on cover?
atoms.text: The SafeTrip extreme sports add-on is for adrenaline seekers, such as people skydiving, parachuting, white-water rafting, paragliding or doing another adventure sport. The add-on covers accidents, injury and medical evacuation, so travelers can focus on the fun ahead.
qs: Does travel insurance cover skydiving or paragliding?
What does an extreme sports travel add-on include?

atoms.title: Sporting equipment loss and delay add-on
atoms.q: What does sporting equipment loss and delay coverage cover?
