atoms.title: Automatic Medicare enrollment at 65
atoms.q: Will I be enrolled in Medicare automatically at 65?
atoms.text: If you start receiving Social Security or Railroad Retirement Board benefits before you turn 65, you should be enrolled in Medicare automatically. If you are not enrolled automatically, you will need to sign up by yourself: online at www.ssa.gov, in person at your local Social Security office, or by phone at 1-800-772-1213 / TTY 1-800-325-0778. You may not be notified when you become eligible, so find your Initial Enrollment Period dates and put them in your calendar.

Am I automatically enrolled in Medicare?

atoms.title: Initial Enrollment Period at age 65
atoms.q: When does my Initial Enrollment Period start and end when I turn 65?
atoms.text: If you first become eligible for Medicare because you are turning 65, your Initial Enrollment Period (IEP) begins three months before the month of your 65th birthday and ends three months afterward. During your IEP, you can enroll in Original Medicare (Part A and/or Part B), a Medicare Advantage plan or a Part D prescription drug plan without penalty. Medicare Advantage plans may not be available in all states or territories.

atoms.title: General Enrollment Period (GEP)
atoms.q: What is the Medicare General Enrollment Period?
atoms.text: The General Enrollment Period (GEP) lets you enroll in Original Medicare Part B if you missed your Initial Enrollment Period and do not qualify for a Special Enrollment Period. If you don't qualify for premium-free Part A and missed your IEP, you can also buy Part A during this time. The GEP runs from January 1 to March 31, and when you enroll during it, your coverage starts the first day of the month after you sign up.

atoms.title: Special Enrollment Period triggers
atoms.q: What is a Medicare Special Enrollment Period?
atoms.text: A Special Enrollment Period (SEP) gives you a chance to change plans after certain life events, such as moving out of your plan's service area, your plan changing its contract with Medicare, losing your current health insurance including from your employer, having an opportunity to get other coverage from your employer or union, or being affected by a disaster or emergency.

atoms.title: Annual Enrollment Period (AEP)
atoms.q: When is the Medicare Annual Enrollment Period?
atoms.text: The Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) is the time each year when you can sign up for a Medicare Advantage plan, switch Medicare Advantage plans, or join or leave a Medicare Part D prescription drug plan. It begins October 15 and ends December 7. Changes made during AEP take effect the following January 1.

Can I switch Part D plans in October?

atoms.title: Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period
atoms.q: What is the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period?
atoms.text: The Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (OEP) is when you can switch from one Medicare Advantage plan to another, with or without drug coverage, or leave a Medicare Advantage plan and return to Original Medicare and enroll in a Part D prescription drug plan if you choose. It begins January 1 and ends March 31 every year.

atoms.title: Medicare enrollment with a disability
atoms.q: When can I enroll in Medicare if I have a disability or medical condition?
atoms.text: With a qualifying disability, you should become eligible for Medicare after you have received SSDI benefits for 24 months. Your 7-month Initial Enrollment Period will include your 25th month of disability, the 3 months before and the 3 months after. You may also qualify for Medicare due to Lou Gehrig's disease (ALS) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD), and your IEP may depend on your diagnosis.

atoms.title: Delaying Medicare while working past 65
atoms.q: Do I need Medicare if I work past age 65?
atoms.text: If you expect to continue working past age 65, you may want to delay enrolling in Medicare. If you have health coverage from your employer or are covered under a spouse's employer plan, you may qualify for a Special Enrollment Period and be able to delay enrolling without penalty. In some situations, such as working for an employer with fewer than 20 employees, you may still be required to take full Medicare benefits at age 65 even if you plan to keep working.

atoms.title: Enrolling later after delaying Medicare
atoms.q: If I delay Medicare now, how do I enroll later?
atoms.text: If you are eligible for Medicare, delay enrollment past age 65 and have health insurance through your employer, you can enroll later in a Special Enrollment Period (SEP) when you retire or lose coverage. During this 8-month period you can enroll in Original Medicare (Part A and/or Part B). You can also enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan or a Part D plan, but you only get the first 2 months of your SEP to do so without penalty.

atoms.title: Medicare and a spouse's insurance
atoms.q: Do I need Medicare if I am covered by my spouse's insurance?
atoms.text: If you have insurance through a spouse's employer, you may be able to delay enrollment in Medicare past age 65. This depends on the employer's rules for covered dependents of Medicare age. Talk with the employer's benefits administrator to learn what you can do about Medicare enrollment.

atoms.title: Medicare vs Social Security eligibility
atoms.q: Is Medicare eligibility the same as Social Security eligibility?
atoms.text: No. Medicare eligibility and benefits are separate from Social Security eligibility and benefits. You can enroll in Medicare at age 65 or with a qualifying disability or medical condition, while your Social Security eligibility depends on what year you were born, when you retire and other factors.

atoms.title: How Medicare enrollment affects your HSA
atoms.q: How will Medicare enrollment affect my Health Savings Account?
atoms.text: Once you enroll in Medicare Part A or Part B, you can no longer make pre-tax contributions to your HSA. If you receive Social Security benefits, Part A is generally automatic and coverage is retroactive for up to 6 months, so you should plan to stop contributing to your HSA about 6 months before enrolling. You can keep contributing if you are eligible for Medicare but have not enrolled, and after enrolling you can still withdraw HSA funds tax-free for some Medicare expenses and qualified medical expenses.

atoms.title: Medicare versus Medicaid
atoms.q: What is the difference between Medicare and Medicaid?
atoms.text: Medicare is a federal health insurance program intended to serve people who are 65 or older, or have a qualifying disability or medical condition. Medicaid is a joint federal and state government program that helps pay health care costs for people with limited income and resources, and Medicaid plans vary from state to state. You may qualify for both based on your health and income level, and people who are dual eligible can often qualify for a D-SNP.

atoms.title: Medicare and Medicaid eligibility requirements
atoms.q: How do I know if I'm eligible for Medicare and Medicaid?
atoms.text: To qualify for Medicare benefits you must be a U.S. citizen or have been a legal resident for at least five years, be 65 years old or have a qualifying disability if younger than 65, and have worked and paid Social Security taxes for at least 10 years (40 quarters). To qualify for Medicaid services you must have an income level within your state's income threshold, live within the state where you apply, have a Social Security number, and be a U.S. citizen or meet immigration requirements.

atoms.title: Copay, coinsurance and out-of-pocket limit
atoms.q: What is the difference between a copay, coinsurance and an out-of-pocket maximum in Medicare?
atoms.text: A copay is a set, flat amount paid each time, such as a $20 copay for each in-office doctor visit. Coinsurance requires you to pay a percentage of the Medicare-approved amount each time. An out-of-pocket limit is a maximum amount of out-of-pocket costs you pay per calendar year. Since Medicare Parts A and B don't have an out-of-pocket maximum, your out-of-pocket medical expenses can add up to hundreds or thousands per year.

atoms.title: How claims flow with Original Medicare and Medigap
atoms.q: How does a Medicare Supplement plan pay claims?
atoms.text: Original Medicare (Part A and Part B) generally pays about 80% of covered expenses, and you are responsible for the rest. When you receive covered care, your provider bills Original Medicare first. After Medicare pays its share, the provider bills the Medicare Supplement plan, which pays some or all of the rest after your Part B deductible is satisfied. The amount depends on the plan type you choose.
qs: Who pays first, Medicare or Medigap?
How much does Original Medicare pay?
How does a Medigap plan work with my doctor bills?

atoms.title: What Medicare Supplement plans do not cover
atoms.q: What do Medicare Supplement plans not cover?
atoms.text: In general, Original Medicare and Medicare Supplement plans don't cover long-term care, such as custodial care in a nursing home, or private-duty nursing services. They also do not cover routine vision, dental, hearing or prescription drugs, though some Medicare Supplement plans offer Wellness extras, which are discounts and additional services to help with these costs. Prescription drug coverage can be obtained separately through a standalone Part D plan (PDP).
qs: Does Medigap cover nursing home care?
Does Medigap cover dental or prescriptions?
What isn't covered by Medicare Supplement?

atoms.title: Benefits of choosing a Medicare Supplement plan
atoms.q: Why choose a Medicare Supplement plan?
atoms.text: With a Medicare Supplement plan you don't need to shop for or renew your plan each year. Benefits include more predictable out-of-pocket costs, the ability to choose any hospital or doctor that accepts Medicare, no prior authorizations or referrals, coverage anywhere in the United States, and a plan that can't be canceled because of your age, health or number of claims, as long as you pay premiums when due and make no material misrepresentation on your application.
qs: Do Medigap plans require referrals?
Can a Medicare Supplement plan be canceled if I get sick?
Can I see any doctor with Medigap?

atoms.title: AARP Medicare Supplement plans: UnitedHealthcare scale
atoms.q: How large is UnitedHealthcare's Medicare Supplement business?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare describes itself as the largest Medicare Supplement insurer nationwide, with more than 4 million insured members and 94% of members renewing their plan each year. Plans carrying the AARP name are endorsed by AARP, and some include Wellness extras like dental, hearing and vision discounts plus gym memberships.
qs: How many people have AARP Medicare Supplement plans?
What percent of members renew their Medigap plan?
Who is the largest Medigap insurer?

atoms.title: Medigap plan letters are standardized by state
atoms.q: Are Medicare Supplement plans the same across insurers?
atoms.text: All Medicare Supplement plans are offered by private insurance companies and regulated by federal and state governments. In most states plans are named with letters, such as Plan A and Plan B, and plans with the same name have the same coverage no matter which company you choose. Not all plans are available in all states. In some states you may also choose a Medicare Select or high-deductible plan, and Massachusetts, Minnesota and Wisconsin have their own standardized plans.
qs: Is Plan G the same at every insurance company?
Why are Medigap plans labeled with letters?
Which states have different Medigap plans?

atoms.title: Plan A, B and G benefits compared
atoms.q: How do Medicare Supplement Plans A, B and G compare?
atoms.text: Plan A is the basic benefits plan: Part A inpatient hospital deductible $1,736, annual Part B deductible $283, Part B excess charges not covered. Plan B adds coverage of the Part A deductible ($0). Plan G is the comprehensive plan: Part A deductible $0, Part B deductible $283, Part B excess charges covered, and foreign travel emergency covered at 20% after a $250 annual deductible with a $50,000 lifetime maximum. All three list $0 for primary care, specialist, urgent care and emergency visits.
qs: What is the difference between Plan A and Plan G?
Does Plan G cover Part B excess charges?
Which Medigap plans cover the Part A deductible?

atoms.title: Plan K, L and N cost-sharing plans
atoms.q: How do Medicare Supplement Plans K, L and N work?
atoms.text: Plan K is the lower premium 50% benefits plan, covering 50% of the Part A inpatient hospital deductible (listed as $868) with 10% coinsurance for primary care, specialist, urgent care and emergency visits. Plan L is the lower premium 75% benefits plan, covering 25% of the Part A deductible ($434) with 5% coinsurance. Plan N is the copay plan, with up to a $20 copay for primary care and specialist visits and up to a $50 emergency care copay; its Part A deductible is $0 and it does not cover Part B excess charges.
qs: What copays does Plan N have?
What is Medigap Plan K?
Which Medigap plans have lower premiums?

atoms.title: Plans C and F are limited to older enrollees
atoms.q: Can I still buy Medicare Supplement Plan C or Plan F?
atoms.text: Plan C and Plan F are only available to those first eligible for Medicare before 2020. Medicare Supplement plans sold to people new to Medicare on or after January 1, 2020, don't cover the Part B deductible. Plan G provides the same benefits as Plan C and Plan F, except for Part B deductible coverage. Plan C and Plan F list a $0 Part B deductible, and Plan F also covers Part B excess charges.
qs: Is Plan F still available?
Why can't new Medicare enrollees buy Plan C or F?
What is the Plan G alternative to Plan F?

atoms.title: Medigap costs: premium, deductible, copay
atoms.q: What costs come with a Medicare Supplement plan?
atoms.text: Medicare Supplement plan costs can include a monthly premium, which varies by insurance company and can change yearly; a deductible, with Medicare deductible amounts set by the federal government; and a copayment or coinsurance on some plans, though many do not have one. Original Medicare doesn't have an out-of-pocket maximum, while Medicare Supplement plans have predictable costs that help you stay ahead of unexpected out-of-pocket expenses.
qs: How much does a Medigap plan cost?
Does Original Medicare have an out-of-pocket maximum?
Do Medigap premiums change every year?

atoms.title: When to apply for a Medicare Supplement plan
atoms.q: When can I apply for a Medicare Supplement plan?
atoms.text: The best time to buy a Medicare Supplement plan is during your six-month Medigap Open Enrollment Period (OEP), which starts the first day of the month in which you are age 65 or older and enrolled in Part B. During this time you are guaranteed acceptance, meaning you have a right to buy any Medicare Supplement plan sold in your state. Your plan starts on the first day of the month after your application is approved and your first payment is received, or on a later month you select.
qs: When is the best time to buy Medigap?
What is the Medigap open enrollment period?
When does my Medicare Supplement plan start?

atoms.title: How to apply for a Medicare Supplement plan
atoms.q: How do I apply for a Medicare Supplement plan?
atoms.text: You can apply for a plan online, by phone at 1-833-591-5020 / TTY 711 or with an agent. You'll need: 1) information from your Medicare card, if you have one; 2) other insurance provider information, if applicable, such as current employer insurance, Medicaid or other Medicare Supplement coverage; and 3) your AARP membership number. You must be an AARP member to enroll in an AARP Medicare Supplement Insurance plan.
qs: What do I need to apply for Medigap?
Do I need AARP membership for AARP Medicare Supplement?
Can I apply for a Medicare Supplement plan online?

atoms.title: What a Medicare Part D plan is
atoms.q: What is a Medicare Part D plan?
atoms.text: A Part D plan is private insurance that offers prescription drug coverage. You can get a Part D plan by itself (PDP) to work with Original Medicare, or as part of a Medicare Advantage plan (MAPD).
qs: What is Part D?
What does PDP stand for?
Can I get drug coverage inside a Medicare Advantage plan?

atoms.title: Benefits common to UnitedHealthcare Part D plans
atoms.q: What benefits do UnitedHealthcare Part D plans include?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers prescription drug coverage through standalone plans (PDP) and as part of most Medicare Advantage plans (MAPD). All of them have these benefits: most Part D covered adult vaccines have a $0 copay, including the shingles vaccine; all Part D covered drugs have a $0 cost share in the Catastrophic Coverage stage; and a 1-month supply of covered insulin costs no more than $35. Members also have access to more than 60,000 pharmacies and can have prescriptions sent from Optum Home Delivery Pharmacy.
qs: Is the shingles vaccine free with Part D?
What is the most I pay for insulin on a Part D plan?
How many pharmacies accept UnitedHealthcare Part D?

atoms.title: Who is eligible for a Part D plan
atoms.q: Who is eligible for a Medicare Part D plan?
atoms.text: Most people become eligible for Medicare coverage when they turn 65 or have a qualifying disability or medical condition. Anyone who has Medicare Part A, Part B or both is eligible to enroll in a prescription drug plan if they live in the plan service area.
qs: Do I need Part A or B to get a Part D plan?
Who can enroll in Part D?
Can I get Part D if I'm under 65?

atoms.title: What Part D plans cover
atoms.q: What do Part D plans cover?
atoms.text: Part D plans cover drugs on the plan's drug list (formulary) and most vaccines not covered by Medicare Part B. Original Medicare and Medicare Supplement (Medigap) insurance plans do not cover prescription drugs, but most Medicare Advantage plans do.
qs: Does Original Medicare cover prescription drugs?
What is a formulary?
Does Medigap cover medications?

atoms.title: What Part D plans generally don't cover
atoms.q: What drugs are not covered by Part D?
atoms.text: Part D plans generally don't cover drugs prescribed for anorexia, weight loss, weight gain, fertility, erectile dysfunction, cosmetic purposes or hair growth. They also don't cover prescription vitamins and minerals, non-prescription drugs, or drugs already covered by Medicare Part A and Part B.
qs: Does Part D cover weight loss medication?
Are over-the-counter drugs covered by Part D?
What isn't covered by a Medicare drug plan?

atoms.title: When you can enroll in a Part D plan
atoms.q: When can I enroll in a Medicare Part D plan?
atoms.text: You can enroll when you first become eligible for Medicare, during your Initial Enrollment Period (IEP). If you already have Medicare coverage, you can add, drop or change Part D coverage during the Annual Enrollment Period (AEP), October 15 to December 7, or during a Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for qualifying life events, with dates that vary.
qs: When can I change my Part D plan?
When is Medicare open enrollment for drug plans?
Can I add Part D outside of AEP?

atoms.title: Working past 65 and the Part D penalty
atoms.q: What happens to Part D if I work past age 65?
atoms.text: If you choose to work past 65 and delay Part D enrollment, you may be subject to a Part D late enrollment penalty. You can avoid this penalty if you can show that you have creditable coverage equal to or better than a Part D plan.
qs: Will I be penalized for delaying Part D if I'm still working?
What is creditable coverage?
How do I avoid the Part D late penalty?

atoms.title: AARP Medicare Rx Preferred vs Rx Saver
atoms.q: How do AARP Medicare Rx Preferred and Rx Saver differ?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers two Part D plans; availability may depend on where you live. AARP Medicare Rx Preferred has a $130 annual deductible for drugs in tiers 3, 4 and 5, a national and U.S. Territories service area, a Premium drug list, and a $0 copay at Optum Home Delivery for a 90-day supply of Tier 1 and 2 drugs. AARP Medicare Rx Saver has a $615 annual deductible, a national service area, a Standard drug list, and a $6 copay for a 90-day supply of Tier 1 generics at Optum Home Delivery. Rx Saver is suggested for people who receive Extra Help or want a robust pharmacy network.
qs: What is the difference between Rx Preferred and Rx Saver?
Which UnitedHealthcare Part D plan has the lower deductible?
What is the home delivery copay for AARP Medicare Rx Saver?

atoms.title: 2026 Part D deductible limit is $615
atoms.q: What is the Part D deductible limit for 2026?
atoms.text: Standalone Part D plans charge a monthly premium and may also have an annual deductible, copays and coinsurance. For plans with an annual deductible, the 2026 limit set by Medicare is $615.
qs: What's the maximum Part D deductible in 2026?
Do Part D plans have deductibles?
How much does a standalone Part D plan cost?

atoms.title: Part D cost sharing: copay and coinsurance
atoms.q: How does cost sharing work for Part D prescriptions?
atoms.text: When you fill a prescription for a covered drug, you may need to pay a copayment (a set amount) or coinsurance (a percentage). Amounts vary based on what tier the drug is in and what pharmacy you use. Total costs also vary with the number of prescription drugs you need, how often you take them, whether you use a network pharmacy and what coverage stage you are in. Your costs may be lower if you qualify for the Extra Help program.
qs: How much will I pay for a prescription under Part D?
What are drug tiers?
Does Extra Help lower prescription costs?

atoms.title: The Part D coverage stages
atoms.q: What are the Part D coverage stages?
atoms.text: Part D costs depend on the coverage stage. In the Deductible stage, if your plan has one, you pay the full cost of your prescriptions. In the Initial Coverage stage, you pay a copay or coinsurance. In the Catastrophic Coverage stage, the plan pays the full amount for Medicare covered Part D drugs.
qs: What is the catastrophic coverage stage?
What are the stages of Part D coverage?
When do I stop paying for drugs under Part D?

atoms.title: What UnitedHealthcare member resources offer
atoms.q: What are UnitedHealthcare member resources?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare member resources are tools and programs offered through a member's health plan to help them make the most of their benefits. Members can use them to find providers, review benefits or explore member programs. Some resources vary by plan and area and may not be available for all plans.
qs: What resources do UnitedHealthcare members get?
How do I make the most of my UnitedHealthcare benefits?

atoms.title: What you can do on the member site
atoms.q: What can I do once I register for a UnitedHealthcare member account?
atoms.text: Once a person registers for a UnitedHealthcare member account, they can use the member site to search for network providers, manage prescriptions, view plan spending, find copays and more.
qs: What can I do with a UnitedHealthcare member account?
Why should I register on the member site?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare app: always-there plan access
atoms.q: What does the UnitedHealthcare app let me do?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare app connects members to their health plan details anytime, anywhere. Members can use it to find care and pricing, refill prescriptions, access their health plan ID cards and more. The app also offers instant access to see prescriptions and find pharmacies.
qs: What can I do in the UHC app?
Can I refill prescriptions in the UnitedHealthcare app?

atoms.title: Tools for using your plan day to day
atoms.q: What tools help me use my health plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists five tools under How to use your plan: the member ID card, how to submit a claim, how to pay your bills, member forms, and UHC Store for members. They are meant to help members submit a claim, access important forms or manage a member ID card.
qs: Where do I find member forms?
How do I manage my UnitedHealthcare member ID card?
Where do I learn how to pay my UnitedHealthcare bills?

atoms.title: UHC Store for members
atoms.q: What is UHC Store?
atoms.text: UHC Store is an online shopping experience available to UnitedHealthcare members with employer-sponsored health plans. It gives members member-exclusive access to health and wellness offerings they can purchase, many at a discount.
qs: What is the UHC Store?
Can I buy health and wellness products through my UnitedHealthcare plan?

atoms.title: Finding care resources for members
atoms.q: What help does UnitedHealthcare offer for finding care?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers resources to help members make informed decisions about care: choosing a doctor (including dentists, mental health providers and eye doctors), wellness and member programs, mental health programs, guidance on where to go for medical care, telehealth and virtual care, and pharmacy benefits including Prescription Drug Lists (PDLs).
qs: How do I find the right doctor on my plan?
Where do I learn about telehealth and pharmacy benefits?

atoms.title: Wellness and member support programs
atoms.q: What wellness and support programs does UnitedHealthcare list for members?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's wellness, rewards and member programs include support for smoking cessation, weight management, clinical and maternity programs, as well as LGBTQ+ resources. Mental and behavioral health benefits are listed separately, including the Employee Assistance Program and the Substance Use Helpline.
qs: What wellness programs does UnitedHealthcare have?
Does UnitedHealthcare help with quitting smoking or losing weight?

atoms.title: Medicare Advantage member resources
atoms.q: Where do Medicare Advantage members find their resources?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage members have a dedicated set of member resources, with featured pages for UCard, over-the-counter (OTC) benefits and transportation benefits, plus a page to view all member resources for Medicare Advantage plans.
qs: Where are Medicare Advantage member resources?
What is UCard for Medicare Advantage members?

atoms.title: Chatting with customer service as a member
atoms.q: How can a UnitedHealthcare member chat with customer service?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare members can use the UnitedHealthcare app or sign in to their member account to chat directly with customer service, find answers and complete tasks online. A Contact us page offers additional ways to reach UnitedHealthcare.
qs: How do I chat with UnitedHealthcare customer service?
How can I contact UnitedHealthcare as a member?

atoms.title: Member ID card questions covered on the hub
atoms.q: What can I do before I receive my member ID card or if I lose it?
atoms.text: The member resources page includes answers for new members who have not yet received a member ID card and for members who cannot find their card or do not have it with them. It points members to the Member ID card page, which explains how to use the card and how to view it in the UnitedHealthcare app.
qs: What if I can't find my member ID card?
Can I use my insurance before my ID card arrives?

atoms.title: Network providers lower costs
atoms.q: Why should I choose a network provider?
atoms.text: Choosing a network provider may help lower costs. Most plans charge more if you see an out-of-network provider, and some will not cover out-of-network care at all. To see if a primary care provider is in your network, view UnitedHealthcare network providers in your member account or browse a provider list.
qs: Why does network matter?
How do I check if a doctor is in network?

atoms.title: Why you need a primary care provider
atoms.q: Why do I need a primary care provider?
atoms.text: Some health plans require you to choose a primary care provider (PCP), and while others do not, it may be a good idea to have one. A PCP can guide you through your care and, as they get to know you, may watch for small changes in your health to help spot warning signs of potential health concerns earlier. Your PCP may also save you money with fewer ER visits, can connect you with specialists and can advocate for you.
qs: Do I need a PCP?
What does a primary care provider do?

atoms.title: Seeing a specialist without a referral
atoms.q: Can I see a specialist without a referral?
atoms.text: Whether you need a referral often depends on your health plan and the specialist's office. With certain plans you can make appointments with a specialist on your own, while other plans may need a referral from a PCP before the visit is covered. If you are not sure, check your plan details or call the specialist's office before you schedule.
qs: Do I need a referral to see a specialist?
How do I know if my plan requires referrals?

atoms.title: Types of primary care providers
atoms.q: What types of primary care providers are there?
atoms.text: Each family member may need a different PCP. A family medicine doctor provides preventive and whole-person care for patients of all ages. An OB/GYN specializes in women's health, including family planning, pregnancy and menopause. A pediatrician serves patients from newborn to 18 years old. An internist treats adults 18 and older. A geriatrician focuses on medical conditions related to aging in older adults aged 60 and up.
qs: What is the difference between a family doctor and an internist?
What does a geriatrician do?

atoms.title: Board certification
atoms.q: How can I check whether a doctor is board certified?
atoms.text: Board certification is a sign of going above and beyond state licensing requirements and receiving supervised in-practice training. To find a board-certified family doctor, you can visit the American Board of Family Medicine online directory, and to check whether a physician is board-certified you can use the American Board of Medical Specialties' Certification Matters database.
qs: What does board certified mean?
How do I verify a doctor's credentials?

atoms.title: Mental and behavioral health provider types
atoms.q: What kinds of mental health providers are there?
atoms.text: Many types of providers can support your mental health, and some people benefit from seeing a combination of mental health professionals. These may include social workers, counselors or therapists, psychiatrists and psychologists. UnitedHealthcare offers a separate guide to choosing a mental health provider.
qs: What is the difference between a psychologist and a psychiatrist?
Who should I see for mental health?

atoms.title: Vision care and dental providers
atoms.q: What eye care and dental providers can I choose?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare Vision network includes two types of eye care providers, optometrists and ophthalmologists, and UnitedHealthcare encourages visiting the eye doctor even if you do not wear glasses or contacts. Routine dental care is important to overall health, and a plan may include coverage for cleanings, fluoride, fillings, crowns, root canals, extractions and dentures.
qs: What is the difference between an optometrist and ophthalmologist?
Does my plan cover dental cleanings?

atoms.title: Questions to ask when choosing a doctor
atoms.q: How do I choose a doctor?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare suggests researching before choosing a doctor. Questions include whether friends, family, specialists or other health professionals recommend them, why people like this doctor, whether gender or age matters, whether you prefer a clinic close to home or work, how far you are willing to drive, and how their consumer reviews look. Reviews are just opinions, so one or two may not paint the whole picture.
qs: How do I pick a good primary care doctor?
Should I trust online doctor reviews?

atoms.title: Consider virtual visits
atoms.q: Can I see a provider virtually instead of in person?
atoms.text: Virtual visits, also known as telehealth, let you connect with a health care provider using your computer, tablet or smartphone and may be covered by your health plan just like an office visit. Depending on your benefits, you may be able to schedule a virtual visit with a local provider and book virtual visits for primary care, therapy, specialty care or urgent care when your provider is not available.
qs: Can I use telehealth for primary care?
Are virtual visits covered like office visits?

atoms.title: When do I need to submit a claim?
atoms.q: When do I need to submit a claim myself?
atoms.text: In most cases, when a member goes to a network provider, they do not need to submit a claim. There are a few occasions where submitting a claim may be required for the member or provider to receive reimbursement. Examples are dependent care reimbursement through an FSA, upfront billing by a provider, and out-of-network care.
qs: Do I have to file a claim with UnitedHealthcare?
When do I submit my own medical claim?

atoms.title: Dependent care FSA claims
atoms.q: Do dependent care FSA reimbursements need a claim?
atoms.text: If a member has an FSA account that covers reimbursement for childcare or elder care, a claim must be submitted for that reimbursement.
qs: How do I get reimbursed from my dependent care FSA?
Does childcare reimbursement require a claim?

atoms.title: Upfront billing and out-of-network claims
atoms.q: When might I have to file a claim for out-of-network or upfront-billed care?
atoms.text: A member may need to submit their own medical claim if a provider collects payment up front rather than billing the insurance company. For out-of-network care, such as when on the road or in an emergency, out-of-network providers can submit a claim on the member's behalf. If the provider is unwilling to do so, the member may have to submit the claim on their own.
qs: What if my provider won't file the claim?
Do I file claims for out-of-network doctors?

atoms.title: Timely filing limit
atoms.q: What is a timely filing limit?
atoms.text: Timely filing is the time limit a member or provider has to file a claim for health services received or provided. If the claim is not submitted in that time frame, insurance can deny the claim, which means the provider could potentially not receive payment or a member could be denied reimbursement.
qs: What is timely filing?
What happens if I file a claim too late?

atoms.title: Submit a claim online or by mail
atoms.q: How do I submit a claim to UnitedHealthcare?
atoms.text: There are two ways to submit claims: online or by mail. 1) Sign in to the member account, go to the Claims & Accounts tab, then select the Submit a claim tab. 2) Digitally submit a form, or download, print and complete a medical claim form. 3) Mail it with claim details and receipts to the mailing address on the member ID card.
qs: Where do I submit a claim online?
What address do I mail a claim form to?

atoms.title: Information needed on a superbill
atoms.q: What information do I need to include to submit a claim?
atoms.text: To process a claim, the superbill must include the patient name; the provider Taxpayer Identification Number (a copy of the W9 may be needed if the provider is out-of-network); diagnosis codes; procedure codes (CPT, HCPC with any applicable modifiers); units for each procedure code; the billed amount for each procedure code; and the place of service code.
qs: What is needed on a superbill for a claim?
Do I need a W9 for out-of-network claims?

atoms.title: Tips for an efficient claim
atoms.q: What tips make submitting a claim easier?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare suggests completing all applicable fields and asking the provider for the Provider Information. Keep a copy of the form, claim details and receipts, send the claim as soon as possible and close to the date of service, complete a separate form for each claim, and include the explanation of benefits (EOB) from other insurance or Medicare if it is primary.
qs: What should I do if I have other insurance before filing a claim?
How can I avoid claim mistakes?

atoms.title: What happens after a claim is processed
atoms.q: What happens after UnitedHealthcare processes my claim?
atoms.text: After a claim is processed, the member receives an explanation of benefits (EOB). It explains the charges applied to the deductible, which is the amount the member pays for covered services before the plan begins to pay, plus any charges the member may owe the provider. Members should keep their EOB on file and can review it anytime in their member account.
qs: What is an EOB?
Where do I see my explanation of benefits?

atoms.title: Mental and behavioral health coverage depends on plan
atoms.q: What mental and behavioral health programs may be covered?
atoms.text: Coverage depends on the specific health plan. Mental health services, like therapy or counseling, can help on their own or as part of a larger care plan. Behavioral health programs, such as coaching, can also be used on their own or with other care. Members can sign in to their member account or the UHC app to view their mental health benefits.
qs: What mental health benefits does my plan have?
What is the difference between mental health and behavioral health programs?

atoms.title: Calm Health app features
atoms.q: What does the Calm Health app include?
atoms.text: The Calm Health app offers mindfulness programs designed by psychologists to support mental well-being. Features may include guided meditation, relaxation and sleep support tools, programs to help manage stress and build resilience, and progress tracking and personalized recommendations. It may be covered at no additional cost by the health plan.
qs: Is Calm Health free with my plan?
What features does Calm Health have?

atoms.title: Substance Use Helpline
atoms.q: How do I reach the UnitedHealthcare Substance Use Helpline?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare members and their families can call the 24-hour Substance Use Helpline at 1-855-780-5955 (TTY 711) to speak with a recovery advocate. The support is private and anonymous, at no extra cost through their health plan.
qs: What is the substance use helpline phone number?
Can my family call the Substance Use Helpline?

atoms.title: Virtual Behavioral Coaching
atoms.q: What is Virtual Behavioral Coaching?
atoms.text: Virtual Behavioral Coaching (VBC) helps people learn ways to handle stress, feeling overwhelmed or exhaustion and gives tools to improve well-being. Participants may get simple tips to manage stress, build resilience and handle challenges, plus private weekly one-on-one sessions with a dedicated coach. It may be covered at no additional cost for members with health plans through work.
qs: What is VBC?
Can I get a coach for stress through my employer plan?

atoms.title: Child and family behavioral coaching
atoms.q: What is Child and Family Behavioral Health Coaching?
atoms.text: Child and Family Behavioral Health Coaching from Bend Health offers counseling for families with kids ages 1-17 and young adults ages 18-25. It may include monthly online coaching sessions, unlimited messaging support between sessions and referrals to therapists or psychiatrists if more support is needed. It may help with issues such as anxiety, ADHD, depression, bullying and sleep problems.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare offer behavioral coaching for kids?
What does Bend Health coaching include?

atoms.title: Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
atoms.q: What does the Employee Assistance Program offer?
atoms.text: Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) provide confidential support for personal or work-related concerns. With an EAP, members may get 24/7 access to support, referrals to licensed professionals and short-term counseling at no additional cost. EAP is among programs that may be available to members with health plans through work.
qs: What is an EAP?
Does my employer plan include short-term counseling?

atoms.title: Family Support Program
atoms.q: What is the Family Support Program?
atoms.text: The Family Support Program helps families navigate complex mental health needs and care transitions. Support may include help creating care plans, guidance during hospital-to-home transitions, and resources for conditions such as autism spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder and depression. It supports caregivers of children ages 0-17 with mental health needs and families needing high-level care.
qs: Is there help for parents of a child with mental health needs?
What support is there after a child leaves the hospital?

atoms.title: Finding a mental health provider and virtual visits
atoms.q: How do I find a mental health provider or a virtual visit?
atoms.text: Members can find a network mental health provider, search for LGBTQ+ friendly doctors, and ask local providers whether they offer virtual mental health visits, also called teletherapy, by phone or video. Coverage depends on the plan, so members can sign in to their member account or the UHC app to see available benefits.
qs: How do I find a therapist on my UnitedHealthcare plan?
Can I do therapy by video?

atoms.title: Mind Your Health for people without insurance
atoms.q: Is there mental health support without an insurance plan?
atoms.text: Mind Your Health, provided by Teladoc Health, gives access to unlimited online therapy without insurance for one monthly fee. UnitedHealthcare describes virtual therapy as a flexible and convenient way to get mental health care.
qs: Can I get therapy without health insurance?
What is Mind Your Health?

atoms.title: 24/7 crisis and emergency hotlines
atoms.q: What crisis hotlines are available 24/7?
atoms.text: Help is available 24/7 in English and Spanish. For emotional distress or suicidal thoughts, call or text 988. For immediate, life-threatening needs, call 911. The Substance Use Helpline is 1-855-780-5955 (TTY 711). The National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233) or text START to 88788.
qs: What number do I call for a mental health crisis?
Is there a hotline for domestic violence?

atoms.title: Prescription Drug List (PDL)
atoms.q: What is a Prescription Drug List?
atoms.text: A prescription drug benefit includes a list of medications covered by the plan, called a Prescription Drug List (PDL). It may also be called a formulary or drug list. When a doctor prescribes a medication, the member should check the PDL to see if it is covered.
qs: What is a formulary?
How do I know if my medication is covered?

atoms.title: Prescription drug tiers
atoms.q: What are prescription drug tiers?
atoms.text: Drug tiers group medications by value and cost. Tier 1 medications provide the highest overall value, are mostly generic and cost $. Tier 2 medications provide good overall value, are mainly preferred brand-name drugs and cost $$. Tier 3 medications provide the lowest overall value and cost $$$, and many have lower-cost options in Tiers 1 or 2, so members should ask their doctor.
qs: What does Tier 1 mean for prescriptions?
Why does my brand-name drug cost more?

atoms.title: Ask about lower-cost medication options
atoms.q: How can I lower prescription costs?
atoms.text: If a prescribed medication is in a higher cost tier, a member can ask their doctor whether a lower-cost option will work. A similar drug or generic version can often work just as well. UnitedHealthcare also notes pharmacy programs that may be available to help members save on costs.
qs: How do I save money on my prescriptions?
Can I ask for a generic drug?

atoms.title: Prior authorization for some medications
atoms.q: Do some medications need prior authorization?
atoms.text: Some medications need prior authorization, which means the doctor must explain why the member needs the drug and then the plan decides how or if it will cover it. To start the prior authorization process, the member can call the number on their member ID card.
qs: How do I start prior authorization for a prescription?
Why does my medication need prior authorization?

atoms.title: PDLs can change
atoms.q: How often does a Prescription Drug List change?
atoms.text: A Prescription Drug List may change. Members with prescriptions they take regularly should review their PDL regularly and watch for notifications about PDL updates and possible cost changes.
qs: Can my drug list change?
How will I know if my medication coverage changes?

atoms.title: What Optum Rx is
atoms.q: What is Optum Rx?
atoms.text: Optum Rx is the UnitedHealthcare pharmacy service provider that members may see named on their prescription benefits. It offers coverage through a large network of retail chain pharmacies and independent pharmacies, and through its mail order pharmacy, Optum Home Delivery.
qs: Who is Optum Rx?
Why does Optum Rx appear on my prescription card?

atoms.title: Find a network pharmacy
atoms.q: How do I find a network pharmacy?
atoms.text: Choosing a network pharmacy may help a member save on medication costs. Members can sign in to their member account to view the list of pharmacies in their plan's network. UnitedHealthcare also links to a search of the Optum Rx pharmacy network and says to confirm a plan's specific coverage details before filling a prescription.
qs: How do I find an in-network pharmacy?
Does using a network pharmacy save money?

atoms.title: Home delivery of prescriptions
atoms.q: How do I set up home delivery for prescriptions?
atoms.text: With some plans, members can fill prescriptions at a participating network pharmacy or with home delivery. Plans that include home delivery help members avoid regular trips to the pharmacy and may save money. Members can enroll through their online account or by calling the number on their member ID card.
qs: Can I get my prescriptions delivered?
How do I enroll in home delivery?

atoms.title: Optum Specialty Pharmacy delivery
atoms.q: How does Optum Specialty Pharmacy deliver medications?
atoms.text: Optum Specialty Pharmacy offers convenient delivery of medications directly to members using experienced carriers. If medications require special handling or refrigeration, they are packed and shipped accordingly. There is no cost for standard shipping or handling.
qs: Is shipping free with Optum Specialty Pharmacy?
How are refrigerated medications shipped?

atoms.title: Pharmacy information for specific plans
atoms.q: Where do I find pharmacy information for Medicare, ACA or Oxford plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare provides separate pharmacy information pages for specific plans: Medicare prescription drug coverage, ACA Marketplace plans and Oxford plans (including the Oxford pharmacy network). Members can also shop over-the-counter products and everyday essentials through Optum Now.
qs: Where is pharmacy information for Oxford plans?
Where can I buy over-the-counter items with Optum?

atoms.title: What a virtual visit is
atoms.q: What is a virtual visit?
atoms.text: A virtual visit, also known as telehealth, uses digital technologies like a smartphone, tablet or computer to talk with a health care provider from home or work. During a virtual visit you can get treatment options and even prescriptions for medications, if needed. UnitedHealthcare offers members options for virtual visits with local providers or with its preferred national providers.
qs: What is a virtual visit?
Is telehealth the same as a virtual visit?

atoms.title: Are virtual visits covered?
atoms.q: Are virtual visits covered by my health insurance?
atoms.text: Virtual visits may be covered by your health insurance in a similar way to an office visit with your doctor. Depending on your benefits, you may be able to schedule a virtual visit with a local provider or have a virtual visit for primary care, therapy, specialty care or 24/7 care with a national provider for urgent care or when your provider is not available. Sign in or call the number on your member ID card to check.
qs: Does my insurance cover telehealth?
How do I check virtual visit benefits?

atoms.title: Virtual visit options by insurance type
atoms.q: How do virtual visit options differ by type of insurance?
atoms.text: Members with health insurance through work should talk to a local provider, and many UnitedHealthcare employer plans include 24/7 Virtual Visits, virtual primary care, virtual therapy and virtual specialty care with preferred national providers. Individual and Family ACA Marketplace coverage depends on plan benefits. Medicare Advantage members should ask local providers and sign in to learn about coverage. Medicaid virtual visit coverage may vary by state.
qs: Does Medicare Advantage cover virtual visits?
Does Medicaid cover telehealth?

atoms.title: Types of services available virtually
atoms.q: What kinds of care can be delivered virtually?
atoms.text: Virtual care may include in-network virtual visits for medical, mental health, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, chiropractic, home health, vision, hearing and dental services. Availability depends on the health plan.
qs: Can I do physical therapy virtually?
Is therapy available through telehealth?

atoms.title: Virtual visits for mental health
atoms.q: Can I have a mental health visit virtually?
atoms.text: If you need care for mental health issues, local health care providers may be able to provide virtual visits. Coverage may depend on your health plan benefits, so sign in to your account or call the number on your member ID card to learn what benefits may be available.
qs: Does my plan cover virtual therapy?
How do I get therapy online?

atoms.title: Calm app and Talkspace emotional support
atoms.q: What emotional support apps may be included with my plan?
atoms.text: Some emotional support programs may be included with certain health plans. The Calm Health app offers programs and tools to support mental health and well-being at your own pace, including mindfulness content created by psychologists. Talkspace online therapy lets you communicate with a therapist from your phone or desktop with no office visit required, and eligible members can get started at talkspace.com/connect.
qs: What is Talkspace?
Is Calm Health included in my plan?

atoms.title: Virtual visit or in-person visit?
atoms.q: When should I choose a virtual visit versus seeing a doctor in person?
atoms.text: It is important to know the difference between when to choose a virtual visit and when to see a doctor in person. Virtual visits can be a convenient way to get care or manage prescriptions, but for more serious issues it may be necessary to go to a clinic or hospital.
qs: Should I do telehealth or go in person?
What conditions need an in-person visit?

atoms.title: Starting a virtual visit through the UHC app
atoms.q: How do I start a virtual visit?
atoms.text: Members can sign in to their member account or use the UnitedHealthcare app to see their virtual visits benefits and find care. For benefits coverage information, UnitedHealthcare directs members to sign in to their account, since coverage differs by plan.
qs: How do I start a telehealth visit with UnitedHealthcare?
Where do I see my virtual visit benefits?

atoms.title: Virtual visits included in employer plans
atoms.q: Do UnitedHealthcare employer plans cover virtual visits?
atoms.text: If a member has a UnitedHealthcare health insurance plan through work, their benefits include coverage for virtual visits, also known as telehealth. It is a way to talk to a health provider and get care, including prescriptions, from wherever they are by mobile device, tablet or computer. UnitedHealthcare says members pay less than a typical office visit and save time.
qs: Are virtual visits included in my employer health plan?
Do virtual visits cost less than an office visit?

atoms.title: 24/7 Virtual Visits for same-day care
atoms.q: What are 24/7 Virtual Visits and what do they cost?
atoms.text: 24/7 Virtual Visits are a way to schedule same-day, urgent care visits so members can talk with a provider 24/7 for common urgent care needs or when their primary care provider is not available. With a UnitedHealthcare plan, the cost for a 24/7 Virtual Visit is usually $54 or less.
qs: How much does a 24/7 Virtual Visit cost?
Can I see a doctor the same day by video?

atoms.title: Virtual primary care
atoms.q: What is virtual primary care?
atoms.text: Virtual primary care offers regular health visits and checkups with a primary care provider without the office visit. Members can choose to see a network PCP regularly so the same provider cares for them over time. It supports preventive care, common and chronic conditions such as diabetes and heart disease, and follow-up visits, and is available for members over 18.
qs: Can I have a regular PCP by video?
Is virtual primary care available for children?

atoms.title: Virtual therapy
atoms.q: What is virtual therapy?
atoms.text: Virtual therapy provides confidential behavioral health care through talking to a psychiatrist or therapist during a virtual visit from home. Members should check their benefits for the cost. The page lists issues it can help with, including anxiety, depression, burnout, grief, insomnia, panic attacks, PTSD, stress, substance use and trauma.
qs: What conditions can virtual therapy help with?
Can I talk to a psychiatrist by video?

atoms.title: Virtual specialty care
atoms.q: What is virtual specialty care?
atoms.text: Virtual specialty care lets members more quickly access specialty care personalized for their care needs, such as migraine or back, joint and muscle care. Members should check their benefits to see whether it is available to them.
qs: Can I see a specialist virtually?
Is there virtual care for migraines?

atoms.title: Conditions 24/7 Virtual Visits can treat
atoms.q: What conditions are 24/7 Virtual Visits good for?
atoms.text: 24/7 Virtual Visits are listed as good for common issues including abdominal pain, urinary tract infection, bronchitis, coughing, diarrhea, fever, migraine or headache, pinkeye, rash, seasonal flu, sinus problems, sore throat, stomachache and yeast infection, among others. Medicare Advantage members should check their plan materials to confirm coverage.
qs: Can I get a virtual visit for pinkeye?
What can a 24/7 virtual urgent care visit treat?

atoms.title: How to prepare for a virtual visit
atoms.q: How do I get ready for a virtual visit?
atoms.text: 1) Gather information: the UnitedHealthcare member ID card, a list of questions about symptoms, procedures or prescriptions, current medications, vitamins and supplements, and the pharmacy name and address. 2) Check technology: test the internet signal, charge the device, set the camera on a steady surface and read the provider's instructions. 3) Test audio and video 10 to 15 minutes before the visit.
qs: What do I need for a telehealth appointment?
How do I troubleshoot a virtual visit?

atoms.title: Virtual visits are not for emergencies
atoms.q: Can I use a virtual visit for an emergency?
atoms.text: Virtual visits are not intended to address emergency or life-threatening medical conditions. If a person is experiencing a medical emergency, they should seek emergency medical assistance such as calling 911. Virtual visits are not an insurance product, health care provider or health plan, and benefits are generally available only through a Designated Virtual Network Provider.
qs: Should I use a virtual visit in an emergency?
Are virtual visits an insurance product?

atoms.title: The UnitedHealthcare app
atoms.q: What is the UnitedHealthcare app?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare app is a mobile app that connects members to their health plan details anytime, anywhere. It is designed to give members instant access to the answers and support they need, with 24/7, always-there access to their plan.
qs: What is the UHC app?
What does the UnitedHealthcare app do?

atoms.title: Find care and pricing in the app
atoms.q: Can I find providers and estimate costs in the UnitedHealthcare app?
atoms.text: In the UnitedHealthcare app, members can search for network providers near them, see ratings and reviews, and estimate out-of-pocket costs for different types of visits.
qs: How do I find a network doctor in the UHC app?
Can I estimate my out-of-pocket costs in the app?

atoms.title: Check benefits and coverage in the app

atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare app lets members find copay and coinsurance amounts, view plan spending and see how their plan covers different types of care and services.
qs: Where can I see my copay in the UnitedHealthcare app?
How do I see what my plan covers?

atoms.title: Refill prescriptions from the app

atoms.text: Members can request prescription refills right from the UnitedHealthcare app. They can also look up drug prices and search for pharmacies near them.
qs: How do I refill a prescription in the UHC app?
Can I look up drug prices in the app?

atoms.title: View claims in the app

atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare app lets members check the status of new and past claims. For each claim, members can see the amount billed, what the plan paid and how much they owe.

Where can I see how much I owe on a claim?

atoms.title: Plan ID cards and digital wallets

Where do I find my digital insurance card?

atoms.title: Are all app features available on every plan?

Does the UHC app work with my plan?

atoms.title: How to download or access the app

qs: How do I download the UnitedHealthcare app?
How do I register if I only have a computer?

atoms.title: Cost estimates are not guarantees
atoms.q: Are the cost estimates in the app guaranteed?
atoms.text: All UnitedHealthcare members can access a cost estimate online or on the mobile app. None of the cost estimates are intended to be a guarantee of costs or benefits, and actual costs may vary. Members are directed to the website or mobile application terms of use under Find Care & Costs.

Is the estimated cost the actual price I will pay?

Does the UHC app support family members?

atoms.title: Wellness and rewards depend on plan type

atoms.text: With UnitedHealthcare wellness and rewards programs, members can earn rewards for reaching activity and health goals. UnitedHealthcare also offers wellness programs, such as One Pass Select and Renew Active, to give support and motivation and help keep the mind and body active. atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage members have many ways to earn rewards and many ways to spend them. Members may be eligible to earn rewards for completing certain activities, like an annual physical or wellness visit.

atoms.title: Walgreens Smart Savings discount

atoms.text: Eligible Individual & Family ACA Marketplace members can save 20% with the Walgreens Smart savings card on thousands of eligible Walgreens branded over-the-counter health and wellness products, such as eye care, dental care, baby essentials and smoking cessation products. atoms.title: What Naviguard is
atoms.q: What is Naviguard?
atoms.text: Naviguard is a service created to help reduce the amount a member may owe for medical care from out-of-network providers. Using advanced analytics and industry expertise, advisors review a member's case and guide them through the bill resolution process. A negotiation team engages directly with health care providers when necessary to resolve balance billing disputes.
qs: What is Naviguard?
Can UnitedHealthcare negotiate my out-of-network bill?

atoms.title: Who can use Naviguard and what it costs
atoms.q: Who can use Naviguard and does it cost extra?
atoms.text: Naviguard is available to UnitedHealthcare members who have qualifying employer-sponsored health plans. There is no additional cost for the service. To find out if they have access, members can call the member phone number on their health plan ID card.
qs: Is Naviguard free?
How do I find out if I can use Naviguard?

atoms.title: When to use Naviguard
atoms.q: When should I contact Naviguard about a bill?
atoms.text: After out-of-network care, a member should look at the explanation of benefits (EOB) from UnitedHealthcare. If the amount owed is higher than the member's cost share, they may receive a balance medical bill from the provider. When the bill arrives, the member should call before deciding to pay so Naviguard can review it and, if needed, negotiate with the provider.
qs: Should I pay an out-of-network bill right away?
How do I know if I have a balance bill?

atoms.title: How Naviguard negotiates and how long it takes
atoms.q: How does Naviguard reduce a balance medical bill?
atoms.text: If Naviguard determines a member was billed too much, its negotiators may contact the provider to try to agree on a lower amount, including for excessive charges from specialists, X-ray services and lab analysis. Naviguard uses industry and provider knowledge combined with market data to determine the right rate, handles all negotiating and keeps the member updated. On average, a case initiated by a member takes 30 to 45 days.
qs: How long does Naviguard take?
What bills can Naviguard negotiate?

atoms.title: Naviguard results
atoms.q: How much does Naviguard reduce out-of-network bills?
atoms.text: Naviguard reports an average reduction of about $2,600 per case and an average reduction of 73% off out-of-network billed charges. The page also says its team of experts has worked more than 1.4 million cases to help reduce out-of-network costs.
qs: How much can Naviguard save me?
What is Naviguard's track record?

How do I check on my Naviguard case?

atoms.text: If a member has an out-of-network claim that is eligible for Naviguard services, it is noted on the claim. Members can see this by signing in to their member account or opening the UnitedHealthcare app.

Does the UHC app show Naviguard claims?

atoms.title: Five care options compared
atoms.q: What is the difference between urgent care, the ER, virtual care, a PCP and a retail clinic?
atoms.text: Urgent care is for issues that are not emergencies when your PCP is not available. The ER is for life-threatening and very serious conditions. Virtual care offers treatment from anywhere for minor medical and mental health care. A primary care provider (PCP) handles preventive and routine care. A retail or walk-in clinic provides quick treatment for minor illnesses or basic screenings.
qs: Should I go to urgent care or the ER?
What care options do I have?
What is a retail clinic?

atoms.title: Common conditions by care setting
atoms.q: What conditions are treated at urgent care versus the ER?
atoms.text: Urgent care commonly treats sprains, minor broken bones such as a finger, minor burns, minor infections, earache and strep throat. The ER handles heavy bleeding, chest pain, major burns, difficulty breathing, broken bones or spinal injuries, and progressive confusion or slurred speech. Retail clinics treat skin rash, routine vaccines, minor injuries, earache and sports physicals, and a PCP handles checkups and immunizations.
qs: Is a sprain an ER or urgent care visit?
Which conditions go to the ER?

atoms.title: When to go to urgent care
atoms.q: When should I go to urgent care?
atoms.text: Urgent care treats illnesses and injuries that need care soon but are not emergencies, and can help when your PCP is away or cannot see you soon. It does not replace seeing your PCP. Urgent care may use simple lab tests such as urine tests, pregnancy tests or rapid strep tests, and may use X-rays. It typically lacks advanced tests such as CT scans or ultrasounds and may send you to an ER for more serious care.
qs: What can urgent care treat?
Does urgent care have X-rays?
Does urgent care have a CT scan?

atoms.title: When to go to the emergency room
atoms.q: When should I go to the ER?
atoms.text: ERs are for serious medical problems and are open 24 hours a day, every day of the year, with special equipment and trained doctors, physician assistants and nurses. For serious or life-threatening situations, call 911 or go to the nearest ER. If you are not sure you need an ambulance, call 911 and they can help you decide.
qs: When should I call 911?
Is the ER open all the time?

atoms.title: When you may need an ambulance
atoms.q: When do I need an ambulance?
atoms.text: You may need an ambulance if someone has chest pain, trouble breathing, sudden confusion or signs of a stroke; is choking, has stopped breathing or needs CPR; or had a car crash, fall or other accident and moving them could make the injury worse. In an emergency where you are unsure, call 911.
qs: What are signs I need an ambulance?
Should I drive someone with chest pain to the ER?

atoms.title: When to use virtual care
atoms.q: When is a virtual visit a good choice?
atoms.text: Virtual visits are a good choice if you do not need to see a provider in person. You can connect with a provider using your computer, tablet or smartphone, anytime and anywhere. Virtual visits can be a convenient way to get treatment options and even prescriptions for medications, if needed. For more serious problems, you may need to go to a clinic or hospital.
qs: When should I use telehealth?
Can I get a prescription from a virtual visit?

atoms.title: When to see your primary care provider
atoms.q: When should I see my primary care provider?
atoms.text: Your PCP is your go-to for routine checkups, preventive care and minor illnesses, and their in-depth knowledge of your health history makes them the best place to start. If you are ever unsure where to go, you can call your PCP, check your health plan's website or call the number on your health plan ID card to speak with an advocate.
qs: Who can help me decide where to go for care?
When is a PCP the right choice?

atoms.title: When to go to a retail or walk-in clinic
atoms.q: When should I use a retail or walk-in clinic?
atoms.text: A retail or walk-in clinic is a good option for minor illnesses such as earaches or rashes. These clinics are typically staffed with nurse practitioners or physician assistants who can treat minor injuries, such as minor cuts or sprains, and give routine vaccines such as the flu shot. Student athletes can typically get a sports physical without an appointment. These clinics are typically faster and cheaper than urgent care or the ER.
qs: Can I get a flu shot at a walk-in clinic?
Where can I get a sports physical?

atoms.title: Hours of availability by care option
atoms.q: Which care options are open outside regular office hours?
atoms.text: Urgent care, the emergency room, virtual care and retail or walk-in clinics are typically open 24/7, while a primary care provider is open during regular office hours and closed outside them. If you get sick after regular office hours, urgent care may be faster than waiting in a hospital emergency room.
qs: What care is available at night?
Is urgent care open 24/7?

atoms.title: Virtual visit service limitations
atoms.q: Are virtual visits meant for emergencies?
atoms.text: 24/7 Virtual Visits are not intended to address emergency or life-threatening medical conditions and should not be used in those circumstances. Unless otherwise required, benefits are available only when services are delivered through a Designated Virtual Network Provider. Services may not be available at all times, in all locations or for all members, so check your benefit plan.
qs: Can I use a virtual visit in an emergency?
Are virtual visits covered everywhere?

atoms.title: ER costs about $2,500 more than urgent care
atoms.q: How much more does an ER visit cost than urgent care?
atoms.text: Based on 2025 median allowed amounts charged by UnitedHealthcare network providers, the median ER visit is $2,750 and the median urgent care visit is $195, an estimated $2,500 difference. The figures are not tied to a specific condition or treatment, and actual payments may vary depending on benefit coverage. UnitedHealthcare says choosing alternatives could save up to $2,500.
qs: How much does an ER visit cost?
How much does urgent care cost compared to the ER?

atoms.title: Cost and wait time by care option
atoms.q: What does each type of care cost and how long is the wait?
atoms.text: Approximate costs and waits: urgent care $195, 30 minutes or less on average; ER $2,750, up to 2 hours; virtual care $60 or less, usually no wait; primary care provider $180 for an in-person visit and $99 or less for virtual primary care, usually a short wait for scheduled appointments; retail or walk-in clinic $105, 30 minutes or less. Most are typically open 24/7, while PCPs keep weekday office hours.
qs: What is the cheapest place to get care?
How much does a virtual visit cost?
How long is the wait at urgent care vs the ER?

atoms.title: Common conditions by care option
atoms.q: Which conditions go to which care option?
atoms.text: Urgent care commonly treats muscle sprains or strains, back pain, skin infections and broken bones. The ER treats chest pain, shortness of breath, major burns, severe injuries and heavy bleeding. Virtual care addresses headache, fatigue, sore throat, congestion, fever and cold or flu symptoms. A PCP can handle cough, fever, pinkeye and urinary tract infection, and retail clinics handle skin rash, flu shots, minor injuries and earache.
qs: Can urgent care treat a skin infection?
What can a virtual visit treat?

atoms.title: ER vs urgent care costs can differ tenfold
atoms.q: Why is the ER so much more expensive than urgent care?
atoms.text: Because ERs are more expensive than urgent care, knowing when to choose the ER can make a big difference in cost. Many common conditions can be treated at urgent care, and costs for treating these conditions may be more than 10 times higher at ERs than at urgent care. Members can sign in to find network urgent care clinics.
qs: Is the ER 10 times more expensive than urgent care?
How do I find an in-network urgent care?

atoms.title: How virtual visits may lower costs
atoms.q: Can virtual visits help lower my health care costs?
atoms.text: Virtual visits may be covered by your health plan just like an office visit with a doctor. Your benefits may cover a virtual visit with a local provider for primary care. If you need care fast or your PCP is not available, you may be able to use 24-hour virtual urgent care with a national provider. Members can check benefits for virtual visit coverage in their member account or the UHC app.
qs: Are virtual visits cheaper?
Does insurance cover virtual urgent care?

atoms.title: What affects the cost of medical care
atoms.q: What factors affect the cost of medical care?
atoms.text: Four factors can affect cost: having health insurance, which helps cover important care and unexpected illness or accidents; the level of care, since a PCP visit for a nonurgent concern likely costs much less than an ER visit; staying in your health plan network, which lowers costs; and regular PCP visits for preventive checkups and screenings, which may help identify issues before they become serious.
qs: What makes a doctor visit cost more?
How can I lower my medical costs?

atoms.title: Cost of an ER visit without insurance
atoms.q: How much does an ER visit cost without insurance?
atoms.text: A visit that requires more extensive care, such as surgery, may cost more than $21,000. Without health insurance, your health care costs are not capped. A health plan's out-of-pocket limit helps protect you from high medical expenses.
qs: What does an ER visit cost without insurance?
What does an out-of-pocket limit do?

atoms.title: What a member ID card is
atoms.q: What is a health plan member ID card?
atoms.text: When a person signs up for health insurance, they receive a member identification (ID) card for themselves and their covered family members. The member ID card, also called a health plan ID card, is proof that the person has health insurance.
qs: What is a member ID card?
Is my health plan ID card proof of insurance?

atoms.title: When to bring your member ID card
atoms.q: When do I need my member ID card?
atoms.text: Members should keep their member ID card handy when they go to the doctor, go to the hospital, have lab work done or get a prescription filled if their plan has drug coverage. Health care providers use the card's information to confirm they are part of the plan's network and to bill the health plan for care.
qs: Do I need my insurance card at the pharmacy?
Why do providers ask for my ID card?

atoms.title: What a digital member ID card is
atoms.q: What is a digital member ID card?
atoms.text: A member may get a digital ID card as well as a physical card. Members can download the UnitedHealthcare app on a mobile device to view their digital member ID card anytime, and can also view it in their member account.
qs: What is a digital insurance card?
Can I use a digital card instead of a physical card?

atoms.title: Using a digital ID card with providers
atoms.q: How do I use my digital ID card?
atoms.text: Members can show a digital ID card at a doctor's office, clinic, pharmacy or wherever benefit information needs to be presented. They can also print, download or email their cards to a provider. Digital ID cards are available for most medical, dental, vision or supplemental benefit plans, and members with more than one plan may see more than one card.
qs: Can I email my insurance card to my doctor?
Do I get separate digital cards for medical and dental?

atoms.title: View your digital ID card in the app
atoms.q: How do I view my digital ID card in the UnitedHealthcare app?
atoms.text: 1) Sign in to the UHC app. 2) Select Member Cards. To store the card in a smartphone's digital wallet, select Member Cards in the app and then Add to Wallet, which gives a secure way to store and access plan details.
qs: How do I add my UnitedHealthcare card to my phone wallet?
Where is Member Cards in the UHC app?

atoms.title: Vision-only members and digital cards
atoms.q: Where do vision-only members find their ID card?
atoms.text: If a member has only vision coverage that is not paired with a UnitedHealthcare medical plan, they access their digital ID card on myuhcvision.com. The page also notes that vision cards are digital only.
qs: Where do I find my UnitedHealthcare vision ID card?
Do vision plans send physical cards?

atoms.title: Information shown on the front of an ID card
atoms.q: What information appears on a member ID card?
atoms.text: A member ID card may vary by plan and coverage but can include member and dependent names, member ID number, group number, primary care provider (PCP) if the plan requires one, copay, deductible and out-of-pocket maximum, network, referrals required, pharmacy benefits and Medicare limiting charges. Most cards show the member ID and group number on the front.
qs: Where is my group number on my insurance card?
What does a UnitedHealthcare ID card show?

atoms.title: Back of the member ID card
atoms.q: What is on the back of a member ID card?
atoms.text: The back of a member ID card may list the member website and phone numbers to connect with customer service, speak with a nurse and discuss behavioral health. It may also include contact information for providers and pharmacists to submit insurance claims.
qs: What phone number is on my UnitedHealthcare card?
Where do providers send claims?

atoms.title: Why no physical card arrived
atoms.q: Why did I not receive a physical member ID card?
atoms.text: If a member chooses a paperless delivery preference, a digital ID card replaces the physical ID card. The member can access the digital health plan ID card whenever needed in the UHC app and on the member site, show it at the doctor's office or clinic, and add it to a smartphone's digital wallet. Vision cards are digital only.
qs: Why didn't I get an insurance card in the mail?
Does paperless mean no physical ID card?

atoms.title: Replacing a lost member ID card
atoms.q: How do I request a replacement member ID card?
atoms.text: If a member loses a physical ID card, they can print, download or view their digital ID card from their member account or the UHC app. They can request a physical card in the app or member account, and it may take 2 weeks for the new card to arrive in the mail.
qs: How long does a replacement UnitedHealthcare ID card take?
What if I lose my insurance card?

atoms.title: Replacing a Medicare card
atoms.q: How do I get a replacement Medicare card?
atoms.text: For a replacement ID card for a UnitedHealthcare Medicare plan, members can request a new physical card in the UHC app or on their member site, or use their digital card. A new government-issued Medicare card must be ordered through medicare.gov.
qs: How do I replace my Medicare Advantage ID card?
Where do I get a new government Medicare card?

atoms.title: UCard for Medicare Advantage members
atoms.q: Is there a different card for Medicare Advantage members?
atoms.text: The member ID card page points Medicare Advantage members to information about the UnitedHealthcare UCard. Members can learn more about UCard on the Medicare Advantage member resources page for UCard.
qs: What is UCard?
Where do I learn about the UCard for Medicare Advantage?

atoms.title: UHC Health Matters news and articles
atoms.q: What is UHC Health Matters?
atoms.text: UHC Health Matters is UnitedHealthcare's news and articles hub. It offers the latest news and articles on topics that support a person's health journey, from healthy living to understanding Medicare benefits to health insurance tips and more.
qs: What is UHC Health Matters?
Where does UnitedHealthcare publish health and insurance articles?

atoms.title: News and article categories
atoms.q: What categories of articles does UnitedHealthcare publish?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealthcare news and articles hub is organized into five categories: Benefits & coverage, Community, Healthy living, Medicare and Newsroom.
qs: What topics does UHC Health Matters cover?
Where do I find UnitedHealthcare newsroom articles?

atoms.title: Special Needs Initiative growth since 2017
atoms.q: How big has UnitedHealthcare's Special Needs Initiative become?
atoms.text: In a featured employee video, a UnitedHealthcare employee says the Special Needs Initiative has grown immensely since it started in 2017. It began with one family advisor connecting with 10 families. Now each year it brings in more than 30,000 new families and connects them to one of over 400 family advisors working on a team.
qs: How many families does UnitedHealthcare's Special Needs Initiative serve?
How many family advisors does the Special Needs Initiative have?

atoms.title: How a family advisor supported one family
atoms.q: What does a Special Needs Initiative family advisor do?
atoms.text: In the featured video, a UnitedHealthcare employee whose daughter has special needs says his Special Needs Initiative family advisor connected all the dots for his family. The advisor helped them start a new journey of dealing with the aftermath of his daughter's illness and the newness of being a dad with a child with special needs.
qs: How can a family advisor help a family with a child with special needs?
What support does the Special Needs Initiative provide?

atoms.title: UnitedHealthcare employee stories
atoms.q: Where can I read stories from UnitedHealthcare employees?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare features employee stories on its news and articles hub. The stories introduce employees whose work is helping people live healthier lives and are collected on a page titled Meet the people behind UnitedHealthcare.
qs: Does UnitedHealthcare share employee stories?
Who works at UnitedHealthcare and what do they do?

atoms.title: Four UnitedHealthcare ACA plan types
atoms.q: What types of ACA Marketplace plans does this article describe?
atoms.text: Everyone has different health care needs, so UnitedHealthcare Individual & Family ACA Marketplace plans come in several plan types to fit your lifestyle and budget.
